It reinforces the connection between divine revelation and the duty of the messenger to communicate this truth effectively.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وإنك لمن المرسلين

translation: Those messengers, We have preferred some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in rank. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs, and We supported him with the Pure Spirit. And if Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after they had received clear proofs. But they differed; so some of them believed and some disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought one another, but Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse signifies the distinction and status of the messengers in Islam, highlighting that some are favored over others based on divine wisdom. The mention of Jesus having been given clear signs and supported by the 'Spirit' emphasizes the special role of Jesus in Islamic theology. Furthermore, it reflects the theme of human choice and free will in the face of clear guidance; despite the evidences presented, people chose to differ. This underscores the notion that belief and disbelief are a result of individual decisions, and reinforces the idea that God's ultimate authority governs all outcomes, including the conflicts that arise among people after receiving divine guidance.
orig: تلك الرسل فضلنا بعضهم على بعض منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس ولو شاء الله ما اقتتل الذين من بعدهم من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات ولكن اختلفوا فمنهم من آمن ومنهم من كفر ولو شاء الله ما اقتتلوا ولكن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, spend from that which We have provided you before a Day comes in which there will be no exchange [of wealth] and no friendship and no intercession. And the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency and importance of charitable giving and spending in the way of Allah. It warns believers to act before the Day of Judgment, when material exchanges and relationships will hold no value. It points to the inevitability of that day, where the consequences of one's actions will become evident, and relations that might have mattered in this life will disintegrate. The mention of disbelievers as wrongdoers serves as a stark reminder of the importance of faith and the moral obligation to support others in this world while there's still time.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا مما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة والكافرون هم الظالمون

translation: Allah! There is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and supremacy of Allah as the only deity worthy of worship. It highlights His eternal nature as 'the Ever-Living' and 'the Sustainer of existence,' indicating that He is not subject to human limitations such as fatigue or sleep. The verse also illustrates Allah's comprehensive knowledge, encompassing all that has happened and will happen, simultaneously asserting that human beings can only know what Allah chooses to reveal. The mention of 'His Kursi' extending over the heavens and the earth illustrates His vast authority and dominion over all creation, reinforcing His magnificence and power. Ultimately, this verse serves to affirm the fundamental Islamic belief in strict monotheism (Tawhid) and Allah's unmatched greatness and control over the universe.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء وسع كرسيه السماوات والأرض ولا يئوده حفظهما وهو العلي العظيم

translation: There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong. So whoever renounces false gods and believes in Allah has certainly grasped the firmest handhold, which will never break. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of free will in matters of faith, stating that one cannot be forced into believing in a particular religion. It highlights the distinction between guidance and misguidance, indicating that the truth is apparent. The verse further outlines that true faith involves rejecting false beliefs (represented by 'taghut') and holding firmly to Allah, seen as a metaphorical stronghold that offers security and assurance. It implies that genuine belief is both a personal choice and a profound commitment, suggesting that God is aware of the intentions and actions of individuals.
orig: لا إكراه في الدين قد تبين الرشد من الغي فمن يكفر بالطاغوت ويؤمن بالله فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى لا انفصام لها والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out of darkness into light. And those who disbelieve, their allies are Taghut; they bring them out of light into darkness. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine guidance and support that Allah provides to the believers, illustrating a transformative journey from ignorance and oppression (darkness) to knowledge and liberation (light). In contrast, disbelievers are seen as reliant on Taghut—false deities or oppressors—who mislead them, resulting in their descent into darkness. The stark juxtaposition highlights the consequences of faith versus disbelief, framing the ultimate fate of individuals based on their choices in this life.
orig: الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور والذين كفروا أولياؤهم الطاغوت يخرجونهم من النور إلى الظلمات أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Did you not see the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, 'My Lord is He who gives life and causes death,' he said, 'I give life and cause death.' Abraham said, 'Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.' So the disbeliever was overwhelmed. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound discourse between Prophet Abraham and a ruler who, due to his power, believed himself to be equal to Allah. Abraham's assertion of God's absolute sovereignty over life and death serves to highlight the limits of human authority. The rhetorical challenge he presents—requesting the disbeliever to bring forth the sun from the west—illustrates the inadequacy of the ruler's claims and his utter failure in comparing himself to God's omnipotence. The verse emphasizes that true guidance is reserved for those who recognize and submit to the ultimate authority of Allah, underscoring the inevitable downfall of those who pride themselves in their status and oppress others.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه أن آتاه الله الملك إذ قال إبراهيم ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال أنا أحيي وأميت قال إبراهيم فإن الله يأتي بالشمس من المشرق فأت بها من المغرب فبهت الذي كفر والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Or like one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then brought him back to life. He said, 'How long have you remained (dead)?' He said, 'I have remained (dead) a day or part of a day.' He said, 'Rather, you have remained (dead) a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not changed over time. And look at your donkey. And We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We bring them together and then clothe them with flesh.' And when it became clear to him, he said, 'I know that Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power of Allah over life and death and serves as a reminder of the resurrection. The resurrection of the dead is presented through the story of a man who questions how Allah can revive a deceased town. One of the key themes is to illustrate that what seems impossible to human understanding is entirely within Allah's ability. The vivid imagery of the man witnessing his food and drink untouched despite a century passing reinforces the miracle of preservation amid decay and reflects the eternal nature of Allah's will. Ultimately, upon witnessing the divine acts, the man acknowledges Allah's omnipotence, reaffirming a foundational belief in the capabilities and the sovereignty of Allah over all creation.
orig: أو كالذي مر على قرية وهي خاوية على عروشها قال أنى يحيي هذه الله بعد موتها فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه قال كم لبثت قال لبثت يوما أو بعض يوم قال بل لبثت مائة عام فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك لم يتسنه وانظر إلى حمارك ولنجعلك آية للناس وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها ثم نكسوها لحما فلما تبين له قال أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said, 'Have you not believed?' Abraham said, 'Yes, but I only ask that my heart may be at ease.' He said, 'Then take four birds and confine them to yourself; then place on each hill a portion of them. Then call them; they will come flying to you. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep human desire for reassurance in matters of faith. Abraham's request to see how God brings the dead to life showcases his profound belief but also his yearning for a tangible confirmation that deepens his understanding. God's response emphasizes that faith should be cultivated through knowledge and certainty, hence the demonstration involving the birds. This act serves to illustrate the miraculous power of God and His dominion over creation, reinforcing the idea that belief and knowledge can coexist, leading to spiritual tranquility. Additionally, it underlines God's might and wisdom, reminding believers of the nature of divine authority and the importance of seeking knowledge to strengthen one's faith.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى قال أولم تؤمن قال بلى ولكن ليطمئن قلبي قال فخذ أربعة من الطير فصرهن إليك ثم اجعل على كل جبل منهن جزءا ثم ادعهن يأتينك سعيا واعلم أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed which sprouts seven ears; in every ear there are a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense reward for those who give charity in the path of Allah. It illustrates that a single act of kindness and generosity can yield abundant returns, symbolized by the seed sprouting numerous grains. The imagery conveys that while the act of giving may seem small, the divine reward can be vast and multiplied beyond human comprehension. Additionally, it highlights the boundless wisdom and knowledge of Allah, who knows the intentions and circumstances of each individual, and can reward them accordingly.
orig: مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة أنبتت سبع سنابل في كل سنبلة مائة حبة والله يضاعف لمن يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah and do not follow their expenditures with reminders of their generosity or with hurtful words, for them is their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of altruistic giving without seeking recognition or causing harm to the recipients. It highlights that true charity is performed selflessly, free from ego and the desire for recompense or praise. The promise of a reward from Allah reinforces the idea that such acts of kindness not only benefit the recipients but also secure a special status and protection for the givers in the eyes of God. The absence of fear and grief reflects a deep sense of peace and assurance for those who give sincerely.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله ثم لا يتبعون ما أنفقوا منا ولا أذى لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of intentions and the state of the heart when performing acts of goodness. It indicates that the manner in which we communicate with others and the way we approach forgiveness hold far greater value than material generosity if it is marred by subsequent harm or insensitivity. It highlights that Allah does not need our charity; therefore, the moral imperative is on creating positive, uplifting interactions with others. The concepts of kindness and compassion take precedence over mere acts of giving, reinforcing that true charity is not just a physical act but also includes the emotional and verbal tone we express towards others.
orig: قول معروف ومغفرة خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى والله غني حليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with wrongdoing or injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a stone upon which is dirt; then a downpour strikes it, so it leaves it bare. They are not able to keep anything of what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and the proper intention behind charitable acts. It warns believers that their good deeds can be rendered ineffective if they follow them with reminders of their generosity or by causing harm to those they help. The comparison made illustrates how without true faith and intention, acts of charity can become void, much like the dirt on a stone that is washed away by rain, leaving nothing behind. Ultimately, it serves as a reminder that one's faith and the spirit behind one's actions are crucial for the acceptance of deeds by Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فمثله كمثل صفوان عليه تراب فأصابه وابل فتركه صلدا لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and affirming themselves is like a garden on a high ground; it is struck by a downpour and it yields its fruit double, and if it is not struck by a downpour, then a drizzle suffices. And Allah is All-Seer of what you do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual and material rewards of charity and righteous spending in the way of Allah. The comparison to a garden on elevated land signifies the elevation of one’s status and the profound impact of their good deeds. The dual yield of fruits symbolizes the amplified rewards and benefits one receives from their generosity, implying that divine blessings can manifest in multiple forms, whether through abundant gains from significant sacrifices or through smaller acts of kindness. The mention of Allah's sight over our actions serves as a reminder of accountability, emphasizing that every act of giving and the intention behind it are fully recognized and rewarded by Allah, encouraging believers to maintain sincerity and commitment in their charitable acts.
orig: ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم كمثل جنة بربوة أصابها وابل فآتت أكلها ضعفين فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Would any of you wish to have a garden with date palms and vines, with rivers flowing underneath it, and for him therein of all fruits while he is afflicted with old age and his children are weak (unable to look after themselves)? Then it is struck with a fiery blast, so that it is burnt. Thus Allah makes clear the verses (of the Qur'an) to you that you may give thought.
interpretation: This verse presents a vivid metaphor regarding the futility of material wealth when faced with the inevitable trials of life, particularly old age and the vulnerability of one's children. It emphasizes that no matter how much one possesses in terms of worldly riches, these can be swiftly taken away or rendered worthless due to circumstances beyond one's control, such as an unexpected disaster. The imagery of a beautiful garden—symbolizing wealth and prosperity—being destroyed serves as a cautionary reminder to prioritize lasting values and spiritual wealth over transient earthly gains. Ultimately, the verse encourages reflection on the purpose of life and the importance of being mindful of spiritual responsibilities.
orig: أيود أحدكم أن تكون له جنة من نخيل وأعناب تجري من تحتها الأنهار له فيها من كل الثمرات وأصابه الكبر وله ذرية ضعفاء فأصابها إعصار فيه نار فاحترقت كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the defective from it, spending from that while you would not take it yourself except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving in charity from what is genuinely good and valuable. It highlights the ethical and moral responsibility of believers to spend from their best possessions, rather than from what is subpar or unworthy. The reference to not taking defective goods illustrates a fundamental principle of integrity and sincerity in acts of worship and righteousness, encouraging believers to engage in dealings that reflect their faith in Allah's generosity. Furthermore, the closing reminder that Allah is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy asserts that He does not require anything from His creation, reinforcing the idea that charitable acts improve the giver’s character and are done for their own spiritual benefit, rather than for divine approval.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه واعلموا أن الله غني حميد

translation: Satan promises you poverty and commands you to immoral acts; Allah promises you forgiveness from Himself and bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting messages between Satan and Allah. While Satan aims to instill fear of poverty and encourages sinful behavior, Allah assures His believers of forgiveness and generosity. It serves to remind the faithful that divine providence is greater than material concerns and that reliance on Allah leads to spiritual wealth and moral righteousness. The verse emphasizes the importance of choosing the path of faith and righteousness over the deceptive promises of despair and immorality.
orig: الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا والله واسع عليم

translation: He grants wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good. And none will remember except those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the value of wisdom as a divine gift. It indicates that wisdom is not universally bestowed but rather given selectively by God to those He chooses. Those who receive wisdom are among the fortunate, possessing a significant blessing that transcends material gains. The mention of 'those of understanding' highlights that true remembrance and recognition of God's gifts are reserved for those who possess intellect and discernment, suggesting a deeper appreciation for the nuances of life and the importance of spiritual insight.
orig: يؤتي الحكمة من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: And whatever you spend of anything or whatever you vow of a vow, indeed, Allah knows it. And for the wrongdoers, there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity in intentions behind charitable actions and vows. It reinforces the idea that Allah is fully aware of every act of giving and the motivations behind them. The mention of the wrongdoers lacking helpers suggests that those who commit injustices or act deceitfully will find no support or protection in the face of divine accountability. Overall, it serves as a reminder that all actions are observed by Allah, and individuals will be judged accordingly.
orig: وما أنفقتم من نفقة أو نذرتم من نذر فإن الله يعلمه وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: If you manifest your charities, it is well; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you. And it will remove from you some of your misdeeds. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of charity and the different approaches one can take in giving. It suggests that while public acts of charity are commendable, there is a greater virtue in giving discreetly, as it directly serves those in need without drawing attention to oneself. The verse further reinforces the idea that charitable actions can lead to the forgiveness of sins, highlighting Allah's awareness of each person's intentions and deeds. This serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize sincerity and humility in their acts of kindness.
orig: إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم ويكفر عنكم من سيئاتكم والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves. And you do not spend except seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between guidance, which is ultimately in the hands of Allah, and the responsibility of individuals to act righteously. It emphasizes that acts of charity and goodness should be intended for the sake of Allah, as the true reward comes from Him. Furthermore, it reassures believers that their charitable actions will not go unnoticed or unrewarded. The notion of fairness and justice is reinforced, indicating that everyone will receive their due, motivating believers to engage in philanthropy with pure intentions.
orig: ليس عليك هداهم ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وما تنفقوا من خير فلأنفسكم وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله وما تنفقوا من خير يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: It is for the poor who have been restricted in the cause of Allah and are unable to move about in the land. The ignorant person thinks them to be rich because of their restraint. You will recognize them by their mark. They do not beg indiscriminately from people. And whatever good you spend, indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dignity and self-restraint of the poor who strive in the path of Allah. It highlights the notion that true wealth is not always visible and that appearances can be deceiving; those who are in need may not outwardly express their situation due to their dignity and self-sufficiency. Additionally, it underscores the importance of compassion and charity towards those in need and reassures believers that their acts of generosity do not go unnoticed by Allah, who is fully aware of the intentions and efforts behind such actions.
orig: للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف تعرفهم بسيماهم لا يسألون الناس إلحافا وما تنفقوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the night and the day, secretly and openly, will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of charitable spending, emphasizing that true generosity is done consistently and sincerely, both in private and public. The phrasing 'by night and by day' suggests that such acts of kindness should be a constant practice, not limited to specific times. The mention of receiving a reward from God indicates that such generosity contributes to one’s spiritual standing, while the assurance of 'no fear nor grief' signifies the deep inner peace and security believers will experience in the sight of their Lord, as their acts of charity shield them from anxiety and future worries.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا وعلانية فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who consume interest cannot stand on the Day of Resurrection except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, 'Trade is just like interest.' But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. And whoever returns [to dealing in interest or usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of usury (riba) in Islam, comparing the state of those who engage in it to a person afflicted by madness. It indicates that they will face severe consequences in the Hereafter, emphasizing not only the immoral nature of their actions but also God's explicit command against such practices. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of adhering to divine guidance, with the promise of forgiveness for past actions upon sincere repentance, while also issuing a warning about the perpetual consequences for those who choose to persist in wrongdoing. It reinforces the principle that lawful trade is encouraged, but usurious practices are detrimental to individual and societal welfare.
orig: الذين يأكلون الربا لا يقومون إلا كما يقوم الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس ذلك بأنهم قالوا إنما البيع مثل الربا وأحل الله البيع وحرم الربا فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه فانتهى فله ما سلف وأمره إلى الله ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Allah abolishes usury and gives increase for charities. And Allah does not like every disbeliever, sinful person.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the contrasting outcomes of engaging in usury versus giving in charity. It highlights that while usury leads to destruction and loss, charity results in growth and blessings. Furthermore, it conveys Allah's disapproval of those who reject faith and commit wrongs, underlining the moral framework within which economic behaviors are judged in Islam.
orig: يمحق الله الربا ويربي الصدقات والله لا يحب كل كفار أثيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and established prayer and given zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the essential elements of faith and righteous action in Islam. It emphasizes that true belief is accompanied by good deeds, such as performing prayers and giving zakah (charitable giving). The promise of reward from Allah underscores the importance of these practices in achieving a favorable status in the Hereafter. Furthermore, the assurance of no fear or grief signifies a state of peace and security for the believers, indicating that their faith and actions safeguard them from anxieties associated with judgment and accountability.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of interest, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to uphold their faith in Allah by cultivating piety and righteousness. It emphasizes the importance of abandoning usurious practices, highlighting that genuine belief in Allah necessitates rejecting unlawful gains. The directive suggests that true faith is demonstrated through ethical financial conduct, and those who adhere to this principle strengthen their relationship with Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: But if you do not do [what you are commanded], then be informed of a declaration of war from Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, you may have your principal - you do no wrong, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse serves as a strong warning against engaging in usury (riba), highlighting its severe spiritual consequences. The phrase 'be informed of a declaration of war' signifies the gravity with which Allah views this sin, indicating that one who persists in usury is opposing divine authority. The latter part reassures those who may have engaged in usury but choose to repent: they will not suffer loss of their original capital, emphasizing justice and mercy in Islam. The overall message stresses the importance of repentance and the possibility of redemption, alongside a condemnation of exploitative financial practices.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم لا تظلمون ولا تظلمون

translation: And if someone is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease. And if you give and charity is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of compassion and leniency towards those who are facing financial difficulties. It highlights the moral responsibility to assist others by allowing them time to repay debts without pressure. Furthermore, the verse promotes the idea that giving to those in need is not only an act of kindness but also a means of earning spiritual rewards. It implies that genuine generosity and the act of charitable giving hold greater value in the sight of God, encouraging individuals to prioritize helping others over their material interests.
orig: وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وأن تصدقوا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It highlights the concept of accountability in the Hereafter, where every individual will face the consequences of their actions in this world. The mention of returning to Allah emphasizes the connection between human actions and divine judgment. The assurance that no soul will be wronged reassures believers of divine justice, implying that every person's deeds will be accurately assessed and rewarded or punished accordingly. This encourages personal responsibility and ethical behavior, as every individual is reminded that their life choices will have lasting effects beyond this earthly existence.
orig: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write between you in justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write and let the one who has the obligation dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not leave anything out of it. But if the debtor is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the women errs, then the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse to testify when they are called upon. And do not get tired of writing, whether it is small or large, for its specified term. That is more just in the sight of Allah and stronger as evidence and more likely to prevent doubt between you. Except when it is an immediate transaction which you conduct among yourselves. For there is no blame upon you if you do not write it. And take witnesses when you conclude a contract. And let no scribe or witness be harmed. And if you do so, it has certainly been wickedness in you. And fear Allah, and Allah will teach you. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of fairness and clarity in financial dealings, emphasizing the necessity of documentation for debts to prevent misunderstandings and disputes. It highlights that writing contracts is not just a legal formality but a moral obligation that reflects a person's commitment to justice and integrity. The verse also recognizes the challenges faced by those who may not be capable of dictating their obligations and instructs that fairness should prevail in such instances. Moreover, the inclusion of female witnesses acknowledges the essential roles women play in society and promotes their participation while providing a safeguard against error. Ultimately, this passage emphasizes that maintaining trust, transparency, and a conscientious approach in financial transactions is crucial, aligning with the greater goal of fostering a fair community underpinned by mutual respect and the consciousness of God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله ذلكم أقسط عند الله وأقوم للشهادة وأدنى ألا ترتابوا إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a pledge (is acceptable). And if one of you entrusts another, let the one who is entrusted discharge his trust, and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it - his heart is indeed sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trustworthiness and integrity in financial dealings, especially when formal contracts cannot be established due to circumstances like travel. It highlights the obligation to uphold trusts and to be honest in testimony, warning against the moral failing of concealing the truth. It serves as a reminder that God is fully aware of our actions and intentions, and thus ethical conduct, even in challenging situations, is paramount.
orig: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته وليتق الله ربه ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete sovereignty and knowledge of Allah over all that exists, both visible and hidden. It reminds believers that their innermost thoughts and feelings are known to Allah, and accountability for one’s intentions and deeds is inevitable. The mention of forgiveness and punishment underscores Allah's mercy as well as His justice; He has the authority to forgive or punish based on His wisdom and discretion. Therefore, followers are encouraged to remain conscious of their inner selves and align them with righteousness, as Allah's power extends over all matters.
orig: لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so do] the believers. All of them believe in Allah and His angels and His Books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [Grant us] Your forgiveness, our Lord. To You is the final destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essence of faith in Islam, highlighting how the Prophet Muhammad and the believers fully accept the revelations from Allah without hesitation or distinction among the messengers. It signifies the unity of belief that encompasses all prophets, advocating for obedience and humility in the pursuit of divine forgiveness. The verse also reflects the ultimate accountability towards Allah, indicating that life is a journey leading to Him, reinforcing the idea that believers should act with faith and sincerity, asking for God's mercy as they strive for righteousness.
orig: آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله وقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير

translation: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or made a mistake. Our Lord, lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and lay not upon us that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's justice and mercy, highlighting that He does not impose more on individuals than they can handle. It acknowledges human limitations and the inevitability of mistakes, calling for divine forgiveness and support. The supplication reflects a desire for relief from burdensome responsibilities and a plea for compassion, positioning Allah as the ultimate protector against adversity and the forces of disbelief. The community of believers is encouraged to seek strength and assistance from God in overcoming challenges while remaining aware of their own fallibility.
orig: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به واعف عنا واغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These letters are known as 'Muqattaʿat' or 'disjoined letters,' and they appear at the beginning of several chapters in the Qur'an. Their exact meaning is known only to Allah. They serve as a reminder of the inimitability of the Qur'an and invite reflection on the divine nature of its message. The letters can also symbolize a deeper spiritual truth, suggesting that understanding the Qur'an requires more than intellectual reasoning; it necessitates a heartfelt approach and divine guidance.
orig: الم

translation: Allah! There is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God (Tawhid) and His unique attributes. 'The Ever-Living' signifies that Allah is the source of all life, undying and eternal, not subject to death or decay. 'The Sustainer of existence' highlights His role in maintaining and nurturing all creations. This reflects a profound aspect of Islamic belief, underscoring that reliance on Allah is paramount, as He alone possesses the attributes necessary for guidance, sustenance, and support in all aspects of life.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم

translation: The Book has been sent down to you with the truth, confirming what is before it; and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and its role as a continuation and confirmation of previous revelations, namely the Torah and the Gospel. It suggests a sense of unity among the scriptures, indicating that they all share the same essential truth and purpose of guiding humanity. The mention of the Qur'an being sent down 'with the truth' highlights its authenticity and the certainty of its message in providing moral and spiritual guidance. This reinforces the idea that the teachings found within these texts are meant to complement each other, indicating a broader theological framework where all prophets and their scriptures serve a singular divine mission.
orig: نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه وأنزل التوراة والإنجيل

translation: This is a guidance for the people, and He has sent down the criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment. And Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Revenge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a guidance and a criterion for humanity, distinguishing between right and wrong. It warns those who reject its messages and signs of severe consequences, highlighting the strength and authority of Allah in administering justice and retribution. The verse reflects the serious implications of disbelief and the divine power that enforces moral order.
orig: من قبل هدى للناس وأنزل الفرقان إن الذين كفروا بآيات الله لهم عذاب شديد والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Indeed, Allah does not conceal anything in the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is in the vastness of the earth or the heavens. It serves as a reminder that Allah's awareness encompasses all actions, thoughts, and intentions of human beings, which can inspire a sense of accountability. This knowledge also instills comfort for believers, as they understand that their struggles and efforts are seen and valued by Allah, who is all-knowing and just.
orig: إن الله لا يخفى عليه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: He it is who forms you in the wombs as He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of God in the process of creation, particularly in the formation of human beings in the womb. It highlights that everything occurs according to His will, reflecting His control over life and existence. The declaration 'There is no deity except Him' underscores the concept of monotheism, asserting that God is the only true source of power and wisdom. The attributes 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise' suggest that not only is He capable of creating and shaping life, but He does so with perfect wisdom, indicating that every aspect of creation serves a purpose within His divine plan.
orig: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is Who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise (محكمات), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous (متشابهات). As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they will follow that which is ambiguous, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. And no one knows its interpretation except Allah and those firm in knowledge say, 'We believe in it; all is from our Lord.' And none will remember except those of reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between clear and ambiguous verses in the Qur'an. The clear verses form the core of its message, while the ambiguous ones can lead to misunderstanding or misinterpretation, particularly for those with insincere intentions. The reference to those 'firm in knowledge' underscores the importance of faith and humility in understanding divine revelation. It emphasizes that true comprehension comes from acknowledging the limits of human knowledge compared to God's ultimate wisdom. The call to reason encourages the faithful to engage deeply with the text, fostering a sincere and enlightened approach to their beliefs.
orig: هو الذي أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب وأخر متشابهات فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ فيتبعون ما تشابه منه ابتغاء الفتنة وابتغاء تأويله وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به كل من عند ربنا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: O our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This verse conveys a deep plea for divine guidance and stability in faith. It emphasizes the fragility of the human heart and the need for constant divine support to remain on the right path. The request for mercy underscores the belief that guidance is a blessing that requires continuous reinforcement from God. It reflects the understanding that human beings, despite receiving guidance, are vulnerable to misguidance and thus seek the nurturing presence of God's mercy to strengthen their conviction and resolve.
orig: ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا بعد إذ هديتنا وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: Our Lord, indeed You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, highlighting that it is an inevitable event where all of humanity will be assembled. It reinforces the concept of accountability, reminding believers of Allah's promise, which is unwavering and certain. The phrase reflects both hope and awe, as it serves as a reminder of divine justice and the ultimate fulfillment of God’s promises, encouraging individuals to live righteously in anticipation of this day.
orig: ربنا إنك جامع الناس ليوم لا ريب فيه إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all. And it is they who are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse conveys the notion that material possessions and familial ties hold no value in the face of divine judgment for those who reject faith. It emphasizes the futility of relying on worldly success or relationships as a means of salvation. The term 'fuel of the Fire' underscores the severity of their fate, indicating that their disbelief leads them to a dire consequence in the afterlife. This serves as a warning to reflect on true righteousness and the importance of faith over earthly gains.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك هم وقود النار

translation: (This is) the manner of the people of Pharaoh and those before them. They denied Our signs, so We seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning through historical examples. It illustrates the fate of those who oppose divine signs and reject the truth. The mention of the Pharaoh's people highlights the consequences of arrogance and denial, emphasizing that divine justice will eventually prevail. The severity of Allah’s punishment underscores the seriousness of turning away from guidance and truth, encouraging believers to adhere to faith and be mindful of their actions.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآياتنا فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم والله شديد العقاب

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place.'
interpretation: This verse is a strong warning to disbelievers, illustrating the inevitable consequences of their rejection of faith. It emphasizes that despite any temporary power or success they may perceive, they will ultimately face defeat and be gathered for judgment, leading to Hell—a place characterized as a dreadful abode. The verse serves to reinforce the seriousness of disbelief and the reality of divine retribution, urging listeners to reflect on their choices and consider the fate that awaits them.
orig: قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون وتحشرون إلى جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: There has already been for you a sign in the two armies that met. One was fighting in the cause of Allah, and the other was disbelieving. They saw them as twice their number with the sight of the eye. And Allah aids with His victory whom He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those of insight.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the lessons that can be learned from the encounter between two distinct groups—the believers fighting for a righteous cause and the disbelievers opposing them. It illustrates that, despite the apparent numerical disadvantage, faith and divine support can grant victory. The phrase 'they saw them as twice their number' highlights the power of perception influenced by faith, as believers often view their struggles through the lens of divine assistance. It serves as a reminder for those who reflect, urging them to recognize the importance of faith and reliance on God in the face of challenges, as well as the potential consequences of disbelief.
orig: قد كان لكم آية في فئتين التقتا فئة تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرة يرونهم مثليهم رأي العين والله يؤيد بنصره من يشاء إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire - of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, and cattle and tillage. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural human inclination towards worldly desires such as wealth, family, and possessions. It serves as a reminder that while these attractions are part of life and can be beautiful, they are ultimately fleeting and are not the ultimate goal. The mention of 'the best return' indicates that true fulfillment and lasting rewards come from Allah, encouraging believers to prioritize spiritual growth and righteousness over transient pleasures.
orig: زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا والله عنده حسن المآب

translation: Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear Allah are Gardens in which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and purified spouses; and the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Seeing of the servants.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the rewards that await the righteous who fear and obey God. It contrasts earthly desires with the eternal bliss promised in Paradise, highlighting the significance of piety and the divine rewards that follow. The mention of 'Gardens' and 'rivers' evokes imagery of abundant and everlasting comfort, while 'purified spouses' signifies purity and spiritual fulfillment in relationships. The 'pleasure of Allah' emphasizes the ultimate goal for believers, which is to attain God's approval and mercy. The closing reminder that 'Allah is Seeing of the servants' serves to reinforce the notion that God is aware of all actions and intentions, encouraging believers to strive for righteousness in anticipation of these rewards.
orig: قل أؤنبئكم بخير من ذلكم للذين اتقوا عند ربهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وأزواج مطهرة ورضوان من الله والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Those who say, 'Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and recognition of believers who acknowledge their faith and seek forgiveness for their shortcomings. It emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah with sincerity and imploring Him for mercy. The plea for protection from the punishment of the Fire signifies a deep understanding of the consequences of one's actions and the believer's desire for divine protection. It underlines the relationship between faith, repentance, and the hope for salvation.
orig: الذين يقولون ربنا إننا آمنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وقنا عذاب النار

translation: The patient, the truthful, the devout, those who spend, and those who seek forgiveness in the early hours (of dawn),
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of specific qualities that are favored in Islam. It emphasizes the importance of patience, truthfulness, devotion, charity, and seeking forgiveness during the quiet moments of dawn, suggesting a deep spiritual discipline. Each of these attributes reflects a strong moral character and dedication to faith, indicating that those who embody these qualities are worthy of God’s mercy and favor. The mention of 'early hours' suggests an ideal time for reflection and supplication, underscoring the value of sincerity in worship and the pursuit of a righteous life.
orig: الصابرين والصادقين والقانتين والمنفقين والمستغفرين بالأسحار

translation: Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, [that He is] maintaining creation in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah and reinforces the truth of monotheism. The testimony of Allah, the angels, and the knowledgeable ones underscores the significance of divine justice, indicating that God's existence and authority are acknowledged universally. It highlights that true knowledge aligns with the recognition of Allah's sovereignty and attributes, such as His might and wisdom, which further affirm His unique status as the sole deity worthy of worship.
orig: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Islam is the true religion decreed by Allah. It points out that the divisions among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) arose only after they received divine knowledge, and these divisions were fueled by jealousy and envy rather than genuine theological disputes. The verse concludes with a reminder of the accountability before Allah for disbelief in His signs, highlighting His swift and just nature in dealing with such matters.
orig: إن الدين عند الله الإسلام وما اختلف الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ومن يكفر بآيات الله فإن الله سريع الحساب

translation: So if they argue with you, say, 'I have submitted myself to Allah, and [so have] those who follow me.' And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, 'Have you submitted?' If they submit, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away - then upon you is only the [duty of] notification. And Allah is Seeing of the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fundamental submission to Allah as the essence of faith. It directs the Messenger to proclaim his total submission to God, alongside his followers, underscoring the communal aspect of belief. The invitation to the people of the Scripture and the unlettered to submit illustrates a call for unity in faith, regardless of previous divisions. The verse highlights that guidance comes through submission to God; if others accept this path, they find true wisdom and clarity. However, the duty of the Messenger is simply to convey the message, emphasizing that ultimate responsibility for belief lies with the individual, while God is fully aware of all human actions and intentions.
orig: فإن حاجوك فقل أسلمت وجهي لله ومن اتبعن وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم فإن أسلموا فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice from among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of disbelief and injustice against divine guidance and messengers. It highlights the gravity of killing prophets and those who advocate for justice, underscoring that such actions lead to dire consequences. The promise of 'a painful punishment' serves as a warning to those who transgress moral and ethical boundaries set by Allah, illustrating the serious repercussions of turning away from faith and righteousness.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير حق ويقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and in the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of one's actions and the state of those who reject truth and righteousness. It signifies that their efforts in life are in vain, leading to a complete lack of support or defense on Judgment Day. Ultimately, it serves as a warning about the futility of disobedience and the importance of aligning one's actions with divine guidance.
orig: أولئك الذين حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They call to the Book of Allah to settle their dispute, and then a party of them turns away, and they are refusing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to follow divine guidance yet reject it when it does not align with their desires. It points to the idea that although they acknowledge the authority of divine scripture in resolving conflicts, they often choose to ignore its mandates when faced with the consequences. This serves as a warning against the superficial adherence to religious principles that do not translate into action or genuine faith.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يدعون إلى كتاب الله ليحكم بينهم ثم يتولى فريق منهم وهم معرضون

translation: This is because they said, "Fire will not touch us except for a few days." And they were deceived in their religion by what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delusions of those who deny the consequences of their actions, believing that their time in the fire will be limited due to their misguided convictions. The statement reflects a sense of false security and a misunderstanding of divine justice. It emphasizes that such beliefs are rooted in fabrications and misinterpretations of faith, leading them away from the truth and ultimately towards their own destruction.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودات وغرهم في دينهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be compensated for what it earned; and they will not be wronged?
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that it is an undeniable reality where all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds. It reassures that everyone will receive fair compensation for their actions in life without any injustice, reinforcing the concept of divine justice. This serves as a reminder for individuals to reflect on their choices and actions, as they will ultimately face the consequences in the hereafter.
orig: فكيف إذا جمعناهم ليوم لا ريب فيه ووفيت كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, "O Allah, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and take the kingdom away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and humiliate whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all matters of rule and authority. It serves as a reminder that all power and dominion belong to Him alone, and He grants it to whomever He chooses, reinforcing the concept of divine will in the affairs of mankind. The verse also indicates that honor and humiliation, like kingdom and power, are within Allah's control, highlighting human dependence on His mercy and authority. It underscores that the ultimate goodness and capability lie with Allah, affirming His omnipotence and the transient nature of worldly power.
orig: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء وتعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء بيدك الخير إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: You bring the night into the day, and You bring the day into the night; and You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living. And You give provision to whom You will without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute control over the natural order and the balance of life. The act of bringing night into day and vice versa illustrates His power to control time and the cycles of existence. The transformation of the living into the dead and the dead into the living signifies the divine authority over life and death, highlighting the interconnectedness of these states. Furthermore, the mention of providing sustenance without account reflects God's generosity and omnipotence, indicating that He can grant wealth and provisions beyond human understanding or measure, showing that all exists by His will and grace.
orig: تولج الليل في النهار وتولج النهار في الليل وتخرج الحي من الميت وتخرج الميت من الحي وترزق من تشاء بغير حساب

translation: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except that you guard yourselves against them, taking [precaution] through fear of them. And Allah warns you of Himself. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of allegiance and loyalty among believers, highlighting that forming alliances with disbelievers can endanger one's faith and connection to God. It also conveys the notion of self-preservation in situations where believers might face oppression or harm from disbelievers, permitting a form of caution or tactical distancing. Ultimately, it serves as a reminder that one's ultimate accountability lies with Allah, who is aware of our intentions and actions, and to whom we will return for judgment.
orig: لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Say, "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And Allah is over all things Competent."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive knowledge and awareness of all that lies within human hearts, whether hidden or expressed. It highlights the idea that Allah's understanding transcends mere words or actions, extending to the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals. The phrase 'Allah is over all things Competent' serves to remind believers that Allah's power and authority encompass everything, reinforcing the importance of sincerity and transparency in one's faith and deeds.
orig: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ويعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: On the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good present (before it), and what it has done of evil, it will wish that there were between it and that evil a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself. And Allah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reality of accountability in the afterlife, where every individual will confront the consequences of their actions—both good and bad. The phrase about wishing for a great distance from evil signifies the deep regret and desire to avoid the repercussions of one's wrongdoings. The warning from Allah about Himself underscores the importance of self-awareness and the need to reflect on one's deeds. It also highlights God's compassion, as He is portrayed as forgiving and merciful, inviting individuals to turn back to Him despite their shortcomings.
orig: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: Say, "If you love Allah, then follow me, so Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad as a means to express love for Allah. It conveys a profound message that true love for God is not just an internal feeling but is demonstrated through actions and obedience. The promise of Allah's love and forgiveness reinforces the idea that divine mercy is accessible to those who sincerely strive to align their lives with His guidance. The verse highlights the attributes of Allah as Forgiving and Merciful, serving as a reassurance that no matter the faults or sins of individuals, repentance and adherence to His path can lead to forgiveness.
orig: قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and the Messenger.' But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger as a fundamental principle of faith. It implies that true believers should willingly adhere to divine guidance. The mention of those who turn away indicates a warning against rebellion or disbelief; it acknowledges that such actions lead to a loss of divine favor. The use of 'disbelievers' here serves to create a clear distinction between believers who submit to divine authority and those who reject it, thus elevating the moral responsibility to follow the teachings of Islam.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله والرسول فإن تولوا فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies the special favor and selection of certain prophets and their families by Allah, highlighting their elevated status among humanity. It points to the importance of these figures in conveying divine messages and leading their communities. The mention of family lineage emphasizes the continuity of faith and the pivotal roles that these chosen individuals played in shaping the spiritual and moral dimensions of their societies. Their selection serves as a reminder of the divine guidance provided to humanity through prophets across generations.
orig: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

translation: Offspring, one of the other. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the interconnectedness of humanity, illustrating that all humans are part of a continuous chain of creation, descended from one another. It highlights the familial bonds that exist among people, suggesting that while each individual is unique, we are all part of the same human family. Furthermore, the mention of Allah being 'Hearing and Knowing' serves as a reminder that He is aware of all actions, intentions, and connections within this lineage, reinforcing the idea that our relationships and behaviors towards each other are under divine observation and accountability.
orig: ذرية بعضها من بعض والله سميع عليم

translation: When the wife of Imran said, 'My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep devotion and commitment of a mother, in this case, the wife of Imran, who dedicates her unborn child to the service of God. It signifies an understanding of the significance of purpose in life, as she recognizes her child as a gift for divine service, echoing themes of sacrifice and faith. The invocation for acceptance emphasizes her reliance on God's omniscience and omnipresence, showing that sincere intentions and acts of worship are valued in the sight of God.
orig: إذ قالت امرأت عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she delivered. And the male is not like the female. And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her offspring from Satan, the expelled.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the significance of gender and the unique status of Mary (Maryam) as a female figure in Islamic tradition. It highlights a mother’s emotional attachment and her apprehensions about the future of her daughter in a society that often prioritized males. The declaration that 'the male is not like the female' underscores the recognition of the differing roles and qualities of each gender. Furthermore, the act of seeking refuge for Mary and her offspring from Satan signifies the protective measures taken by the mother, which can be seen as a universal concern for the well-being of one’s children against negative influences. Mary is presented as a special individual with divine protection, highlighting her importance in the faith.
orig: فلما وضعتها قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت وليس الذكر كالأنثى وإني سميتها مريم وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and entrusted her to Zechariah. Whenever Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision. He said, "O Mary, from where is this coming to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and provision bestowed upon Mary (Maryam), illustrating the miraculous nature of her sustenance, which comes directly from Allah. It emphasizes the idea that God supplies and bestows bounty upon individuals beyond conventional means, reinforcing the theme of trust in divine provisions. The mention of Zechariah's role as her guardian suggests a continuity of support and guidance, while Mary's response serves as a reminder of the boundless possibilities of God's mercy and power. This narrative illustrates the importance of faith in God's providence amidst challenging circumstances.
orig: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا وكفلها زكريا كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: There, Zakariya called upon his Lord, saying, 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep yearning and humility of Zakariya (Zachariah) as he earnestly seeks the blessing of a righteous child from Allah. It underscores the significance of making sincere supplications and acknowledges God's responsiveness to the cries of His servants. The term 'good offspring' implies not only a desire for children but also reflects the hope for them to be virtuous and pious, further emphasizing the link between prayer and divine mercy in fulfilling such heartfelt requests.
orig: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة إنك سميع الدعاء

translation: And the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah and distinguished, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine announcement of the birth of Yahya (John the Baptist) to his father, Zachariah, emphasizing the miraculous nature of this event. It signals Yahya's significant role as a prophet who will confirm the message of God and his virtuous qualities, such as being chaste and a leader among the righteous. The mention of him being a 'word from Allah' underscores the miraculous conception and the importance of his prophetic mission, positioning him within the larger narrative of the prophetic lineage in Islam.
orig: فنادته الملائكة وهو قائم يصلي في المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا من الصالحين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy when I have reached old age and my wife is barren?' He said, 'Thus Allah does what He wills.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the theme of divine power and the miraculous nature of God's will. It illustrates the dialogue between Prophet Zakariya and Allah, emphasizing human limitations in the face of divine possibilities. Zakariya’s question stems from his disbelief at the prospect of having a son due to his old age and his wife's barrenness. Allah’s response signifies that what seems impossible to humans is entirely possible for Him, reinforcing the belief in God's sovereignty and ability to bring forth life in any circumstance. This teaches the faithful to trust in God's plans, regardless of their current situation or understanding.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وقد بلغني الكبر وامرأتي عاقر قال كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, having lost your voice. And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning.'
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound communication between the Prophet Zakariya (Zachariah) and Allah. Zakariya's request for a sign reflects his human desire for reassurance regarding the miraculous birth of his son, Yahya (John). Allah responds not only by granting him a sign but also by imposing a period of silence, which serves a dual purpose: it emphasizes the miraculous nature of the event and deepens Zakariya's spiritual connection to Allah. The instruction to 'remember your Lord much and glorify Him' highlights the importance of constant remembrance of God in both times of trial and ease, encouraging believers to engage in regular worship and reflection—especially during the quiet moments of the evening and morning.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا واذكر ربك كثيرا وسبح بالعشي والإبكار

translation: And when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, and that word is the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those who are near [to Allah ]'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the extraordinary status granted to Mary (Mariam) by Allah, highlighting her selection and purification. It reflects not only her unique virtue among women but also her key role in the divine plan as the mother of Jesus (Isa), who is honored in both this life and the next. The verse signifies the honor bestowed upon Mary, showcasing her as an exemplary figure of faith and obedience, illustrating that divine choices are rooted in purity and purpose.
orig: وإذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله اصطفاك وطهرك واصطفاك على نساء العالمين

translation: O Mary, be devout to your Lord and prostrate and bow down along with those who bow down.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of devotion and humility in worship. It calls Mary to engage in acts of worship—specifically praying and performing bowing and prostration, which are fundamental aspects of submission to God. The directive to join 'those who bow down' suggests a sense of community in faith, indicating that worship is not just an individual act but one that is linked to a collective devotion. It also highlights Mary’s exemplary status as a figure of obedience and piety, reinforcing her role in Islamic tradition as a model for faithful submission to God.
orig: يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen, which We reveal to you; and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that the events surrounding the birth of Mary and the subsequent disputes were known to Him alone. It serves to affirm the prophetic status of Muhammad, as he was not present during these historical moments, yet he is given knowledge of them through revelation. The casting of pens symbolizes the serious decisions made regarding Mary's guardianship, showcasing the human element of decision-making while underlining that such matters are part of a larger divine plan. The verse reinforces the idea that while people may engage in debates and choices, ultimately, it is Allah who orchestrates the outcomes, highlighting His power and foreknowledge.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون

translation: When the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine announcement made to Mary regarding the miraculous birth of Jesus (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the significance of Jesus as the Messiah, indicating his elevated status and distinctive role in both earthly existence and the afterlife. The verse also underscores the importance of Mary in this miraculous event and signifies the closeness of Jesus to Allah. It reflects the theme of divine intervention and the fulfillment of prophecies regarding the coming of a significant figure in spiritual history.
orig: إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله يبشرك بكلمة منه اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين

translation: And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be one of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of Jesus (Isa) speaking as an infant, indicating his unique status and divine mission. It highlights the idea that wisdom and prophethood are not confined to age; even as a child, he possesses knowledge and the ability to communicate divine truths. His growth into adulthood as 'one of the righteous' reinforces the continuity of righteousness and guidance throughout his life. This serves as a reminder of the potential for wisdom and virtue to manifest regardless of age.
orig: ويكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا ومن الصالحين

translation: She said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy when no man has touched me?' He said, 'Thus said Allah, He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be!' and it is.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine power of Allah and His capability to bring about creation from impossible circumstances. The reply emphasizes that God's will transcends human limitations and natural laws. It signifies that when Allah decides a matter, it is fulfilled instantly and effortlessly by His command. This also reflects the concept in Islam that miracles can occur by Divine decree, reaffirming faith in God's omnipotence and the nature of miraculous births in religious narratives.
orig: قالت رب أنى يكون لي ولد ولم يمسسني بشر قال كذلك الله يخلق ما يشاء إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine knowledge bestowed upon certain individuals, particularly Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). It signifies the importance of scripture and wisdom in guiding humanity, linking the teachings of the Qur'an with previous revelations such as the Torah and the Gospel. This indicates a continuity in divine guidance and the necessity of wisdom in understanding and applying the teachings of these scriptures in a meaningful way.
orig: ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل

translation: And [I am] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [I have come] to you with a sign from your Lord, that I design for you from clay [something] like the form of a bird; then I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird, by permission of Allah.
