And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life, by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your homes. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous powers granted to Prophet Jesus (Isa) as evidence of his prophethood. The act of creating a bird from clay and breathing life into it symbolizes divine authority over life and creation, establishing that true power belongs to Allah alone. Furthermore, the healing of the blind and leper, as well as raising the dead, points to the compassion and mercy that accompany divine signs. Additionally, the ability to know the unseen aspects of people’s lives shows deep insight and knowledge, reinforcing the message that faith must be based on signs and miracles that testify to the truth of his message. For believers, these acts validate the existence of a higher power and serve as encouragement to hold steadfast in their faith.
orig: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيي الموتى بإذن الله وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And confirming that which is before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you part of that which was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord; so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance through scriptures. It highlights the role of the Prophet in affirming the teachings of previous revelations, particularly the Torah, while also introducing new directives that facilitate spiritual and social well-being. The call to 'fear Allah and obey me' underlines the importance of piety and adherence to divine commandments, as well as the concept of obedience to prophetic authority, which is essential for believers seeking to align their lives with God's will.
orig: ومصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم وجئتكم بآية من ربكم فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord; so worship Him. This is the Straight Path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshiping Him alone. It signifies the relationship of Allah as not only the Creator but also as a guiding force for humanity. The phrase 'this is the Straight Path' indicates that following the guidance of Allah leads to righteousness and clarity in life, contrasting with paths that may lead one astray. It serves as a reminder that the worship of Allah must be sincere and dedicated, aligning oneself with His will.
orig: إن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And when Jesus felt [persistence in] disbelief from them, he said, 'Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah. We have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse exemplifies the theme of seeking support in the face of adversity. Jesus, sensing the disbelief around him, calls for those who will stand with him in faith. The response from the disciples reflects their unwavering commitment and solidarity with his mission. They express their belief and identification as Muslims, highlighting the importance of faith and the collective action of believers. This interaction underscores the necessity of community and support in propagating faith, particularly during challenging times of doubt and skepticism.
orig: فلما أحس عيسى منهم الكفر قال من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You have revealed and have followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep commitment and sincerity in faith. It signifies a recognition of divine guidance through revelation and the importance of following the Messenger of Allah. The plea to be registered among the witnesses highlights the desire to be part of a community that acknowledges the truth, thereby striving to uphold righteousness and integrity in their beliefs. It embodies the aspiration for a collective testimony to faith, indicating the communal aspect of spirituality and the importance of accountability in one's actions.
orig: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of human scheming against divine will. It emphasizes that while people may devise intricate plans to achieve their goals or to harm others, God's wisdom and strategy far surpass and ultimately prevail over all human efforts. The assurance that Allah is 'the best of planners' serves to bolster the faith of the believers, illustrating that divine intervention can thwart the malicious intents of those who oppose the truth.
orig: ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: When Allah said, 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and cleanse you of those who disbelieve and make those who follow you in submission [to Allah alone] [in religion] superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise of protection and honor bestowed upon Jesus and his followers, contrasting their faith with that of disbelievers. It signifies that true believers in God's message will ultimately prevail and be vindicated, suggesting a division between faith and disbelief that holds significance until the Day of Judgment. Furthermore, it reminds believers of their ultimate return to Allah, where true justice will be served regarding their disputes, reinforcing the importance of adhering to God's guidance and the ultimate supremacy of faith.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي ومطهرك من الذين كفروا وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا إلى يوم القيامة ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief in God, indicating that it results in severe punishment both in this life and in the Hereafter. It highlights the lack of any means of support or intercession for those who reject faith, stressing the isolation and helplessness they will face in their judgment.
orig: فأما الذين كفروا فأعذبهم عذابا شديدا في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds, We will surely give them a reward in full, and Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and reward. It highlights that faith combined with righteous actions leads to fulfillment of rewards from Allah, affirming that true belief must be accompanied by good deeds. Moreover, it underscores that Allah's disfavor is upon those who commit injustices or wrongs, suggesting that social and moral injustices are not tolerated in the realm of faith.
orig: وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: This We recite to you from the verses and the Wise Reminder.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of divine revelation, indicating that the messages conveyed are not mere words but verses with profound wisdom. The use of 'Wise Reminder' suggests that these revelations serve as a guide for moral and spiritual awakening, encouraging reflection and understanding of deeper truths about existence and one's relationship with the Divine.
orig: ذلك نتلوه عليك من الآيات والذكر الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of creation in Islam, emphasizing that both Adam and Jesus were created by God's command. It underscores that divine will alone is sufficient for creation, illustrating that Jesus, like Adam, is a significant figure in Islamic theology without the need for a natural lineage. This reinforces the idea of God's absolute power and the equality of all prophets in the face of divine creativity, clarifying misconceptions about Jesus' nature and role.
orig: إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the truth as a divine revelation from God. It encourages believers to have steadfast faith and not to fall into doubt or uncertainty regarding His message. The instruction to avoid being 'among the doubters' serves as a reminder to maintain conviction and trust in God's guidance, especially in the face of challenges or skepticism.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين

translation: So whoever argues with you about it after what has come to you of knowledge, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us supplicate earnestly, and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars."
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of mutual understanding and clarity in faith. It highlights the seriousness of debating religious truths, emphasizing that if someone challenges the truth after having been informed, the response should be one of deep spiritual engagement. The call to 'bring our families' signifies the importance of collective certainty and the gravity of invoking divine judgment upon falsehood. It symbolizes a profound commitment to truth, urging believers to stand firmly with their community in the pursuit of faith, and portrays the necessity for a shared quest for truth in dialogue.
orig: فمن حاجك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنت الله على الكاذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the true narrative, and there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity of the stories conveyed in the Qur'an, asserting that they are not mere tales but hold profound truths. It underscores the oneness of God, reinforcing the central tenet of monotheism in Islam. The attributes of Allah being 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise' suggest His supreme authority and knowledge, highlighting that His decrees and narratives are beyond human comprehension and possess ultimate wisdom.
orig: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: But if they turn away, indeed Allah is All-Knowing of the corruptors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the awareness and knowledge of Allah regarding those who choose to reject guidance or turn away from the truth. It highlights the idea that divine observation goes beyond mere actions, focusing on the intentions and moral corruption that may lie within individuals or communities. The mention of 'corruptors' implies that turning away from Allah's path can lead to societal or personal degradation, and serves as a warning of accountability in the face of such choices.
orig: فإن تولوا فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is common between us and you: that we not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords instead of Allah.' But if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the call for dialogue and unity among different religious communities, specifically between Muslims and the People of the Book (Christians and Jews). It invites them to come together on fundamental principles of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry. The emphasis is on worshiping Allah alone and recognizing Him as the sole authority. The mention of not taking each other as lords underlines the importance of divine sovereignty over human authority. The final statement serves as a declaration of faith and identity for Muslims, asserting their commitment to Islam even in the face of rejection.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you dispute about Abraham when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Do you not understand?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, namely Jews and Christians, questioning their disputes regarding the figure of Abraham. It highlights the fact that both the Torah and the Gospel, which are foundational texts for these faiths, were revealed after Abraham’s time. The verse implies that arguing about Abraham’s role or the legitimacy of different religious narratives is illogical, considering that the key texts that define their beliefs came later. It invites the audience to reflect on the significance of Abraham as a common ancestor in faith, thereby urging an understanding that transcends doctrinal differences.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تحاجون في إبراهيم وما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل إلا من بعده أفلا تعقلون

translation: Here you are, you have argued about that of which you have knowledge, but why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the tendency of some individuals to engage in debates and discussions about matters beyond their understanding or knowledge. It highlights a fundamental principle: that discussions should be grounded in knowledge and understanding. It underscores the distinction between what is known and what is unknown, suggesting that arrogance in disputation, especially on matters that are not clearly understood, is misguided. The verse serves as a reminder to humbly acknowledge the limits of one's knowledge and to trust in Allah's ultimate understanding of all matters, encouraging believers to seek genuine knowledge and to be cautious in their assertions.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء حاججتم فيما لكم به علم فلم تحاجون فيما ليس لكم به علم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a Hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that true monotheism and submission to God were embodied in the figure of Abraham, who existed prior to the establishment of Judaism and Christianity. It highlights the concept of 'Hanif', which signifies a pure and uncorrupted faith in one God, signifying that Abraham is a model of those who submit to God without associating partners with Him. This underscores the universality of the message of Islam, suggesting that all true believers ultimately follow the path of Abraham, transcending institutional religious identities and focusing on the essence of faith.
orig: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا ولا نصرانيا ولكن كان حنيفا مسلما وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the closest people to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the ally of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the bond between Prophet Abraham and his followers, emphasizing that true kinship and closeness are determined by faith and allegiance to God's messengers. It suggests that belief is a unifying force that transcends mere biological relationships. The inclusion of 'this Prophet' refers to Muhammad, linking him to the legacy of Abraham and reinforcing the message of faith as central to the community of believers. Moreover, the affirmation that 'Allah is the ally of the believers' serves as a powerful reminder that divine support and guidance are granted to those who truly believe and follow the right path.
orig: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا والله ولي المؤمنين

translation: A sect of the People of the Book wish that they could mislead you, but they only mislead themselves, and they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of envy and malice. It points out that some individuals from among the People of the Book desire to lead others astray, driven by their own discontent or rivalry. However, their attempts to mislead others only result in their own self-deception, as they fail to realize that genuine belief and guidance cannot be transferred through manipulation. This reinforces the idea that one's spiritual state is marked more by their intentions and understanding than by external influences, prompting reflection on the importance of seeking truth and staying steadfast in one's own faith.
orig: ودت طائفة من أهل الكتاب لو يضلونكم وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while you witness [their truth]?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, primarily Christians and Jews, highlighting the contradiction of denying God's revelations despite acknowledging their authenticity. It calls for introspection about their beliefs and actions, urging them to recognize and affirm the truth of divine guidance that they have received. The emphasis on 'witnessing' implies that they have knowledge and understanding of God's signs, yet they choose disbelief, which is presented as both illogical and a grave error. This verse serves as a reminder of accountability and the importance of aligning one's beliefs with the truth.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله وأنتم تشهدون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know [it]?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, urging them to stop the practice of distorting the truth to suit their interests and to be honest in their beliefs. It highlights the moral responsibility of possessing knowledge and the importance of acting upon it. The act of mixing truth with falsehood suggests a manipulation of divine revelations for personal or communal gain, which is deemed a serious offense. This call to honesty emphasizes that knowledge should lead to truthful expression and integrity in faith.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل وتكتمون الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: A party of the People of the Book said, 'Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day and reject it at its end, so perhaps they will return.'
interpretation: This verse highlights a manipulative strategy attributed to some among the People of the Book, suggesting that they intended to sow doubt among the believers by encouraging them to believe in the truth of their message temporarily, as a means to create confusion and division. The verse underscores the themes of faith, deception, and the struggle between belief and disbelief, illustrating how some may take advantage of the vulnerability of others for their own ends. It serves as a reminder for the followers of the faith to remain steadfast in their beliefs and wary of such tactics.
orig: وقالت طائفة من أهل الكتاب آمنوا بالذي أنزل على الذين آمنوا وجه النهار واكفروا آخره لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And do not trust except those who follow your religion. Say, 'Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah, that anyone should be given the like of what you have been given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord.' Say, 'Indeed, the favor is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing and All-Wise.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the exclusivity often held by certain groups regarding faith and guidance. It emphasizes that true guidance comes from Allah alone, not from any specific group or individual. The verse also highlights the idea that Allah's favor and wisdom are beyond human comprehension; He grants His bounties to whom He wishes regardless of their lineage or religious affiliation. The emphasis is on humility and recognition that one's blessings are a result of divine choice rather than personal merit or the validity of one's beliefs alone. This serves as a reminder to avoid arrogance and to seek understanding and unity in faith.
orig: ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم قل إن الهدى هدى الله أن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم أو يحاجوكم عند ربكم قل إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: He selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine selection and mercy. It emphasizes that God's mercy is not arbitrary but is granted to those who are chosen by Him, indicating a profound wisdom behind His decisions. It invites believers to recognize that mercy is a gift from God, associated with His will and wisdom. Furthermore, the phrase ‘Allah is the Possessor of great bounty’ underscores the vastness and abundance of God's favors, suggesting that His grace and generosity are beyond human comprehension.
orig: يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And among the People of the Book is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount of wealth, he will return it to you; and among them is he who, if you entrust him with a single coin, will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him. This is because they say, 'There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered.' And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it to be true].
interpretation: This verse highlights the varying degrees of trustworthiness among the People of the Book, indicating that some individuals are reliable and uphold their commitments while others betray trust, especially when dealing with those they consider inferior or uneducated. It critiques a mentality that justifies dishonesty towards non-believers and reflects a deeper issue of moral integrity and accountability. The assertion of a lack of responsibility towards 'the unlettered' illustrates a flawed view that diminishes the intrinsic value of all human relationships, regardless of faith or knowledge, and reinforces the importance of honesty and accountability in all transactions, as these define a person's character.
orig: ومن أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار يؤده إليك ومنهم من إن تأمنه بدينار لا يؤده إليك إلا ما دمت عليه قائما ذلك بأنهم قالوا ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, whoever fulfills his pledge and fears [Allah] – indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being trustworthy and pious. The fulfillment of promises is a significant trait in a believer, reflecting their commitment to honesty and integrity. Coupled with the concept of 'taqwa' (piety or fear of God), it suggests that true righteousness stems from a combination of fulfilling one's commitments and maintaining a consciousness of God in all actions. The love of Allah is bestowed upon those who embody these qualities, indicating that piety and trustworthiness are key attributes that draw individuals closer to Him.
orig: بلى من أوفى بعهده واتقى فإن الله يحب المتقين

translation: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, they will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them, nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave consequence of those who violate their sacred commitments and oaths in exchange for worldly gains. It serves as a warning that such actions lead not only to a loss of divine favor but to a complete estrangement from Allah in the Hereafter. The reference to Allah not speaking to them, nor looking at them, signifies a total rejection and evidence of severe punishment awaiting them. This encapsulates the seriousness of dishonoring one's word, especially when tied to one's faith and covenant with God, highlighting the importance of integrity and moral responsibility in the life of a believer.
orig: إن الذين يشترون بعهد الله وأيمانهم ثمنا قليلا أولئك لا خلاق لهم في الآخرة ولا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, among them is a party that twists their tongues with the Book so that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book; and they say, 'It is from Allah,' but it is not from Allah; and they speak untruth about Allah while they know.
interpretation: This verse addresses a critical issue concerning the manipulation of divine texts for personal gain or deceptive purposes. It highlights how some individuals or groups alter the meanings of sacred scriptures, presenting them as authentic when they are not. This act not only misleads others but also constitutes a severe violation of the trust placed in them regarding the truth of faith. The verse warns of the dire consequences of such actions, emphasizing the moral responsibility that comes with knowledge and the grave sin of bearing false witness against God.
orig: وإن منهم لفريقا يلوون ألسنتهم بالكتاب لتحسبوه من الكتاب وما هو من الكتاب ويقولون هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Scripture and the judgment and the prophethood, and then he says to the people, 'Be my servants rather than Allah's;' but [instead, he would say], 'Be pious scholars by virtue of what you have taught of the Scripture and what you have studied.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of true servitude to Allah alone, delineating that even those who are granted divine knowledge, such as prophets and scholars, do not seek to be worshipped themselves but guide others towards the worship of Allah. It affirms that the role of such individuals is to educate people in divine matters and encourage them to grow in their understanding and fear of Allah, thereby cultivating a community of knowledgeable and pious individuals anchored in the teachings of the Scriptures.
orig: ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله ولكن كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون

translation: And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the true nature of worship in Islam. It indicates that neither angels nor prophets should be revered to the extent of being considered divine or worthy of worship. Instead, they are servants of Allah. The verse challenges any notion that would lead believers to disobey the fundamental tenet of Islam, which is the oneness of God (Tawhid). It highlights the absurdity of turning away from monotheism after having embraced Islam, underlining that true submission should lead to a deep understanding of the sole authority and divinity of Allah.
orig: ولا يأمركم أن تتخذوا الملائكة والنبيين أربابا أيأمركم بالكفر بعد إذ أنتم مسلمون

translation: And when Allah took the covenant from the prophets, [He said], 'What I have given you of scripture and wisdom, then comes to you a messenger confirming that which is with you, you must believe in him and support him.' He said, 'Do you affirm and accept My covenant on that?' They said, 'We affirm.' He said, 'Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significant covenant that Allah established with all prophets, highlighting the importance of a unified message of belief and support for the coming of the final messenger. The essence of this agreement underscores accountability among the prophets to each other and to their mission, invoking a collective responsibility to uphold the guidance provided through divine scriptures. This concept indicates that faith and support for the truth revealed to one’s own prophet extends to affirming and aiding others who come with the same message, thus binding the community of believers across different eras and revelations. The act of bearing witness signifies a profound commitment to testify not only in belief but also in action, reinforcing the idea that spiritual responsibilities are interconnected and mutually reinforcing.
orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة ثم جاءكم رسول مصدق لما معكم لتؤمنن به ولتنصرنه قال أأقررتم وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري قالوا أقررنا قال فاشهدوا وأنا معكم من الشاهدين

translation: But whosoever turns away after that, they are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of turning away from guidance and the truth after it has been presented. It emphasizes that those who choose to reject the message do so out of willful defiance, and as a result, they fall into the category of 'fasiqoon' (transgressors), who are characterized by their disobedience and deviation from the right path. This serves as a warning about the seriousness of neglecting divine guidance and the moral responsibilities of individuals.
orig: فمن تولى بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Is it other than the religion of Allah that they desire, while to Him have submitted all those within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned?
interpretation: This verse highlights the universality of submission to God's will, asserting that all beings in existence, whether they acknowledge it or not, ultimately operate under divine authority. The phrasing suggests that human efforts to seek alternative paths to salvation or righteousness are futile since God's plan encompasses all creation. The mention of returning to God emphasizes accountability and the ultimate reality of divine judgment, reinforcing the idea that true peace and resolution lies in acceptance of God's guidance.
orig: أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون

translation: Say, 'We have believed in Allah and in that which was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims to Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of belief in all prophets and revelations sent by Allah throughout history. It highlights the idea of inclusivity in faith, asserting that true believers accept all prophets without distinction, recognizing them as part of one divine message. The declaration of being 'Muslims' underlines a commitment to submission to Allah's will, reinforcing the concept that faith is holistic and interconnected, transcending divisions that may arise among different religious communities.
orig: قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا وما أنزل على إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى والنبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam – it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Islam as the only acceptable path to God. It conveys the message that adherence to any belief system outside of Islam will not grant an individual spiritual fulfillment or acceptance in the eyes of God. The finality of this statement underscores the importance of choosing the right faith and suggests that the ultimate consequence of rejecting Islam leads to loss in the afterlife, highlighting a critical warning for believers regarding the gravity of their spiritual choices.
orig: ومن يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: How can Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their faith and bore witness that the Messenger is true, and came to them the clear proofs? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of turning away from faith after having recognized the truth of Allah's messenger and the evidence provided. It emphasizes the seriousness of disbelief following belief and serves as a warning about the consequences of such actions. The phrase 'Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people' indicates that persistent rejection of truth leads to divine guidance being withdrawn, pointing to the important concept that faith must be maintained with sincerity and integrity.
orig: كيف يهدي الله قوما كفروا بعد إيمانهم وشهدوا أن الرسول حق وجاءهم البينات والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those are the ones for whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of the people, all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences awaiting those who commit grave sins or act with injustice, indicating that they are not only condemned by Allah but also by the angels and all people. It illustrates the universality of their condemnation and the seriousness of their actions, underscoring the idea that such behavior alienates individuals not just from divine mercy but from communal acceptance as well.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم أن عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: They will abide therein, and the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence and severity of the punishment for those who disbelieve or commit grave sins. The use of 'خالدين فيها' indicates an eternal state, reinforcing that once they are subjected to this punishment, there is no reprieve or alleviation. It serves as a stern warning about the consequences of their actions and the justice of divine retribution. The absence of hope for mercy ('ولا هم ينظرون') signifies the finality of their fate, suggesting that they will face the consequences of their choices without any possibility of escape or forgiveness. This underlines the importance of moral accountability and the significance of belief and righteousness in shaping one's destiny.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and transformation. It indicates that no matter the severity of one's past actions, sincere repentance and efforts to improve are met with God's mercy and forgiveness. The verse highlights that God's compassion and willingness to forgive are vast, offering hope to those who seek to amend their ways and grow spiritually.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their faith and then increased in disbelief, their repentance will not be accepted, and they are the ones who are astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of forsaking faith after having accepted it, highlighting that persistent denial of truth after belief reflects a deep-rooted rejection of guidance. It signifies that a point may be reached where repentance is no longer possible, underscoring the importance of maintaining one's faith and the dangers of turning away from it, suggesting that true faith requires steadfastness and sincerity.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بعد إيمانهم ثم ازدادوا كفرا لن تقبل توبتهم وأولئك هم الضالون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never will the earth's fill of gold be accepted from any one of them, even if he should offer it as a ransom. Those are for them a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of faith in one's life, pointing out that mere wealth or material offerings cannot substitute for the belief in God. It underscores the futility of trying to redeem oneself after death through material means if one has lived a life of disbelief. The 'painful punishment' mentioned serves as a warning and reinforces that in the afterlife, spiritual state and belief are of utmost importance, rather than worldly possessions or status.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به أولئك لهم عذاب أليم وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. And whatever you spend, indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of selflessness and the willingness to sacrifice what one holds dear for the sake of righteousness and the betterment of others. It suggests that true piety and closeness to Allah cannot be achieved merely through belief or ritual acts; rather, it requires tangible deeds. By spending from what one loves, individuals demonstrate their commitment to faith and compassion, highlighting that their intentions and actions are closely observed by Allah.
orig: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون وما تنفقوا من شيء فإن الله به عليم

translation: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel, except what Israel (Jacob) made unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, 'Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of dietary laws and how they pertain specifically to the Children of Israel, highlighting that prior to the revelation of the Torah, they had a different set of dietary guidelines based on their ancestor Jacob’s personal prohibitions. It challenges those who claim adherence to the truth of their religious claims to substantiate them with the Torah, indicating that the foundational texts hold authority over religious practices. This serves as a reminder of the importance of knowledge and scripture in defining and understanding one's faith and practices.
orig: كل الطعام كان حلا لبني إسرائيل إلا ما حرم إسرائيل على نفسه من قبل أن تنزل التوراة قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: So whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after that - those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness of attributing falsehoods to Allah. It highlights that fabricating lies in the name of God is a grave injustice and a violation of the truth. Those who engage in such actions are classified as wrongdoers, indicating that they are not only misleading others but also committing an offense against divine authority. This serves as a warning against false statements and misrepresentation of God's words or attributes, stressing the importance of truthfulness and integrity in matters of faith.
orig: فمن افترى على الله الكذب من بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, "Allah has spoken the truth; so follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the path of monotheism as demonstrated by Prophet Abraham. It calls for adherence to a pure and unadulterated faith, free from polytheism, suggesting that true submission to God is characterized by a sincere alignment with His oneness. The reference to Abraham serves as a model for believers, highlighting his unwavering commitment to God and his rejection of idolatry, thus urging the followers to emulate his stance in their faith.
orig: قل صدق الله فاتبعوا ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: The first House established for mankind was indeed the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Kaaba in Mecca, known as Bakkah, as the first place of worship dedicated to Allah. It emphasizes its sanctity and importance as a unifying symbol for all believers. The mention of it being a 'guidance for the worlds' indicates that it serves not only the immediate community but holds universal relevance for all of humanity. It reflects the notion that true guidance from God is available to everyone, transcending geographical and cultural boundaries, inviting individuals across different backgrounds to seek spiritual connection and unity in their worship.
orig: إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذي ببكة مباركا وهدى للعالمين

translation: In it are clear signs [such as] the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe. And [due] to Allah from the people is [a pilgrimage to] the House - for whoever is able to make the journey thereto. And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is Free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and significance of the Kaaba in Mecca, highlighting it as a place of spiritual safety and divine signs. The mention of 'the standing place of Abraham' serves to connect the sanctuary to the legacy of the prophet Abraham, reinforcing the concept of faith and submission to God. The command to perform pilgrimage (Hajj) outlines the obligation for those who possess the means to do so, demonstrating the importance of physical and spiritual devotion in Islam. The concluding statement about disbelievers reflects God's independence from humanity's beliefs, illustrating that faith is a personal obligation with spiritual consequences.
orig: فيه آيات بينات مقام إبراهيم ومن دخله كان آمنا ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا ومن كفر فإن الله غني عن العالمين

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians), calling out their disbelief in the divine signs and revelations. It emphasizes that despite their knowledge and heritage of past revelations, they are questioned about their rejection of the truth. The phrase 'Allah is Witness over what you do' serves as a reminder of divine observation and accountability. This calls for self-reflection on one's faith and actions, highlighting the seriousness of disbelief in the context of divine signs and the reality of God's omniscience.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله والله شهيد على ما تعملون

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, why do you avert those who have believed from the path of Allah, seeking to make it appear deviant, while you witness [to its truth]? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the People of the Scripture, particularly the Jews and Christians, to reflect on their actions of leading believers away from the path of Allah. It emphasizes the seriousness of their role as witnesses to the truth of divine revelation, suggesting that their denial or distortion of faith is both deceptive and detrimental. The phrase 'seeking to make it appear deviant' highlights the intent behind their actions, which is not merely passive but actively attempts to misguide others. Moreover, it reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of all human actions, signalling that there will be consequences for such behavior. This verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and the responsibility to uphold and spread the truth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن تبغونها عوجا وأنتم شهداء وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back after your belief to being disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers, emphasizing the importance of remaining steadfast in their faith and not being swayed by those who may distort or undermine their beliefs, particularly individuals from the People of the Book. It highlights the potential danger of external influences that can lead one to renounce their faith, reminding the community to be vigilant and discerning in their interactions with others, especially regarding matters of belief and spirituality.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا فريقا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب يردوكم بعد إيمانكم كافرين

translation: And how can you disbelieve while to you are recited the verses of Allah and among you is His Messenger? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has indeed been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound contradiction of disbelief among those who have direct access to divine revelations and the presence of the Prophet Muhammad, who embodies the message of Islam. It highlights the significance of holding on to one's faith and connection with Allah as the true source of guidance. The notion of 'holding firmly to Allah' signifies not just belief, but an active commitment to the teachings of Islam, ensuring one's path aligns with divine guidance. This serves as a reminder of the responsibilities individuals carry in acknowledging the signs of God and the role of the Prophet in their lives.
orig: وكيف تكفرون وأنتم تتلى عليكم آيات الله وفيكم رسوله ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah with [the fear He deserves], and do not die except as Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a deep and genuine consciousness of Allah (taqwa), underscoring that true faith requires not just acknowledgment of Allah's existence, but also living in accordance with His commands to the utmost degree. It serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive for righteousness throughout their lives, ultimately encouraging them to ensure that they leave this world with their faith intact, identifying as Muslims. The exhortation to fear Allah 'as He deserves' suggests a recognition of His greatness and mercy, prompting believers to live with responsibility and moral integrity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and by His favor you became brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of fire, and He saved you from it. Thus Allah makes clear His verses to you that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity among believers, urging them to hold together firmly to the guidance of Allah. The reference to Allah's past favor highlights how He transformed enmity into brotherhood, underscoring His mercy and the transformative power of faith. The imagery of being on the brink of a pit of fire serves as a reminder of the consequences of division and conflict, and the importance of remaining steadfast in faith to avoid spiritual peril. Ultimately, this passage calls for reflection on divine guidance and the necessity of communal harmony for spiritual progress.
orig: واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ كنتم أعداء فألف بين قلوبكم فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا وكنتم على شفا حفرة من النار فأنقذكم منها كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to all that is good and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And those will be the succeeding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of communal responsibility among believers to promote virtue and prevent vice. It highlights the concept of a dedicated group or nation within the community that actively engages in the promotion of good and the prevention of wrongdoing. Such action is portrayed as a key characteristic of successful individuals or groups in the eyes of God, indicating that societal reform and moral leadership are essential for spiritual success and fulfillment.
orig: ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And do not be like those who divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against division and discord among the community, especially after receiving clear guidance and evidence. It highlights the importance of unity and adherence to the truth, urging believers to remain steadfast in faith and avoid the pitfalls of sectarianism and disputes. The mention of a 'great punishment' underscores the seriousness of such divisions, indicating that those who fail to uphold unity in the wake of the truth will face dire consequences.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا من بعد ما جاءهم البينات وأولئك لهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On the Day when some faces will become bright, and some faces will become dark. As for those whose faces have turned dark, 'Did you disbelieve after your faith? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrasting fate of the believers and disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The brightness of some faces symbolizes the joy and reward for the believers, while the darkness of others' faces reflects despair and regret for those who turned away from faith. The rhetorical question directed at those with darkened faces underscores their choice to reject belief and the consequences that follow. It serves as a powerful reminder that the choices made in this life have lasting repercussions in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم أكفرتم بعد إيمانكم فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: And as for those whose faces will be white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, therein abiding eternally.
interpretation: This verse reflects the ultimate reward for the righteous and the believers on the Day of Judgment. The imagery of white faces symbolizes purity, acceptance, and the favor of Allah. It indicates that those who have led a life in accordance with divine guidance will experience His mercy and live eternally in paradise, emphasizing the importance of faith and good deeds in achieving salvation.
orig: وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون

translation: These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth. And Allah does not wish injustice for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the revelations, highlighting that they are genuine and meant to convey truth. It reassures the recipients that Allah's intentions are just, contrasting divine fairness with human injustice. The phrase 'Allah does not wish injustice for the worlds' asserts that Allah's guidance and commands are meant to establish justice and righteousness among all creation.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وما الله يريد ظلما للعالمين

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah belong the final destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah over all creation. It reminds believers that everything in existence, both heavenly and earthly, is under His dominion. The phrase 'to Allah belong the final destination' signifies that all matters will eventually return to Him for reckoning, highlighting accountability in the hereafter. It serves to instill a sense of humility and responsibility among individuals, urging them to acknowledge Allah's ultimate authority and to act righteously in their lives.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: You are the best nation produced [as an example] for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the elevated status and responsibility of the Muslim community as the 'best nation', signifying their role as moral exemplars. It highlights the importance of promoting virtue (enjoining what is right) and preventing vice (forbidding what is wrong) as fundamental characteristics of their identity. The mention of belief in Allah underscores the spiritual foundation that should guide their actions. Additionally, it addresses the People of the Scripture, suggesting that their belief would lead to greater benefit. However, the phrase about the majority being 'defiantly disobedient' serves as a critique of those who fail to uphold these values, underscoring a call to adhere to righteousness and faith.
orig: كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وتؤمنون بالله ولو آمن أهل الكتاب لكان خيرا لهم منهم المؤمنون وأكثرهم الفاسقون

translation: They will not harm you except for a little hurt; and if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the enemies of the believers may cause some minor harm or distress, but ultimately their power is limited and they will not prevail against the believers. Their attempts to fight will result in defeat and failure, highlighting the strength and protection that faith provides to those who believe. It reassures the faithful that as long as they remain steadfast, no true harm can come to them from those who oppose them.
orig: لن يضروكم إلا أذى وإن يقاتلوكم يولوكم الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: And humiliation was put upon them wherever they were overtaken, except for a rope from Allah and a rope from the people. And they returned with anger from Allah and struck upon them poverty. That was because they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and transgression against divine commands. It signifies that humiliation and poverty are the results of rejecting God's signs and committing grave injustices, such as the unjust killing of prophets. The 'rope from Allah and a rope from the people' suggests that there is a glimmer of hope and support for those who may seek it, but ultimately, it is the rejection of faith and righteousness that leads to a life of disgrace. It serves as a warning about the serious repercussions of defiance against divine guidance, illustrating the moral and spiritual decline that results from such actions.
orig: ضربت عليهم الذلة أين ما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس وباءوا بغضب من الله وضربت عليهم المسكنة ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون الأنبياء بغير حق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing firm. They recite the verses of Allah during the hours of the night and prostrate (to Him).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity within the People of the Scripture, highlighting that not all individuals share the same qualities or dedication. It points to a particular group among them who are committed to their faith, engaging in the recitation of Allah's verses and dedicating themselves to prayer and humility, especially during the night. This signifies the importance of sincere worship and spiritual discipline, illustrating that true faith is manifested through actions and devotion rather than mere affiliation.
orig: ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten to good deeds. Those are among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the essential characteristics of the righteous believers. It emphasizes that true faith is not merely a matter of belief in Allah and the Day of Judgment, but also involves active engagement in promoting goodness and virtue while preventing wrongdoing. The act of hastening towards good deeds signifies not just willingness but also a proactive approach to doing good in the community. This comprehensive understanding of faith illustrates that being pious entails social responsibility and moral integrity.
orig: يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين

translation: And whatever good they do, they will not be denied it; and Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of Allah's knowledge regarding the deeds of the righteous. It conveys a message of reassurance that any good actions performed by individuals will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. The verse underscores the importance of doing good and reinforces the belief that such acts hold value in the eyes of the Creator. It suggests that God's mercy and recognition of righteous behavior are all-encompassing, encouraging people to continue striving toward goodness without fear of it being overlooked.
orig: وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and children will not avail them against Allah at all. And they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of relying on material wealth and family ties in the face of divine judgment. It asserts that disbelievers will find no protection or advantage from their worldly assets or their offspring when facing the consequences of their disbelief. The phrase 'companions of the Fire' indicates a permanent state of punishment in the afterlife for those who reject faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability before God, highlighting that true value lies in faith and righteousness rather than in material success or social standing.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind with a freezing cold that strikes the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves, and destroys it. And Allah did not do wrong to them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of worldly possessions and efforts in the face of divine reckoning. It emphasizes that while individuals may accumulate wealth and engage in worldly pursuits, such endeavors are transient and vulnerable to destruction—much like a crop ruined by an unexpected cold wind. The phrase 'who have wronged themselves' points to the idea that misdeeds and poor choices lead to one's own detriment, suggesting that the hardships faced are a consequence of one's actions rather than a result of divine injustice. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of how one's actions align with moral and ethical principles.
orig: مثل ما ينفقون في هذه الحياة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر أصابت حرث قوم ظلموا أنفسهم فأهلكته وما ظلمهم الله ولكن أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than your own kind, for they will not fail to corrupt you. They wish you harm; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse serves as a caution to the believers regarding their associations and friendships, particularly with those who do not share their faith. It emphasizes the idea that such relationships can lead to corruption and harm, reflecting the deeper animosities that may exist beneath the surface. The mention of hidden animosities points to the treachery that can lurk in seemingly harmless interactions. The call to use reason and reflection when forming bonds highlights the importance of choosing companions wisely, considering their intentions and the potential effects on one’s faith and wellbeing.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا بطانة من دونكم لا يألونكم خبالا ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر قد بينا لكم الآيات إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: Here you are, you love them but they do not love you, and you believe in the entire Book. When they meet you, they say, 'We believe', but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips out of rage. Say, 'Die in your rage; indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicity of those who outwardly profess belief and friendship, yet harbor resentment and malice inwardly. It emphasizes the contrast between sincere faith and superficial alliances, illustrating a significant emotional disconnect. The act of biting one's fingertips symbolizes deep frustration and anger, suggesting that their discontent can't be concealed. Furthermore, the reassurance that Allah is aware of what lies within people's hearts serves as a reminder that true judgment comes from God, who sees beyond mere outward expressions to the true intentions of individuals.
orig: ها أنتم أولاء تحبونهم ولا يحبونكم وتؤمنون بالكتاب كله وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: If a good touch you, it distresses them; but if a misfortune strikes you, they rejoice at it. And if you remain patient and conscious of Allah, their cunning will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dynamics of the relationship between the faithful and their adversaries. It highlights the nature of envy and animosity that the enemies feel towards believers when they experience success or joy, while conversely emphasizing their delight at the misfortunes of the faithful. The call to remain patient (sabr) and pious (taqwa) serves as a reminder that one's steadfastness in faith and obedience to Allah provides protection against the plots and schemes of others. The concluding assurance that Allah is fully aware of all actions reaffirms that ultimate justice resides with Him, thereby encouraging believers to maintain their integrity and trust in divine wisdom despite external challenges.
orig: إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها وإن تصبروا وتتقوا لا يضركم كيدهم شيئا إن الله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And when you set out from your family to appoint the believers their positions for battle; and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of leadership and preparation in the context of battle. It highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in organizing and mobilizing the believers for the cause of Islam. The mention of Allah being 'Hearing and Knowing' serves as a reminder that He is aware of the intentions and efforts of individuals, thereby promoting the idea that actions should be taken for the right reasons, with devotion and sincerity to God.
orig: وإذ غدوت من أهلك تبوئ المؤمنين مقاعد للقتال والله سميع عليم

translation: When two parties among you were about to lose heart, but Allah was their protector. And upon Allah should the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and reliance on Allah in times of difficulty. It underscores that even when faced with adversity or the fear of failure, believers should trust in God's support and protection. The mention of two parties suggests the challenge of division and discouragement among believers, but the assurance of divine assistance reinforces the idea that unity and trust in Allah are crucial for overcoming challenges.
orig: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا والله وليهما وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And indeed, Allah granted you victory at Badr while you were weak. So fear Allah that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine assistance and victory granted by Allah despite the apparent weaknesses of believers. It serves as a reminder that true strength comes from faith and reliance on Allah. Furthermore, it encourages the faithful to be conscious of their relationship with Allah and to express gratitude for His support, as well as to maintain a sense of humility and righteousness in their actions.
orig: ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة فاتقوا الله لعلكم تشكرون

translation: When you said to the believers, 'Will it not suffice you that your Lord should send down to you three thousand angels?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the assurance and divine support that Allah provides to the believers in times of difficulty. It emphasizes the concept of reliance on Allah and His ability to assist the faithful in overcoming challenges. The mention of angels signifies a powerful, spiritual reinforcement that strengthens the hearts of the believers, encouraging them to maintain their faith and perseverance in the face of adversity. The rhetorical question underlines the expectation of believers to trust in Allah's promises and the effectiveness of divine intervention in their struggles.
orig: إذ تقول للمؤمنين ألن يكفيكم أن يمدكم ربكم بثلاثة آلاف من الملائكة منزلين

translation: Indeed, if you remain patient and conscious of Allah, and if they come at you (to attack) this way, your Lord will assist you with five thousand angels, marked (for battle).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience (sabr) and piety (taqwa) in the face of adversity. It reassures believers that if they uphold these virtues, they will receive divine support in times of conflict. The mention of angels signifies God’s direct intervention and assistance for those who remain steadfast, highlighting the belief in spiritual reinforcement during challenging times.
orig: بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين

translation: And Allah has not made it except as a glad tidings for you and so that your hearts may be assured by it. And victory comes only from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that divine revelations serve as a source of comfort and reassurance for believers, enabling them to maintain faith and hope. It emphasizes that ultimate success and victory are granted by Allah alone, who possesses supreme authority and wisdom. This reinforces the idea that human effort should be coupled with trust in God's plan, highlighting the importance of relying on divine support rather than solely on personal capabilities.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى لكم ولتطمئن قلوبكم به وما النصر إلا من عند الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Let him cut off a part of those who disbelieve or let him subdue them, so that they may turn back disappointed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate fate of those who oppose faith and righteousness. It suggests that either through divine intervention or moral consequence, those who deny the truth will face loss and humiliation. The concept of being 'cut off' indicates both a physical and a spiritual separation from the community of the believers, while 'turning back disappointed' suggests an inevitable realization of their misguided choices. It conveys the message that denial of faith has repercussions, reinforcing the importance of belief and the consequences of turning away from the truth.
orig: ليقطع طرفا من الذين كفروا أو يكبتهم فينقلبوا خائبين

translation: You have no control over the matter at all; either He will forgive them or punish them, for they are wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that ultimate authority and control lies with God alone. It underscores the futility of human desire for power over divine judgment. The options of forgiveness and punishment reflect God's mercy and justice. The mention of wrongdoers serves as a reminder of the consequences of one's actions, pointing to the moral responsibility individuals hold. It suggests that regardless of human intentions, the outcome is determined by God's will and wisdom.
orig: ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah over everything in existence, reinforcing the idea that all possessions and beings belong to Him. It highlights Allah's authority to forgive or punish based on His wisdom and choices. The mention of His attributes as 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' reflects the balance in His nature, reminding believers of His capacity to grant mercy and forgiveness, while also acknowledging the accountability of their actions.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, but fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prohibition of usury (riba), which is exploiting others through interest-based transactions. It suggests that believers should engage in just and fair economic practices and avoid practices that lead to societal harm and inequality. The mention of fearing Allah implies that spiritual and ethical considerations should guide financial dealings. The call to 'success' indicates that adherence to these principles not only promotes individual and communal welfare but also aligns with divine favor.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being aware of the consequences of disbelief and the eternal punishment that awaits those who reject faith. It serves as a warning to individuals, urging them to recognize the severity of their actions and the reality of divine justice. The mention of fear suggests a profound awareness of the repercussions of one's choices in the moral and spiritual realm, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to avoid actions that lead to such dire ramifications.
orig: واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger as a means to attain divine mercy. It suggests that following divine guidance and the teachings of the Prophet is essential for those seeking forgiveness and compassion. The phrase 'that you may receive mercy' indicates that obedience is not only a duty but also a pathway to spiritual blessings and a deeper relationship with the divine.
orig: وأطيعوا الله والرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency for believers to seek God's forgiveness and strive for the rewards of Paradise. It highlights the vastness of Paradise, indicating that it is not limited in size but encompasses the expanses of the heavens and the earth, signifying the greatness of what is offered. Additionally, the mention of 'the righteous' underscores the importance of piety and good conduct in attaining such divine rewards, portraying the moral responsibility of individuals to act justly and righteously.
orig: وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها السماوات والأرض أعدت للمتقين

translation: Those who spend in times of ease and hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people; and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of generosity, patience, and forgiveness. It illustrates that true piety is shown through one's actions in both favorable and adverse situations. Spending in 'seraa' (ease) represents acts of charity during good times, while spending in 'darraa' (hardship) signifies supporting others even when one is facing difficulties. Restraining anger is a call to control one's emotions, which is a significant aspect of personal discipline and moral character. Pardon signifies the importance of forgiveness and letting go of grievances, which fosters community harmony. The concluding phrase, 'Allah loves the doers of good,' reinforces that such virtues are cherished by God, encouraging believers to embody these qualities in their lives.
orig: الذين ينفقون في السراء والضراء والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين

translation: And those who, when they commit a disgraceful act or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins; and who can forgive sins except Allah? And they do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-awareness and the consciousness of God in instances where individuals fall into sin or commit wrongdoings. It emphasizes that true repentance involves acknowledgment of one's faults and turning back to God for forgiveness. The text stresses that only Allah has the authority to forgive sins, encouraging believers to approach Him sincerely when seeking redemption. Furthermore, it underlines that genuine remorse should be accompanied by a commitment to avoid repeating the sins, rather than a casualness towards one's actions.
orig: والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون

translation: Those are their reward: forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. And excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense reward awaiting those who strive in the path of righteousness. It highlights that their efforts will be met with divine forgiveness and eternal bliss in paradise, where the beauty of flowing rivers symbolizes abundance and serenity. The term 'abiding therein forever' underscores the permanence of their reward, contrasting with the transient nature of worldly life. Furthermore, the phrase 'excellent is the reward of the workers' serves as an encouragement for believers to persist in their good deeds, reinforcing the notion that true fulfillment comes from dedicating oneself to righteous actions.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم مغفرة من ربهم وجنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ونعم أجر العاملين

translation: Generations before you have passed away; so travel through the earth and see what was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of history and the consequences of denying the truth. It calls upon individuals to observe the outcomes of past nations that rejected divine guidance, serving as a reminder of the inevitable accountability that follows denial of faith. The directive to travel the earth underlines the value of personal experience and reflection on historical lessons, encouraging believers to strengthen their faith and avoid the pitfalls faced by those who came before them.
orig: قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: This is a declaration for the people and guidance and advice for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of divine revelation as a clear communication meant for all of humanity. It highlights that the message contained within is not limited to a select few but is intended for everyone, serving as guidance that leads individuals towards righteousness. Furthermore, it stresses the importance of being mindful and pious, indicating that the teachings provided act as reminders and moral lessons specifically beneficial to those who are conscious of their actions and strive to lead a life aligned with divine will.
orig: هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And do not weaken and do not grieve, while you are the uppermost, if you are indeed believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast and strong in their faith, even in the face of adversity and challenges. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining confidence and hope, reminding them that true believers hold a superior position because of their faith. The message reassures them that their faith elevates their status, and they should not succumb to despair or discouragement, as their belief equips them with strength and a sense of purpose.
orig: ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: If a blow touches you, a blow has also touched the people. And those days [of varying fortunes] We alternate among the people, and that Allah may make evident those who believe and may take to Himself from among you martyrs. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of shared human experience and the inevitability of trials in life. It emphasizes that both the believers and their opponents face challenges, signifying that hardship is a normal part of existence. The changing fortunes serve as a test to discern the true believers. Additionally, it suggests that those who face adversity with faith may attain a higher status, such as becoming martyrs in the sight of Allah. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah does not favor injustice, reinforcing the idea that righteousness is paramount in facing life's trials.
orig: إن يمسسكم قرح فقد مس القوم قرح مثله وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس وليعلم الله الذين آمنوا ويتخذ منكم شهداء والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And Allah will purge those who have believed and eliminate the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine justice, where Allah distinguishes between the believers and the disbelievers. The purification of the believers signifies a process of testing and strengthening their faith, while the elimination of the disbelievers represents a form of divine retribution. It underscores the idea that faith will be rewarded and disbelief will ultimately lead to loss, emphasizing the importance of sincerity in belief and the consequences of one's choices.
orig: وليمحص الله الذين آمنوا ويمحق الكافرين

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive for His cause and made evident those who are patient?
interpretation: This verse addresses the misconception that mere belief or identification as a believer is sufficient for entry into Paradise. It emphasizes that Allah will distinguish between those who sincerely strive in His path and those who merely claim faith. The act of striving (jihad) and the virtue of patience (sabr) are essential qualities that reflect true commitment and resilience in the face of trials. Thus, the verse reminds believers that enduring tests and showing dedication are crucial elements in fulfilling their spiritual obligations and attaining divine rewards.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ويعلم الصابرين

translation: And indeed, you used to wish for death before you encountered it, and now you have seen it while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to desire what seems noble or desirable from a distance, yet when faced with the reality of death, one realizes its true weight and seriousness. It serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of recognizing the inevitable reality of death. This can evoke a sense of gratitude for life and an imperative to live meaningfully and righteously, as the wish for death may come from an escape from worldly struggles, but facing it confronts one with the ultimate truth of existence.
orig: ولقد كنتم تمنون الموت من قبل أن تلقوه فقد رأيتموه وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Muhammad is but a messenger; other messengers have passed on before him. If he should die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental truth that prophets are merely human messengers of Allah and that their existence or absence should not affect the faith of believers. The test of faith is not based on the life or death of a messenger but rather on the enduring commitment to the teachings they brought.
