translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you kings and brought you that which He had not brought anyone among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessings bestowed upon the Children of Israel by Allah. Moses is urging his people to recognize and appreciate the past gifts they have received, which include the appointment of prophets to guide them, the elevation to kingship, and the unique favors that set them apart from other communities. It serves as a reminder of their responsibilities to uphold the values and directives imparted by these prophets, and to be grateful for their privileged status in the divine plan. The emphasis on remembrance is a call to awareness and humility, urging them to reflect on how they should respond to such blessings with obedience and gratitude.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you, and do not turn back on your heels, for then you will become losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of obeying divine commands and the consequences of turning away from them. It emphasizes the importance of faith and commitment, urging the believers to enter the land that has been promised to them, symbolizing God's favor and blessings. The warning against retreating suggests that hesitation or doubt can lead to failure and loss, encouraging steadfastness in the face of challenges. It serves as a reminder that faith requires action and that the faithful should pursue their rightful path without fear or hesitation.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed there are people in it who are powerful, and indeed we will not enter it until they leave it. If they leave, then we will enter.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and reluctance of the Children of Israel in the face of adversity. Their response to Moses highlights their lack of faith and trust in God's promise of victory despite being led by a prophet. It showcases a human tendency to hold back in the presence of perceived threats, revealing the struggle between faith and fear. Their insistence on waiting for the enemies to leave before entering signifies an avoidance of confrontation, and it also illustrates a deeper theme of reliance on divine support in facing challenges.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: Two men from those who feared [God] said, 'Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be dominant. And upon Allah rely if you should be believers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and reliance on God in facing challenges and adversity. The two men, representing courage rooted in faith, encourage their people to act confidently, as they believe that entrance into the land will lead to victory. The call to trust in God highlights a key principle in Islam: true strength and success come from a deep belief in and dependence on the Divine. It serves as a reminder that faith should precede action, and when one is genuinely committed to their beliefs, they can overcome obstacles, assured of divine support.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed we will not enter it, so long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and reluctance of the Israelites to confront their enemies and fulfill God's command. Their refusal to enter the land indicates a lack of faith and trust in God's support. It highlights the broader theme of struggle against oppression, the importance of collective responsibility, and the consequences of disobedience to divine guidance. The act of sitting still while Moses is urged to fight shows a divide between leadership and the people, emphasizing the need for courage in the face of adversity.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: He said, 'O my Lord, indeed I do not possess [power over] anything except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of despair and vulnerability. The speaker acknowledges their limited power and influence, emphasizing the bonds of familial loyalty and the struggle against oppression. It highlights the deep yearning for justice and separation from those who are corrupt and disobedient to divine law. This plea for division symbolizes not just a physical separation, but also a moral and spiritual distinction from those engaged in wrongdoing, underscoring the importance of righteousness and faith in the face of adversity.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: He said, 'Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land. So do not grieve over the disobedient people.'
interpretation: This verse conveys the consequence of the people's disobedience to God's commands, specifically in the context of the Israelites after they refused to enter the Holy Land. Their punishment of wandering for forty years serves as a reminder of the repercussions of turning away from divine guidance. The phrase 'do not grieve over the disobedient people' reflects God's reassurance to His Prophet, emphasizing that such consequences are part of divine justice. It illustrates the importance of faithfulness and obedience to God's will, suggesting that those who rebel against His guidance will face hardships while believers remain steadfast in their commitment.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, when they both offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them, but it was not accepted from the other. He said, 'I will surely kill you.' The other replied, 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine acceptance and righteousness. The narrative of Adam's sons serves as a moral lesson about intentions and the criteria through which one's deeds are valued by God. It emphasizes that rituals, such as sacrifices, are not sufficient without the sincerity and piety of the one offering them. The statement 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous' underscores the importance of personal integrity, highlighting that even acts of worship need to emerge from a state of true faith and moral uprightness to be considered valid and accepted by Allah.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights a profound moral stance, emphasizing the principle of non-violence even in the face of aggression. The speaker demonstrates a commitment to righteousness and a fear of God, suggesting that the sanctity of life is paramount. It indicates that true strength lies not in taking life, but in choosing restraint and upholding divine values, reflecting a deep ethical conviction rooted in faith.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, so you will be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the grave consequences of wrongdoing, particularly in the context of responsibility for one's actions. It emphasizes the idea that each individual must bear their own sins, and the desire for someone else to carry one's sins reflects a deep sense of accountability and the weight of guilt. The reference to being among the companions of the Fire symbolizes the ultimate punishment for those who engage in injustice and lead others astray. It serves as a powerful warning that moral choices have eternal implications and can lead to an unbearable fate for the unjust.
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: So his soul facilitated for him the killing of his brother, and he killed him; thus he became among the losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the destructive power of envy and anger, as it describes a grave sin where one individual succumbs to the temptation to harm his own sibling. The act of murder is not just a physical loss but also a moral and spiritual downfall, marking the murderer as one of the 'losers.' It serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of allowing negative emotions to dictate one's actions, ultimately leading to regret and loss of righteousness.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: So Allah sent a raven searching in the ground to show him how to cover the shame of his brother. He said, 'Oh woe to me! Am I not able to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother?' And he became of the regretful.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound moment of realization and regret. It illustrates the lesson of humility and the importance of responsibility towards others. The raven symbolizes guidance and the natural instinct to protect one's kin. The character's inability to act as the raven did highlights the weight of guilt and the sorrow of missed opportunities to act with compassion. Ultimately, it serves as a reminder of the potential for remorse and the need for self-reflection on one's actions in relation to others.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: For that reason, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, even after that, throughout the land were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of human life and the severe consequences of taking a life unjustly. It emphasizes that killing an innocent person is a crime against all of humanity, reflecting a collective responsibility towards preserving life. Conversely, saving a life is portrayed as a profound act of value that benefits all. The mention of messengers bringing clear signs implies that divine guidance was provided, yet many chose to ignore it, highlighting human tendencies toward transgression and moral decay despite receiving divine warnings.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: The only reward for those who fight against Allah and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides, or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the severe consequences for those who actively oppose and create discord against the divine message of Islam and engage in acts of corruption. It signifies the gravity of such actions in the eyes of Allah, emphasizing that justice must be served for those who threaten the moral fabric of society. The punishments described reflect both a physical and social dimension of justice, where not only are the perpetrators dealt with harshly for their crimes, but they also face disgrace and isolation. Moreover, it highlights the notion that worldly punishment is a precursor to the severe spiritual ramifications that await in the Hereafter for such individuals, underscoring the principle of accountability and divine justice.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Except for those who repent before you overpower them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy of Allah towards those who sincerely repent for their wrongdoings before facing the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes the importance of repentance and the boundless forgiveness that Allah offers to His servants who turn back to Him with a genuine heart. The mention of 'overpowering' suggests a time constraint; it underscores the need for immediate repentance when one is still in a position to do so, indicating that it is never too late to seek forgiveness as long as one is sincere.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of nearness to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of piety and striving for closeness to Allah through various means, including acts of worship and righteous deeds. It highlights that true success in this life and the hereafter comes from a combination of faith, taking proactive steps towards Allah, and engaging in struggle or effort for His sake. The call to 'fear Allah' serves as a reminder of the importance of consciousness of God in all actions, while 'striving' indicates that faith must be accompanied by action.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and its equivalent with it to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of trying to evade divine punishment through worldly riches or offerings. It emphasizes that no material possessions or wealth can save the disbelievers from the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment. Their attempts to bargain with God using their earthly possessions will be in vain, as repentance and belief are the true requirements for salvation, not wealth. The verse serves as a stern warning about the importance of faith and adherence to divine guidance, as well as the severe repercussions awaiting those who reject it.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They want to escape from the Fire, but they will never escape from it, and theirs is a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse reflects the despair of those who are in Hell, highlighting their wish to escape the torment they face. However, the text emphasizes their inability to do so, illustrating the permanence of their punishment. This serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of one's actions in this world, suggesting that there is no refuge from divine justice once the final judgment has been rendered. It imparts the lesson that repentance and righteousness are vital in this life to avoid such dire outcomes.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: As for the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they earned as a deterrent from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of justice and retribution within Islamic law regarding theft. It emphasizes that the punishment is not only a response to the crime but also serves as a deterrent for society, reflecting God's authority and wisdom in establishing laws that maintain order and discourage wrongdoing. The mention of both male and female thieves underscores the principle of equality before the law, holding all accountable for their actions, regardless of gender.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: So whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, then indeed, Allah will turn to him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the compassionate nature of Allah, highlighting that repentance and reform are not only encouraged but also sincerely welcomed. It assures that even after committing wrongdoings, individuals have the opportunity to return to righteousness. The use of 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' underscores Allah's readiness to forgive those who genuinely seek to amend their ways, reflecting the transformative power of sincere repentance in establishing a connection with the Divine.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is All-Powerful over everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, highlighting His authority over life and death, punishment and forgiveness. It serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and omniscience, reinforcing the idea that human judgment is limited, while divine judgment is all-encompassing and just. The reference to God's ability to forgive and punish also reflects the themes of mercy and justice, indicating that ultimately, accountability lies with Him alone.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger, let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you, from among those who say, 'We have believed' with their mouths but their hearts have not believed. And of the Jews are some who listen eagerly to falsehood and listen to another people who have not come to you. They distort words from their proper places, saying, 'If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware.' And whoever Allah intends to put him to trial - you will never possess for him against Allah anything. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah does not intend to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and they will have in the Hereafter a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) directly, reassuring him not to be distressed by the hypocrisy of some individuals who outwardly profess faith while their hearts harbor disbelief. It highlights the deceptive nature of those who are insincere and actively mislead others, including their propensity to twist words for their own agenda. The verse also underscores Allah's sovereignty in guiding and purifying hearts, indicating that for those who reject faith, there is a dual consequence: humiliation in this life and severe punishment in the hereafter. This serves as a reminder of the importance of sincere belief and the dangers of hypocrisy and deceit.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: They are listeners to falsehood, eaters of unlawful gain. So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and integrity in dealing with others, particularly those who may engage in deceitful behavior or seek to exploit unlawful gains. It highlights that while one may choose to disengage from individuals who are known to be dishonest, it is crucial to maintain a standard of fairness and equity when adjudicating matters that arise. Additionally, the verse reassures that turning away from unjust individuals does not diminish one's own integrity or standing in the sight of Allah, reinforcing that He values just behavior.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: And how [can they judge you] when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away, and those are not the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who possess divine guidance in the form of the Torah yet choose to disregard its teachings. It underscores the importance of following God's commandments and suggests that true belief is demonstrated through adherence to religious law. The verse critiques those who claim to believe while failing to act according to the principles that should govern their actions, emphasizing that mere acknowledgment of faith is insufficient without obedience to God's directives.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and the scholars, by that which they were entrusted of the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear people, but fear Me. And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance as encapsulated in the Torah, highlighting it as a source of light and insight for those who are righteous. It underscores the responsibility of religious authorities and leaders to uphold the teachings of the scripture faithfully and dispel fears of human judgment in favor of divine command. Additionally, it warns against the temptation to barter away God's revelations for worldly gains, indicating that such actions lead one away from faith and truth. The directive to judge by what Allah has revealed is a fundamental principle that underscores the integrity and sincerity required in the governance of spiritual and moral matters.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون

translation: And We ordained for them therein a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is a legal retribution. But whoever gives up [his right as charity] - it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of equal retribution, known as 'qisas,' highlighting the importance of justice and balance in human interactions. It indicates that punishment should be proportional to the crime committed, thereby promoting a sense of fairness and responsibility in society. The mention of forgiving or giving up one's retribution is seen as an act of moral and spiritual elevation, suggesting that such choices can serve as atonement. Furthermore, the verse warns against those who fail to adjudicate according to divine guidance, labeling them as wrongdoers, which underscores the significance of adhering to divine laws in maintaining societal order and morality.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We followed in their footsteps with Jesus, son of Mary, confirming that which was before him of the Torah. And We gave him the Gospel, containing guidance and light, and confirming that which was before it of the Torah and as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse signifies the continuity of divine revelation through successive prophets, underscoring the role of Jesus as a fulfillment and confirmation of previous scriptures, particularly the Torah. It highlights the importance of the Gospel as a source of light and guidance for humanity, particularly for those who are mindful of their duties to God. The repetition of the theme of confirmation emphasizes the unity of God's message throughout history and the shared foundation of faith across different revelations.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance as revealed in the scriptures. It underscores that authority and judgment should derive from the principles laid out by Allah, suggesting accountability for those who possess knowledge of the Divine scriptures. Failure to do so classifies individuals as transgressors, indicating a serious moral and spiritual failure. It reflects a broader principle in Islam regarding the necessity for all communities to govern their lives according to God's revelations, suggesting a unified approach to moral and ethical standards across differing faiths.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires away from what has come to you of the truth. For each of you We have appointed a law and a method. If Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but He intended to test you in what He has given you. So race to good deeds. To Allah is your return all together, and He will inform you concerning that in which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of divine revelation and the authority of the Qur'an as a decisive guide for judgment among people. It highlights the need for adherence to God's commandments rather than personal inclinations or desires, thereby establishing a moral and ethical foundation for governance and social interaction. The mention of different laws and paths for various communities serves as a reminder of divine wisdom in human diversity, intended to foster spiritual growth through trials and the pursuit of righteousness. The ultimate accountability to Allah serves as a call for unity in striving towards good deeds, reinforcing the idea that while humanity may differ, the core objective remains the same: to seek God's pleasure and guidance.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they entice you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away, then know that Allah intends to afflict them with some of their sins; and indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding divine commandments above human desires. The directive to judge by what Allah has revealed highlights the primacy of divine guidance in legal and ethical matters. It warns against being swayed by the whims of others, suggesting that societal pressures can lead one to stray from righteous paths. The mention of Allah's intention to cause afflictions as a consequence of turning away serves as a reminder of accountability, indicating that deviation from God's laws can result in punishment. Furthermore, it acknowledges the prevalence of disobedience among humanity, implying a challenging environment where one must remain steadfast in faith and principles.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: Do they seek the judgment of [the days of] ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain [in faith]?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of divine judgment over human or traditional judgments of ignorance. It critiques those who prefer the flawed and unjust systems of the past when the ultimate wisdom and fairness is found in Allah's rulings. It serves as a reminder for believers to trust in God's guidance and authority, particularly when faced with moral or ethical dilemmas, asserting that true certainty and faith come from adhering to divine laws rather than to fallible human traditions.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are, in fact, allies of one another. And whoever of you takes them as allies - then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a distinct identity and community among believers, highlighting the potential pitfalls of forming alliances with those who do not share the same faith. It suggests that such alliances can undermine the unity and values of the Muslim community and may lead to moral and spiritual dilution. The warning about being counted among those whom one allies with underscores the seriousness of this matter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, 'We fear a misfortune might strike us.' Perhaps Allah will bring about a victory or an event from Himself, and then they will be struck with regret for what they have concealed within themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of individuals who harbor doubts and malice in their hearts. Their fear of misfortune leads them to quickly side with those they would otherwise oppose, indicating a lack of conviction. It suggests that true believers should remain steadfast in their faith, regardless of external pressures or fears. The verse also warns that those who act out of insincerity will ultimately regret their choices when the truth prevails and the consequences of their hidden intentions become apparent.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believed will say, 'Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that indeed they were with you?' Their deeds have become invalid, and they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the disillusionment of the believers upon realizing that some individuals, who had confidently claimed allegiance and faith, were ultimately revealed to be insincere. The strong oaths they took attest to their prior deception. Their actions, which seemed righteous, are rendered void as a consequence of their deceit, emphasizing a key moral lesson: genuine faith must be accompanied by integrity and truthfulness. This serves as a warning against hypocrisy and reinforces the idea that mere claims of belief without corresponding righteous deeds will not suffice in the sight of Allah. The notion of being 'losers' underscores the dire consequences of failing to uphold true faith and sincerity in one's actions.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [for] a people He will love and who will love Him, [they will be] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers. They strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a blameworthy. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of abandoning it. It conveys a message of reassurance that even if some individuals turn away from their beliefs, Allah will replace them with others who are devoted and wiling to sacrifice for their faith. The qualities of these new believers highlight a balance between humility towards fellow believers and strength against those who oppose their faith. Additionally, it underscores Allah's sovereignty in choosing who receives His guidance and blessings, reinforcing the idea that divine favor is a matter of His will and knowledge. This serves as both a warning to those who may consider leaving their faith and encouragement to remain steadfast, as Allah is always aware of the true intentions of the heart.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Your only protector is Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give zakah while they bow [in worship].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine and communal support in Islam. It underscores that true guardianship comes from God, His Messenger, and the believers who are consistent in their faith and practices, specifically mentioning prayer and zakah (charity) as critical aspects of that faith. The act of giving zakah while in a state of humility (bowing) symbolizes the believers' devotion and the importance of supporting one another in righteousness. It reinforces the community aspect of faith, suggesting that genuine friendship and support are found within the community of believers who actively engage in worship and charitable acts.
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And whoever allies with Allah and His Messenger and those who believe - indeed, the party of Allah will be the predominant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and allegiance to Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers. It indicates that true strength and victory come from being part of the collective 'party of Allah,' which signifies those who are steadfast in their faith and support one another in righteousness. The message suggests that, despite worldly challenges, those who unite in their faith and support can find triumph through divine assistance, highlighting a profound sense of communal identity and faith-driven resilience.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and play from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers as allies. And fear Allah, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the sanctity of one's faith and warns against forming alliances with those who mock or trivialize religious beliefs. It highlights the danger of associating with individuals or groups that do not respect the tenets of the faith and encourages believers to hold steadfastly to their convictions. The call to 'fear Allah' serves as a reminder that true belief entails an awareness of divine oversight and accountability, urging believers to make conscious choices that align with their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disdain and lack of seriousness that some people show towards the act of prayer, viewing it merely as an occasion for entertainment rather than a significant spiritual practice. It underscores the importance of understanding the purpose and gravity of religious duties. The verse also suggests that such frivolity stems from a deeper issue of a lack of comprehension or reflection on spiritual matters, indicating a broader spiritual blindness or ignorance within certain individuals or communities.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do you resent us for no reason other than that we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed previously? And most of you are defiantly disobedient.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the misunderstanding and resentment that often exists between different faith communities. It emphasizes that the core reason for conflict is not often legitimate grievances or actions but rather the differences in belief and faith. Furthermore, it points to a moral challenge where the verse calls out the hypocrisy of those who, despite claiming to follow God's revelations, act contrary to the principles of faith and righteousness. It serves as a reminder that faith should be a unifying force rather than a cause for division, and it critiques those who abandon righteous conduct despite their claimed beliefs.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say, 'Shall I inform you of a worse reward from Allah than that? It is for whom Allah has cursed and whom He has been angry with and made of them apes and pigs, and who worshiped Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the sound way.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of turning away from divine guidance and engaging in unrighteous behavior. It highlights that those who have incurred God's anger and curse, symbolized by their transformation into apes and pigs, represent the ultimate failure in spiritual and moral alignment. Furthermore, it points out that idol worship and excessive subjugation to false deities lead individuals further away from the right path, indicating that moral and spiritual misguidance leads to a degradation of one's station in the eyes of God. Ultimately, this serves as a warning against hypocrisy and the folly of forsaking God’s commandments for transient worldly gains.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they come to you, they say, 'We believe'; but they have entered with disbelief, and they have gone out with it. And Allah knows best what they were concealing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly profess faith while internally holding onto disbelief. It emphasizes the idea that true belief is not merely verbal affirmation but must correspond with genuine inner conviction. The knowledge of Allah encompasses all intentions and secrets, indicating that human claims of faith can be deceptive, and only Allah truly knows the hearts of individuals. This serves as a reminder to be sincere in one's faith and to be aware of the potential duplicity in oneself and others.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them hastening towards sin and aggression and devouring unlawfully. Evil is what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who hasten towards sinful actions, showing a willful inclination towards wrongdoing. The mention of 'sin and aggression' indicates both personal and social transgressions, while 'devouring unlawfully' highlights corruption and moral decay. The overall message reflects a condemnation of such behaviors, urging believers to recognize the gravity of these actions and their consequences.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: If it were not for the rabbis and the scholars who forbid them from speaking evil and consuming unlawful things, how evil would they be doing!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of religious leaders to guide their communities away from wrongdoing. It indicates that the presence of righteous scholars is crucial in maintaining ethical standards and preventing moral decay. The implication is that when leaders fail to uphold their duties or remain silent in the face of corruption, they are complicit in the negative actions of their followers. The verse also underscores the gravity of sin and the consumption of unlawful gains, highlighting that these actions can lead to severe consequences for society as a whole.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: The Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained.' Their hands are chained, and they are cursed for what they say. Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills. And indeed, We will increase for many of them what was revealed to you from your Lord, as transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindle the fire of war, Allah extinguishes it; and they strive to cause corruption on earth, and Allah does not like the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse addresses the severe misconceptions held by certain groups regarding God's power and attributes. The claim that 'the hand of Allah is chained' symbolizes an accusation of weakness or limitation, which is vehemently rejected. Instead, it emphasizes that God’s generosity and capability are boundless, signifying that He can give and take as He pleases. Furthermore, the verse points to the consequences of disbelief, revealing that such attitudes lead to increased animosity and strife among people, as illustrated by the cycle of igniting conflict that is ultimately extinguished by divine intervention. This underscores the futility of the efforts of those who sow discord and corruption, as God's will ultimately prevails, portraying a clear dichotomy between transgression and the divine order.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if the People of the Scripture had believed and been conscious of Allah, We would have erased from them their misdeeds and admitted them to gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of belief and piety among the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians). It indicates that true faith in God and righteous conduct can lead to redemption and rewards in the afterlife. The promise of erasing misdeeds reflects God's mercy, suggesting that repentance and faith can transform a person's spiritual state and lead them to divine blessings, symbolized by 'gardens of pleasure.' It underscores the idea that salvation is accessible to all who sincerely seek it, regardless of their past actions, provided they turn to God with genuine faith and consciousness.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if only they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what had been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed [good things] from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them are a moderate community, but many of them - evil is that which they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine revelations and guidelines provided in the Torah and the Gospel. It suggests that doing so would lead to prosperity and abundance, reflecting a moral and spiritual alignment with God's will. The mention of a 'moderate community' indicates that while some maintain a balanced and righteous approach, many stray into wrongdoing, highlighting the struggle between faithfulness and moral failure in communities. This calls for personal and collective accountability and encourages believers to reflect on their actions in relation to divine teachings.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger! Notify [the people] of that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not do [this], then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense responsibility placed upon the Messenger to convey the divine message without omission. It highlights the seriousness of the role of a prophet and the consequences of failing to deliver the message, as it implies that omission would mean failing in the divine duty. Additionally, it reassures the Messenger of God's protection against the harm or opposition of people, indicating that divine support is guaranteed against disbelief and rejection. This serves as a reminder that true guidance is ultimately in God's hands, and those who deny the truth will not find their way.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not on anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And indeed, many of them wish to lead you astray. But do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, specifically emphasizing that true guidance and faith cannot be claimed without adherence to their own scriptures—the Torah and the Gospel—as well as the revelations sent to Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that genuine belief requires both recognition and practice of these divine instructions. Furthermore, it highlights the challenges faced by believers, as many among the People of the Book might harbor resentment or disbelief against the revelations to Muhammad, thereby encouraging Muslims not to be disheartened by such opposition. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following divine guidance as the basis for faith and action.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews or Sabeans or Christians - those who have believed in Allah and the Last Day and done righteous deeds - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inclusivity of faith and righteousness in the sight of God. It suggests that true belief in God and the Last Day, accompanied by good deeds, transcends specific religious identities. The verse assures that all who sincerely strive for righteousness, regardless of their religious background (be it Judaism, Sabeanism, or Christianity), will find comfort and security from fear and sorrow. It highlights the core values of faith, morality, and accountability, suggesting that God's mercy is vast and encompasses all who earnestly seek Him and uphold righteous actions.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Indeed, We took the covenant from the Children of Israel, and We sent them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group of them denied, and a group killed.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the frequent rebellion and ingratitude of the Children of Israel towards the divine messages sent to them. Despite receiving multiple prophets, they often rejected their teachings if they contradicted their desires or societal norms. This reflects a broader theme of human resistance to divine guidance when it challenges personal or collective interests. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of ignoring truth and the importance of adhering to the divine will, highlighting the cyclical nature of acceptance and rejection faced by prophets.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: And they thought that there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned toward them, but many of them became blind and deaf again. And Allah is All-Seer of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of people becoming complacent and neglecting the signs of a trial or test from Allah. Their initial blindness and deafness symbolize a refusal to see the truth and hear His message. When they are given another chance through divine mercy, many still turn away, illustrating the persistent obstinacy of the human heart. The mention of Allah’s complete awareness of their actions serves as a reminder that nothing escapes His sight, emphasizing the need for accountability and self-reflection.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Those who disbelieve have said, 'Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' And the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the central tenet of monotheism in Islam, rejecting any notion of divinity attributed to Jesus Christ, the son of Mary. It stresses the importance of worshiping only Allah as the singular deity. The severe warning against associating partners with Allah highlights the grave consequence of disbelief, which is exclusion from paradise and a place in hellfire. The message is a call to the Children of Israel to recognize and adhere to the worship of Allah alone, reinforcing the idea that divine assistance is absent for those who commit injustices against this fundamental principle.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Indeed, they have disbelieved who say, 'God is the third of three.' And there is no deity except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely touch the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of polytheism and the belief in the Trinity, emphasizing the oneness of God. It asserts that attributing partners to God is a grave error and reflects a significant deviation from monotheism. The verse warns that if those who hold such beliefs do not cease, they will face severe consequences in the hereafter, underscoring the seriousness of rejecting the fundamental tenet of Islamic faith, which is the absolute oneness of God.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: Why do they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah. It emphasizes that regardless of the sins committed, Allah's mercy is vast and His willingness to forgive is boundless. The rhetorical question encourages individuals to reflect on their actions and turn back to Allah, who is always ready to accept sincere repentance. It serves as a reminder that compassion and mercy are fundamental attributes of Allah, motivating believers to seek His pardon and strive for righteousness.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was but a messenger; other messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a woman of truth. They both used to eat food. See how We make the signs clear to them; then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of Jesus, affirming that he was a messenger and not divine, as is sometimes claimed. It highlights the reality of his lineage and his mother's virtue. The reference to eating food illustrates the human nature of both Jesus and Mary, emphasizing that they had practical needs just like any other human beings. The verse also points to a broader message about recognizing the signs of truth and the delusions that can lead one away from the true understanding of God's messengers. It calls for reflection on how people often misinterpret or reject clear signs due to their preconceived notions or biases.
orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, "Do you worship besides Allah that which does not possess for you any harm or benefit?" And Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshiping entities or idols that have no power to affect one's life positively or negatively. It highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah, who is all-hearing and all-knowing. The verse calls for reflection on the nature of the beings being worshiped, urging believers to recognize that only Allah holds true power and authority over all matters.
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and have misled many and have strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse serves as a caution against extremism in faith, urging the People of the Scripture to adhere to the core truths of their religion without distorting or exaggerating their beliefs. It also warns against the dangers of following misguided groups, highlighting how such paths can lead to misdirection and confusion. The importance of discernment and the need to remain steadfast on the right path is emphasized, suggesting that true faith should be grounded in righteousness and not swayed by erroneous inclinations.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. That was for their disobedience and their transgression.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and disobedience among the Children of Israel, illustrating how their actions led to their curses by prominent prophets like David and Jesus. It serves as a warning against rebellion and highlights the divine disapproval of those who turn away from faith, seeking to reinforce the importance of obedience to God's commands. The mention of such revered figures underscores the gravity of the message and the significance of maintaining faith and righteousness.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They did not prohibit one another from wrongdoing that they committed. How wretched was what they did!
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral failing of a community that neglects the responsibility of advising and preventing each other from engaging in sinful behavior. It underscores the importance of communal accountability and the consequences of inaction in the face of wrongdoing. The phrase 'how wretched was what they did' serves as a condemnation of their behavior, indicating that their lack of mutual support in upholding righteousness leads to collective corruption and moral decay.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies. Evil is what they have sent forth for themselves; with which Allah has become angry with them, and they will abide in torment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave consequences of alliances with those who reject faith. It underscores the idea that turning one's back on fellow believers and forming relationships with disbelievers is not only a betrayal but also a serious spiritual misstep. Such actions provoke Allah's anger, leading to eternal consequences in the hereafter. The notion of 'evil sent forth' implies that one's choices have direct repercussions on their spiritual standing, illustrating the importance of loyalty to one's faith and community.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere faith in Allah and the Prophet Muhammad and the teachings brought forth in the divine revelation. It suggests that true belief should guide one's alliances and relationships. The verse points out that those who are hypocritical in their faith, who claim to believe yet take the enemies of God as allies, are acting contrary to what their faith should compel them to do. The mention of 'many of them are transgressors' highlights a common state among people who, despite the clarity of belief, choose paths of disobedience and betrayal.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers are the Jews and those who associate others with Allah. And you will find the closest of them in affection to the believers are those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the complex relationships between different groups and the nature of animosity and affection within them. It points out that the Jews and polytheists are depicted as the most antagonistic towards the believers, which may reflect historical tensions and conflicts. Conversely, it identifies Christians as those who are closest in affection, explaining this by noting their humility and spiritual leadership. The mention of priests and monks signifies the presence of genuine faith and devotion among some Christians, suggesting that true kindness and affinity are found in individuals who practice humility and religious piety, regardless of their group identity.
orig: لتجدن أشد الناس عداوة للذين آمنوا اليهود والذين أشركوا ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound emotional response that the truth can evoke in sincere believers. The imagery of weeping eyes suggests a deep understanding and acceptance of the revealed message. Their plea to be counted among the witnesses indicates a desire not only for belief but also for acknowledgment in the community of those who testify to the truth. This reflects the importance of both belief and action in the context of faith, emphasizing a collective recognition of God's message and the humility that comes with true faith.
orig: وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق يقولون ربنا آمنا فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, while we hope that our Lord will admit us alongside the righteous people?
interpretation: This verse expresses a deep yearning for faith and righteousness. It highlights the natural inclination of a believer to trust in Allah and His revelations, especially when they are presented with clear truths. The verse also emphasizes the desire for belonging to a group of the righteous, reflecting the importance of community and acceptance in spiritual matters. It invites reflection on the reasons for faith and the hope for divine mercy, reinforcing the belief that one’s faith can lead to a just and honorable standing with God.
orig: وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله وما جاءنا من الحق ونطمع أن يدخلنا ربنا مع القوم الصالحين

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. And that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine reward for those who speak righteousness and act benevolently. It highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah towards those who strive to do good deeds, promising them everlasting paradise and fulfillment. The imagery of rivers flowing beneath the gardens symbolizes abundance and eternal bliss, reinforcing the idea that good actions lead to eternal rewards. This serves as a motivation for believers to engage in virtuous acts and maintain a steadfast commitment to righteousness.
orig: فأثابهم الله بما قالوا جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: And those who disbelieved and rejected Our signs, they are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting faith and denying the signs of God. It serves as a solemn reminder that disbelief leads to spiritual ruin and suffering in the afterlife. The term 'companions of Hellfire' signifies not just punishment, but an eternal state of being with those who similarly chose to reject divine guidance. It highlights the seriousness of one's choices in this life, urging believers to reflect on the importance of faith and obedience to God's revelations.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the guidelines set by Allah regarding what is permissible and enjoyable in life. It serves as a reminder that believers should not impose unnecessary restrictions on themselves or others concerning the blessings that are lawful. Additionally, it warns against exceeding limits, as such actions are disapproved by Allah. This reflects the balance of enjoying the bounties of creation while staying within the boundaries of divine law.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you that is lawful and good, and fear Allah in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of consuming only what is halal (lawful) and tayyib (good) as a fundamental aspect of Islamic life. It encourages believers to maintain a pious consciousness of Allah while engaging in the everyday act of eating, reminding them that their sustenance should align with divine guidance. The call to 'fear Allah' suggests that ethical and moral consideration should govern not just dietary choices, but all aspects of life, reinforcing the idea that true faith manifests in both belief and action.
orig: وكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: God will not hold you accountable for your meaningless oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. The expiation for that is to feed ten poor people with the average of what you feed your families, or to clothe them, or to free a slave. But whoever cannot find the means must fast for three days. This is the expiation for your oaths when you swear, and be mindful of your oaths. Thus God makes clear His verses to you so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between trivial and serious oaths. It emphasizes that while God does not impose penalties for thoughtless or casual oaths, there is serious accountability for oaths made with intent. The prescribed expiation methods indicate a compassionate framework that allows for flexibility, stressing the importance of social responsibility by encouraging the act of feeding or clothing the needy. This not only serves as a means of atonement but also underlines the value of kindness and community support. The call to understand and cherish God’s signs suggests that proper awareness of divine guidance is essential for gratitude and moral responsibility.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما عقدتم الأيمان فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prohibition of certain harmful practices, including intoxicants and gambling, which are described as 'defilement' and 'the work of Satan.' It warns the believers to avoid these actions as they lead to moral decay and spiritual harm. The call to abstain is linked to the promise of success, suggesting that true achievement and prosperity come from steering clear of vices that can corrupt one's character and societal order. It conveys a broader message about the importance of maintaining purity in both personal conduct and community life, highlighting the need for self-discipline in the pursuit of righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the destructive influence of intoxicants and gambling, highlighting how they sow discord and hatred among people. It indicates that such vices distract individuals from their spiritual obligations, particularly the remembrance of Allah and prayer. The rhetorical question at the end serves as a call to reflection, urging believers to reconsider their engagement with these harmful practices and to refrain from them to maintain their spiritual integrity and community harmony.
orig: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهل أنتم منتهون

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. If you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (Prophet Muhammad). The command to 'obey' suggests a strong obligation on the part of the believers to follow divine guidance and the teachings of the Prophet. The warning to 'beware' indicates the seriousness of turning away from this guidance, highlighting that neglecting these commands could lead to dire consequences. Lastly, it reinforces that the Prophet's role is to convey clear messages from Allah, encouraging individuals to take these messages seriously rather than disregarding them.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا فإن توليتم فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten, if they have feared Allah and believed and done righteous deeds, and then feared Allah and believed, and then feared Allah and done good. And Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith and righteous deeds exempt believers from shame regarding their permissible actions, as long as they maintain their piety and commitment to goodness. It highlights the importance of a continuous cycle of faith and good deeds while expressing Allah's love for those who excel in virtuous actions. The repetition of the themes of 'fearing Allah' and doing 'righteous deeds' signifies the importance of consistency and the layering of spiritual and moral development in a believer's life.
orig: ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا إذا ما اتقوا وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally - his compensation is an equivalence of what he killed, from livestock, adjudged by two just men among you as a sacrifice to be taken to the Ka'bah or an expiation; or the feeding of the poor; or an equivalence in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has forgiven what is past; but whoever returns (to violation) - Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse serves as a test of faith and obedience for the believers, indicating that certain actions are prohibited during the sacred state of ihram. It highlights that God tests individuals in subtle ways to distinguish between those who sincerely fear Him and those who do not. The reference to ‘game’ emphasizes the importance of adherence to divine laws, even in seemingly minor matters. The consequence for transgression illustrates God's justice and the seriousness of violating sacred directives, underscoring the need for accountability and the opportunity for repentance. This approach fosters a deeper understanding of temporary abstentions and the moral responsibilities believers carry within sacred contexts.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of Ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent from livestock, adjudicated by two just men among you, as a sacrifice to the Ka'bah, or an expiation of food for the poor, or an equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his action. Allah has already forgiven what has passed; but whoever returns [to violation] - Allah will seek retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of certain sacred conditions, notably the state of Ihram during pilgrimage, which prohibits actions like hunting. It establishes a legal framework for accountability, indicating that intentional wrongdoing incurs an appropriate reparation, reflective of the severity of the offense. The verse signifies Allah's mercy in forgiving past transgressions while also warning against repeated violations, reinforcing the consequences of one's choices. It underlines the balance between divine mercy and justice, urging believers to adhere to their commitments and reminding them of the spiritual repercussions of their actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم ومن قتله منكم متعمدا فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم هديا بالغ الكعبة أو كفارة طعام مساكين أو عدل ذلك صياما ليذوق وبال أمره عفا الله عما سلف ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food as a provision for you and for those who travel, but forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the permissibility of sea goods and the prohibition of land game while in the state of ihram, which is a state of spiritual purity during pilgrimage. It emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine regulations as an expression of obedience and reverence towards Allah. Furthermore, it serves as a reminder of the eventual return to Allah for accountability, urging believers to maintain a conscious relationship with Him in all matters, including those related to lawful sustenance.
orig: أحل لكم صيد البحر وطعامه متاعا لكم وللسيارة وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a standing place for mankind, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the neck-ornaments. That is so you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and that Allah is All-Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Kaaba as a spiritual center and sanctuary for all humanity, highlighting its role in promoting unity, worship, and reverence. The mention of the sacred month and offerings indicates the importance of designated times and actions in the practice of faith. Ultimately, the verse serves to remind believers of Allah's omniscience, reinforcing that God is fully aware of the innermost thoughts and actions of all beings, thus encouraging accountability and mindfulness in one's conduct.
orig: جعل الله الكعبة البيت الحرام قياما للناس والشهر الحرام والهدي والقلائد ذلك لتعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Know that Allah is Severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual attributes of Allah; His capacity for both severe punishment and forgiveness. It serves as a reminder to believers about the balance between fear and hope in their relationship with God. The mention of Allah's severe punishment emphasizes the seriousness of disobedience, while the reference to His forgiveness and mercy encourages individuals to seek repentance and remain hopeful, knowing that Allah's grace is vast. This understanding is crucial for a believer's journey towards righteousness, guiding them to strive for obedience while seeking forgiveness for their shortcomings.
orig: اعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب وأن الله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messenger is only responsible for conveying the message, and Allah knows what you reveal and what you hide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Messenger as the one who transmits divine guidance without being held accountable for the response of the people. It highlights the importance of free will and individual responsibility in accepting or rejecting the message. Moreover, it serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of both the outward actions and the inner intentions of individuals, suggesting that genuine belief and submission to His will are of utmost importance.
orig: ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say, "The foul and the good are not equal, even though the abundance of the foul might impress you. So fear Allah, O people of reason, that you may be successful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental distinction between good and evil, urging individuals to recognize that quantity does not define value or quality. It calls on those with understanding to avoid being swayed by the superficial allure of what is 'foul' or impure, and instead to fear Allah, which implies a deep awareness of morality and accountability. Success is tied to this awareness and the conscious choice of what is good over what is tempting but ultimately detrimental.
orig: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب ولو أعجبك كثرة الخبيث فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if shown to you, would distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has overlooked them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to refrain from inquiring into matters that may lead to discomfort or distress. It implies that excessive questioning about certain issues can result in burdensome revelations, which may not be beneficial to one’s faith. The verse also reassures believers that some past questions have been forgiven by Allah, highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and patience. It encourages a focus on faith and trust in divine wisdom rather than dwelling on unnecessary uncertainties.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تبد لكم عفا الله عنها والله غفور حليم

translation: Indeed, a people before you asked for it, but then they became disbelievers because of it.
interpretation: This verse serves as a cautionary reminder about the consequences of questioning or demanding signs of faith. It suggests that previous communities sought more evidence or clarification of divine truths but ultimately fell into disbelief when faced with the expectations they had placed upon themselves. This reflects a broader theme in the Qur'an regarding the dangers of insincere inquiry and the importance of faith without doubt.
orig: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين

translation: Allah has not appointed any Bahirah, or Sa'ibah, or Wasilah, or Ham; but those who disbelieve fabricate lies against Allah, and most of them do not understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the misguided practices of pre-Islamic Arabian tribes who invented certain rituals and classifications regarding animals and their use in worship. The mention of Bahirah (a she-camel whose milk was reserved for idols), Sa'ibah (an animal freed for gods), Wasilah (a designated animal for certain deities), and Ham (a camel dedicated to gods) illustrates the absurdity of superstitions that deviate from pure monotheism. The verse emphasizes that such fabrications are a result of ignorance and disbelief, highlighting the importance of adhering to true faith and rejecting baseless claims that distort the understanding of the divine.
orig: ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة ولا وصيلة ولا حام ولكن الذين كفروا يفترون على الله الكذب وأكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away in aversion. And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away in aversion. And they say, 'Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our forefathers.' Even if their forefathers knew nothing and were not guided?
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance of those who cling to tradition in the face of divine guidance. It underscores the tendency of individuals to prioritize ancestral beliefs over seeking truth from Allah and His Messenger.
