translation: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like of it; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and the generosity of God towards good actions. It illustrates that for every good deed performed, the reward is multiplied tenfold, underscoring the importance of good intentions and actions in Islam. Conversely, it states that the punishment for evil deeds is limited to the act itself, preventing excessive retribution or injustice. This balance serves as a reminder of both the mercy and fairness of God, encouraging individuals to strive for righteousness while also being mindful of the consequences of their actions.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a sound religion, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not among the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine guidance towards a true and straight path in life, which is characterized by a sound and upright religion. It highlights the importance of following the monotheistic faith exemplified by Abraham, who is portrayed as a model of purity and dedication to God without any association of partners. This reflects a call to avoid polytheism and maintain a clear and direct relationship with the divine, aligning oneself with the core tenets of faith that promote truth and righteousness.
orig: قل إنني هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم دينا قيما ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the total devotion and surrender of a believer to Allah. It signifies that every aspect of life, including acts of worship and even one's existence and death, should be dedicated to Allah. This reflects the concept of Islamic monotheism, where every action, whether it be spiritual or worldly, is intended to please God. The verse urges individuals to align their intentions with the divine purpose, reinforcing the idea that true fulfillment and identity come from serving and being accountable to Allah alone.
orig: قل إن صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي لله رب العالمين

translation: He has no partner. And so I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God (Tawhid) and the command to worship Him exclusively without associating any partners with Him. The declaration 'I am the first of the Muslims' signifies a commitment to submission to God's will, highlighting the importance of following the path of faith and obedience to God as exemplified by the prophets. It reflects the idea that true faith is an individual undertaking that leads one to be among the first to submit to Allah's authority.
orig: لا شريك له وبذلك أمرت وأنا أول المسلمين

translation: Say: 'Shall I seek a lord other than Allah while He is the Lord of all things?' And no soul earns [evils] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that in which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God as the ultimate authority and sustainer of all creation, reinforcing the futility of seeking out any other deity or source of guidance. It also highlights individual responsibility for one's actions, indicating that each person is accountable solely for their own deeds and cannot shift their burdens onto others. The reference to returning to Allah signifies that ultimately all judgments will be made by Him, where disputes and differences will be resolved with divine justice. This conveys a strong message of personal accountability and the importance of aligning one's life with the truths of faith, reminding believers that their ultimate fate rests in God's hands.
orig: قل أغير الله أبغي ربا وهو رب كل شيء ولا تكسب كل نفس إلا عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And He it is who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees, that He may try you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in creating a hierarchy among people, where some are elevated in status or abilities to test their character and faithfulness in what has been entrusted to them. It reflects the idea that life is a trial, where our responses to the varying fortunes we are given determine our standing with God. Furthermore, it serves as a reminder of God's attributes: His readiness to administer swift justice, balanced with His ample capacity for forgiveness and mercy. This encourages believers to act righteously, recognizing their responsibilities as caretakers of the earth and the consequences of their actions, while also maintaining hope in God's compassion.
orig: وهو الذي جعلكم خلائف الأرض ورفع بعضكم فوق بعض درجات ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم إن ربك سريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem
interpretation: This verse consists of three Arabic letters which are among the mysterious letters at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. Their exact meanings are known only to Allah, and they serve as a reminder of the complexity and the miraculous nature of the Qur'an. The presence of such letters invites reflection on the divine origin of the scripture and encourages believers to focus on the deeper meanings and messages that follow.
orig: المص

translation: A Book has been sent down to you, so let there not be in your breast any discomfort from it, that you may warn thereby and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a divine revelation meant to guide and warn humanity. The instruction not to harbor discomfort or uneasiness signifies the need for a sincere acceptance of the message. It also highlights the role of the messenger, who must deliver the message without hesitation. Finally, the verse underscores that the Qur'an serves as a reminder for believers, reinforcing their faith and guiding them in their spiritual journey.
orig: كتاب أنزل إليك فلا يكن في صدرك حرج منه لتنذر به وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than Him as allies. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to divine guidance as revealed in the Qur'an, highlighting the notion that true guidance comes only from Allah. It warns against seeking support or guidance from sources outside of this divine instruction, suggesting that such actions can lead to misguidance. The phrase 'Little do you remember' reflects on human tendency to forget or overlook this imperative, serving as a reminder to reflect on one's commitment to following divine teachings over worldly influences.
orig: اتبعوا ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم ولا تتبعوا من دونه أولياء قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed while it was committing wrong, and We have made its quaking its prospective end, or its inhabitants were sleeping.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences that befall communities when they engage in wrongdoing and sin. The mention of cities being destroyed 'while it was committing wrong' highlights that divine retribution can occur unexpectedly, whether the people are unaware or caught off-guard in their daily routines. The imagery of destruction coming at night or while the people are resting emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of fate, urging individuals and societies to remain vigilant about their actions and seek righteousness to avoid similar fates.
orig: وكم من قرية أهلكناها فجاءها بأسنا بياتا أو هم قائلون

translation: So their only cry when Our punishment came to them was, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of people when they are faced with divine punishment after having lived in denial or disbelief. It emphasizes the moment of realization and regret that comes too late, as they acknowledge their wrongdoings only when it is too late to repent or seek forgiveness. This illustrates the concept of accountability and the eventual recognition of one's misdeeds when faced with the consequences of those actions.
orig: فما كان دعواهم إذ جاءهم بأسنا إلا أن قالوا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, We will question those to whom [Our messengers] were sent, and We will question the messengers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability that both the recipients of divine messages and the messengers themselves will face. It underscores the concept of justice in the Hereafter, where individuals will be asked about their responses to the teachings brought to them by the messengers of God. The messengers will also be held responsible for their delivery of the message and whether they fulfilled their duty. This verse serves as a reminder of the gravity of faith and the implications of one's choices in life, stressing that knowledge of truth carries the burden of choice and consequences.
orig: فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين

translation: Indeed, We will narrate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine knowledge and awareness, emphasizing that God is fully aware of all that occurs among people. The promise to narrate with knowledge implies that all events and stories of individuals will be presented with complete accuracy and understanding, underscoring accountability in the hereafter. It serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from God and reinforces the idea that every action is observed and will be addressed in due time. This fosters a sense of moral responsibility and encourages individuals to live righteously, knowing they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين

translation: And the weighing on that day will be the truth. So, whoever's scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of accountability and justice on the Day of Judgment. The 'weighing' refers to the assessment of one's deeds, illustrating that true success is determined by the balance of good versus bad actions. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad ones will find success and salvation, signifying the mercy of God towards those who strive to live righteously. It reinforces the concept that moral integrity and adherence to divine guidance are crucial for ultimate success in the hereafter.
orig: والوزن يومئذ الحق فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those whose scales are light - they are the ones who have lost their souls because they used to wrong Our verses.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of failing to uphold the truth and justice as dictated by the divine revelations. It suggests that those whose good deeds are insufficient will suffer significant loss, indicating that righteousness and adherence to divine guidance are critical for success in the hereafter. The wording emphasizes personal accountability and the gravity of one's choices in relation to the signs of God, pointing towards the realization that one’s disregard for divine messages leads to spiritual and existential failure.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم بما كانوا بآياتنا يظلمون

translation: And We have certainly established you upon the earth and made for you therein livelihoods; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine provision and establishment granted to humanity. It emphasizes that God has given people the ability to thrive and find sustenance in the world, yet it critiques the common human tendency to overlook gratitude for these blessings. The reference to 'little are you grateful' serves as a reminder of the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the gifts and opportunities provided by God, urging people to reflect on their lives and be more thankful for what they have.
orig: ولقد مكناكم في الأرض وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And We created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis; he was not of those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique status of humanity and the special role of Adam as the first human being created by Allah. The act of prostration by the angels signifies submission to divine will and acknowledgment of Adam's place in creation. Iblis's refusal to prostrate illustrates the concept of pride and disobedience, highlighting a fundamental distinction between obedience to God and the consequences of arrogance. It underscores the importance of humility and submission to God's commands, as well as the existence of free will and the potential for individuals to choose paths that lead away from righteousness.
orig: ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس لم يكن من الساجدين

translation: He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Iblis (Satan) who refused to obey Allah's command to prostrate to Adam. His belief in his superiority over Adam, based on the materials from which they were created, reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the nature of true worth and obedience to divine command. It emphasizes that one's creation or origin does not determine their value in the eyes of God, and that pride can lead to rebellion against divine authority. This story serves as a warning against the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility before God's will.
orig: قال ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, 'Descend from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So go out, for you are of the despised.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and pride. The command to descend signifies a fall from grace due to one's actions. It suggests that arrogance is incompatible with the humility required in the presence of God and within His creation. The term 'despised' underscores the severe repercussions of elevating oneself above others and failing to recognize one's own limitations and the greatness of God. This serves as a warning against pride and a reminder of the importance of humility and submission to divine authority.
orig: قال فاهبط منها فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها فاخرج إنك من الصاغرين

translation: He said, 'Give me respite until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for delay from a figure who desires to avoid judgment or punishment. It signifies a common theme in the Qur'an where individuals request extra time to prove themselves or to change their ways. It highlights the tension between divine justice and the human tendency to seek reprieve from accountability. The request to be held until the Day of Resurrection underscores the inevitability of that day and the understanding that life has consequences that will ultimately be faced. This interaction invites contemplation on the nature of time, accountability, and the hope for mercy amidst the reality of divine decree.
orig: قال أنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you are among the ones given respite.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine mercy and the allowance for time given to wrongdoers. It suggests that those who commit wrongdoing may be granted a temporary respite or delay in consequences, allowing them a chance for reflection, repentance, and change. It emphasizes that God's judgment may not be immediate, but is ultimately certain, encouraging individuals to be mindful of their actions and seek forgiveness before their time runs out.
orig: قال إنك من المنظرين

translation: He said, 'Because You have put me in error, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the defiance of Iblis (Satan), acknowledging God's power while vowing to mislead humanity. It portrays the concept of free will and the spiritual struggle between good and evil, highlighting Iblis's intention to intercept believers on the path of righteousness. It serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by individuals striving to remain faithful, emphasizing the need for vigilance and perseverance against temptation.
orig: قال فبما أغويتني لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم

translation: Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and you will not find most of them grateful.
interpretation: This verse reflects the comprehensive approach of temptation and challenges that a believer faces from all directions—spiritually, mentally, and emotionally. It emphasizes the tendency of people to be ungrateful for the blessings and guidance provided to them by God, highlighting the struggle between faith and doubt. The statement serves as a reminder of the constant vigilance required to maintain gratitude and awareness of divine mercy in the face of worldly distractions and doubts.
orig: ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين

translation: He said, 'Get out of it, despised and banished. Whoever follows you among them, I will surely fill Hell with you all.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the consequence of disobedience and the severity of punishment for those who follow the path of misguidance. The commanding tone emphasizes the finality of judgment, where the speaker, likely a representation of divine authority, expresses a determination to separate the faithful from the unfaithful. The mention of 'filling Hell' indicates an overwhelming consequence for those who choose to reject the right path, serving as a warning and a reminder of accountability in the hereafter. Overall, it underscores the importance of following the right guidance and the dire implications of leading others astray.
orig: قال اخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا لمن تبعك منهم لأملأن جهنم منكم أجمعين

translation: And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you wish. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of free will and the presence of boundaries set by divine wisdom. Adam and his wife are granted a bountiful existence in Paradise, symbolizing God's providence and generosity. However, the command to avoid a specific tree signifies the importance of obedience to God's commandments. The warning about being among the wrongdoers emphasizes the consequences of disobedience and serves as a moral lesson about the nature of temptation and the potential for straying from divine guidance.
orig: ويا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة فكلا من حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: Then Satan whispered to them to make apparent to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts, and he said, 'Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive nature of Satan and his ability to manipulate the truth. He suggests that God's command was not to protect Adam and Eve but to prevent them from achieving greatness, such as becoming angels or attaining immortality. This suggests a wider theme in the Qur'an regarding human susceptibility to temptation and the importance of discerning God's intentions. The emphasis on the revelation of private parts symbolizes the loss of innocence and the awareness of one's vulnerabilities, provoking thoughts about the human condition and the consequences of disobedience to divine guidance.
orig: فوسوس لهما الشيطان ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما وقال ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

translation: And he swore to them, 'Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers.'
interpretation: This verse captures the essence of deception and false sincerity. The speaker, in this case, is appealing to the listeners by presenting himself as a trustworthy adviser. The emphasis on 'swearing' highlights the intensity of the claim to sincerity. It serves as a warning about how appearances can be misleading, and that not all who claim to offer good counsel have honest intentions. This can reflect broader themes in human relationships regarding trust, manipulation, and the conflicts that can arise from ulterior motives.
orig: وقاسمهما إني لكما لمن الناصحين

translation: Then Satan misled them about the tree, and when they tasted of it, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called out to them, 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is a manifest enemy to you?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of the first disobedience committed by Adam and Eve. The consequence of their actions was immediate; upon tasting the forbidden fruit, they became aware of their nakedness, which symbolizes a loss of innocence and purity. Their attempt to cover themselves with leaves underscores the human instinct to try to hide one's mistakes and shame. The calling of God emphasizes the importance of divine guidance and the seriousness of ignoring it, highlighting that the nature of Satan as an enemy leads to regret and awareness of moral failure. This narrative serves as a reminder of the inherent challenges of following divine instructions and the presence of temptation in human life.
orig: فدلاهما بغرور فلما ذاقا الشجرة بدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وناداهما ربهما ألم أنهكما عن تلكما الشجرة وأقل لكما إن الشيطان لكما عدو مبين

translation: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound recognition of human fallibility and the need for divine mercy. The speakers admit their wrongdoing, demonstrating humility and the acknowledgment of their dependence on God's compassion. It highlights the crucial concept of repentance in Islam, where seeking forgiveness is fundamental. The phrase underscores the existential consequence of losing divine grace—being among the 'losers.' This is not just a fear of spiritual failure, but a broader existential crisis, emphasizing the importance of mercy and forgiveness in the relationship between humanity and the Divine.
orig: قالا ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا وإن لم تغفر لنا وترحمنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: He said, "Descend from it, you are enemies to one another. And for you on earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time."
interpretation: This verse reflects the fundamental nature of human relationships marred by rivalry and enmity. It acknowledges the enmity that exists among people, suggesting that life on earth will be filled with challenges and conflicts. However, it also reassures that the earth provides a place for humans to live and enjoy their time. This duality of conflict and provision serves as a reminder of the transient nature of existence, where despite differences, there is opportunity for sustenance and comfort in the world.
orig: قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: In it you will live, and in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse conveys the cyclical nature of human life in relation to the Earth. It emphasizes the interconnectedness of life, death, and resurrection. The phrase 'you will live' signifies the vitality and growth that the Earth provides, while 'you will die' acknowledges the inevitability of mortality. The concluding part, 'from it you will be brought forth,' alludes to the resurrection, indicating that from the Earth where we return after death, we will be revived for the afterlife. This reinforces the concept of accountability and the transient nature of worldly existence.
orig: قال فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون

translation: O Children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to cover your shame and as adornment; and the clothing of righteousness, that is better. This is from the signs of Allah, that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of clothing, both as a means of physical covering and as a symbol of righteousness. The mention of 'clothing of righteousness' suggests that true honor and dignity come not just from physical attire, but from one's piety and moral conduct. The verse also emphasizes that these provisions are a sign of Allah's mercy and wisdom, encouraging believers to reflect on the blessings they have received and to cultivate an awareness of their moral responsibilities.
orig: يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوآتكم وريشا ولباس التقوى ذلك خير ذلك من آيات الله لعلهم يذكرون

translation: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he caused your parents to come out of Paradise, stripping them of their garments to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to humanity about the deceptive nature of Satan. It draws a parallel between the temptation faced by Adam and Eve and the ongoing struggle against temptation that each individual faces. The stripping away of garments symbolizes vulnerability and a loss of dignity, and the reminder that Satan and his followers can observe humanity unobtrusively implies that they strategize from a position of hiddenness. This highlights the necessity for mindfulness and vigilance against falling into this trap, emphasizing that those who lack belief may become easily swayed and thus lose their moral and spiritual compass.
orig: يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة ينزع عنهما لباسهما ليريهما سوآتهما إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم إنا جعلنا الشياطين أولياء للذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And when they commit an immorality, they say, 'We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.' Say, 'Indeed, Allah does not command immorality. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the tendency of some individuals to justify their immoral actions by referencing the practices of their forefathers, implying a misguided sense of tradition. It emphasizes that true divine command cannot endorse such behavior, as it contradicts Allah's nature and will. The verse challenges blind adherence to ancestral customs and calls for personal accountability and the pursuit of knowledge over mere imitation. Ultimately, it underlines the importance of discerning right from wrong based on divine guidance rather than societal norms.
orig: وإذا فعلوا فاحشة قالوا وجدنا عليها آباءنا والله أمرنا بها قل إن الله لا يأمر بالفحشاء أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, 'My Lord has commanded justice and that you maintain yourselves at every place or time of prostration, and invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion. As He began you, so will you return.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and sincerity in worship. It calls for individuals to uphold their integrity and align their actions with divine commandments, particularly in the context of prayer and devotion. The mention of returning as one was initially created serves as a reminder of the cyclical nature of life and the need to remain devoted to God with a pure heart, reinforcing the idea that true worship must be devoid of hypocrisy and fully directed towards God alone.
orig: قل أمر ربي بالقسط وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد وادعوه مخلصين له الدين كما بدأكم تعودون

translation: A party He has guided, and a party deserves to be in error. Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, thinking that they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the division among humanity where some are guided by divine truth while others have chosen a path of misguidance due to their association with malevolent forces, represented as devils. It reflects on the consequences of turning away from divine guidance and relying on misguided influences, leading them to mistakenly believe they are on the right path. The mention of 'taking devils as allies' signifies a willful choice to follow destructive ideologies or companions that lead one away from the truth, indicating that misguided beliefs can lead individuals to a state of self-deception about their moral and spiritual standing.
orig: فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة إنهم اتخذوا الشياطين أولياء من دون الله ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of presenting oneself properly and with dignity in places of worship, reflecting the belief that worship is a significant part of life. The directive to eat and drink suggests that God allows for enjoyment of the blessings provided, yet it comes with the caution against excess. The notion of moderation is central, indicating that while one may indulge in the bounties of life, doing so excessively is contrary to divine preference. This encourages a balanced approach to life, where one's sustenance and appearance are harmonized with respect for the sacred and an awareness of the consequences of overindulgence.
orig: يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: Say, 'Who has forbidden the adornments of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good of provisions?' Say, 'They are for those who believe during the worldly life, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.' Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and adornments provided by Allah are not inherently forbidden; rather, they are intended for His servants. It highlights the distinction between the enjoyment of these blessings in the earthly life for believers and their ultimate exclusivity on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'thus do We detail the verses for a people who know' indicates that the wisdom in these provisions and the divine laws are made clear for those who seek understanding and knowledge. The verse encourages believers to appreciate and accept the gifts from Allah while being mindful of the greater rewards in the hereafter.
orig: قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق قل هي للذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا خالصة يوم القيامة كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know.'
interpretation: This verse outlines the boundaries set by Allah regarding actions that are considered immoral and sinful. It emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance in matters of ethics and morality, cautioning against both overt and subtle forms of immorality. The mention of associating partners with Allah underscores the severity of shirk, or polytheism, while the prohibition against speaking on behalf of Allah without knowledge highlights the necessity of understanding religious tenets before making claims. Overall, the verse serves as a reminder to maintain integrity in one's beliefs and actions, urging believers to seek knowledge and refrain from indulging in wrongdoing or promoting falsehoods.
orig: قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق وأن تشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And for every nation is a term appointed. When their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine decrees and the appointed lifespan of all nations. It highlights the concept of predestination in Islamic belief, emphasizing that each community or nation has a specific period set by God. When that time arrives, it cannot be delayed or hastened. This serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly existence and the importance of fulfilling one's responsibilities before one's appointed time ends. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and the transient nature of this life, understanding that they must ultimately return to their Creator when their time is up.
orig: ولكل أمة أجل فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves recounting My verses to you, then whoever fears [Allah] and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of receiving divine guidance through the messengers chosen by God. It highlights the role of human messengers as conveyors of God's messages, which are aimed at encouraging fear of Allah and fostering moral and ethical reform. The promise of safety from fear and grief for those who heed the message indicates that spiritual integrity and obedience to divine guidance lead to both emotional peace and security in the hereafter.
orig: يا بني آدم إما يأتينكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي فمن اتقى وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who disbelieved in Our verses and were arrogant towards them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and arrogance towards God's signs and revelations. It highlights a critical distinction between those who accept and submit to divine guidance and those who reject it out of pride. The implication is clear: rejection of truth leads to eternal punishment, indicating the seriousness of accountability in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning about the dangers of turning away from divine truth and the severity of the eternal consequences that await those who do so.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their share of the decree, and when Our messengers come to take them, they will say, 'Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?' They will respond, 'They have withdrawn from us,' and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave injustice of attributing falsehood to Allah and rejecting His signs. It underscores the consequences faced by those who commit such acts, emphasizing that they will face a reckoning when the messengers of Allah come. It is a reminder that when the time comes for accountability, those who have turned away from divine guidance will find themselves isolated, regretting their choices, and acknowledging their disbelief. The verse serves as a powerful warning about the seriousness of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and the ultimate accountability in the afterlife.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته أولئك ينالهم نصيبهم من الكتاب حتى إذا جاءتهم رسلنا يتوفونهم قالوا أين ما كنتم تدعون من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: He said, 'Enter among the nations which had passed on before you of jinn and mankind into the Fire.' Every time a nation entered, it cursed its sister until they had all embraced one another therein. The last of them said to the first, 'Our Lord, these have led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire.' He will say, 'For each is a double, but you do not know.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of collective wrongdoing and the mutual blame that ensues among those who led each other astray. It emphasizes that in the hereafter, individuals will seek to shift responsibility onto others, revealing the depth of their regret and acknowledgment of hellfire as a punishment. The mention of a 'double punishment' indicates that those who misguide others are held to account not only for their own misdeeds but for those they influenced as well. This serves as a reminder of the importance of personal responsibility and the impact of one's actions on themselves and others.
orig: قال ادخلوا في أمم قد خلت من قبلكم من الجن والإنس في النار كلما دخلت أمة لعنت أختها حتى إذا اداركوا فيها جميعا قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا فآتهم عذابا ضعفا من النار قال لكل ضعف ولكن لا تعلمون

translation: And those who were followed will say to those who followed [them], "What [is the matter] with you? You have no favor over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse reflects the dynamics between the influential leaders and their followers on the Day of Judgment. The leaders, once proud of their status, will disavow any responsibility for their followers, highlighting the notion that every individual is accountable for their own actions. The statement serves as a warning that reliance on others for guidance does not absolve one of personal accountability. It emphasizes the idea that even in community or groups, every person's choices and deeds ultimately determine their fate.
orig: وقالت أولاهم لأخراهم فما كان لكم علينا من فضل فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who have denied Our verses and were arrogant toward them — the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel goes through the eye of a needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences for those who reject the signs of God and display arrogance in their disbelief. It uses the metaphor of a camel passing through the eye of a needle to illustrate the impossibility of their entering Paradise due to their unyielding nature. The imagery stresses the extremity of their situation, highlighting divine justice that excludes the proud and unjust from mercy and eternal bliss.
orig: إن الذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها لا تفتح لهم أبواب السماء ولا يدخلون الجنة حتى يلج الجمل في سم الخياط وكذلك نجزي المجرمين

translation: They will have beds of hellfire, and over them, coverings [of fire]. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences awaiting those who commit injustices and transgressions against divine law. The imagery of beds and coverings made of hellfire signifies not only physical torment but also spiritual desolation. It emphasizes a divine system of justice where wrongdoers are met with retribution commensurate with their actions. The mention of 'beds' conveys the idea of being enveloped in punishment, while 'coverings' suggest an unending atmosphere of suffering. Ultimately, this serves as a stern warning about the importance of righteousness and the dire consequences of moral failures.
orig: لهم من جهنم مهاد ومن فوقهم غواش وكذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We do not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It is they who are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and justice of God in not placing burdens on individuals beyond their capabilities. It reassures believers that their faith and good deeds will lead them to eternal reward in Paradise, highlighting the importance of sincerity in belief and the necessity of righteous actions. The promise of eternal residence in Paradise reinforces the hope and motivation for believers to strive for good, while also implying that everyone will be judged according to their own strengths and circumstances.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And We removed whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [so they are] like brothers, on couches facing each other. Rivers flow beneath them, and they will say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this. We would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Indeed, the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth.' And it will be called out to them, 'This is the Paradise that you have inherited for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the state of the believers in Paradise, highlighting the removal of any ill feelings or grudges they may have held in their hearts, fostering an environment of brotherhood and harmony. The rivers flowing beneath them symbolize abundance and the perpetual delight found in Paradise. Their acknowledgment of Allah's guidance signifies the importance of divine guidance in realizing the truth and attaining salvation. The reference to inheriting Paradise reflects the just reward for their righteous deeds, reinforcing the concept of divine justice and mercy in the Hereafter.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل تجري من تحتهم الأنهار وقالوا الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله لقد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And the companions of Paradise called to the companions of the Fire, 'Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. So have you found what your Lord promised to be true?' They said, 'Yes.' Then a crier called out among them, 'The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of stark realization and affirmation of fate. The message highlights the contrast between the rewards of the righteous and the consequences faced by the wrongdoers. The dialogue emphasizes a communal recognition of divine truth and justice, as the inhabitants of Paradise celebrate their rewards while the inhabitants of Hell acknowledge their loss. The mention of the curse upon the wrongdoers serves as a reminder of the gravity of their actions in life, illustrating the importance of adhering to moral and ethical principles to avoid such a dire fate.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الجنة أصحاب النار أن قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقا فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا قالوا نعم فأذن مؤذن بينهم أن لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who turn others away from the Path of Allah and seek to make it crooked, while they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of individuals who actively oppose and obstruct the way of Allah, indicating their deep-seated enmity towards faith and truth. Their attempt to distort the path signifies not only their lack of faith but also a deliberate effort to mislead others. The reference to their disbelief in the Hereafter underscores the severity of their actions, as it reveals their rejection of ultimate accountability and the consequences in the afterlife for their misconduct.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة كافرون

translation: And between them is a veil, and on the heights are men who know each by their mark. And they call to the companions of Paradise, 'Peace be upon you.' They have not yet entered it, although they aspire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of separation between the inhabitants of Paradise and Hell, represented by a barrier or veil. The 'men on the heights' symbolize those who possess knowledge and can recognize the righteous based on their distinct attributes or marks. Their greeting of peace to the inhabitants of Paradise highlights a sense of hope and aspiration, as these individuals have not yet entered Paradise but still yearn for it. This underlines the theme of divine mercy and the potential for salvation, as even those who have not yet achieved entry express longing and a desire for tranquility among the righteous.
orig: وبينهما حجاب وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون

translation: And when they cast their eyes toward the companions of the Fire, they said, 'Our Lord, do not make us among the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment of recognition and despair among those who find themselves reflecting on their past choices in the Hereafter. The act of turning their gaze toward the companions of the Fire symbolizes their awareness of the consequences of their actions. In their plea to Allah, they express a deep-seated fear of being grouped with the wrongdoers, highlighting the importance of seeking forgiveness and divine mercy. This invocation is a call for protection from the ultimate fate of punishment, revealing the essential human desire for redemption and the pursuit of righteousness in the face of judgment.
orig: وإذا صرفت أبصارهم تلقاء أصحاب النار قالوا ربنا لا تجعلنا مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And the People of the Heights will call to men whom they will recognize by their marks, saying, 'What benefited you from your gathering and your arrogance?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are rewarded for their faith and good deeds and those who failed to recognize the truth due to their arrogance and worldly pursuits. It suggests that superficial status and wealth are meaningless in the face of divine justice, and that true identity is determined by one's faith and actions, which will be discernible even in the Hereafter. The questioning by the People of the Heights serves as a reminder of accountability and the ultimate futility of pride without righteousness.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الأعراف رجالا يعرفونهم بسيماهم قالوا ما أغنى عنكم جمعكم وما كنتم تستكبرون

translation: Are these the ones of whom you swore that God would never grant them mercy? Enter Paradise, for you have no fear, nor shall you grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the judgment of people and God's mercy. It addresses those who wrongfully assume that certain individuals are beyond God's grace. The verse encourages believers to recognize that God's mercy is boundless, and it invites those who are righteous and true believers to enter Paradise, promising them safety from fear and sorrow, which signifies the ultimate reward for their faith and piety.
orig: أهؤلاء الذين أقسمتم لا ينالهم الله برحمة ادخلوا الجنة لا خوف عليكم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or from what Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deep desperation and suffering of those in Hell, juxtaposed with the contentment and abundance of those in Paradise. The plea for water signifies not just physical thirst but a deeper yearning for relief and mercy that they can no longer attain. The response highlights the ultimate justice of God, showing that the rewards and provisions of Paradise are exclusive to the believers. This serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of disbelief, emphasizing the finality of divine justice and the irrevocable separation between the two groups.
orig: ونادى أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة أن أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله قالوا إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين

translation: Those who have taken their religion as play and amusement, and whom the worldly life has deluded. So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, and as they used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of treating religion as mere entertainment or a form of distraction, ultimately leading to negligence toward spiritual responsibilities and accountability. It underscores a warning that individuals who prioritize worldly pleasures over spiritual truths will face oblivion in the Hereafter. The use of the phrase 'We will forget them' signifies divine justice, emphasizing that those who dismiss their faith will be similarly disregarded on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being mindful of one's beliefs and actions in preparation for the afterlife.
orig: الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا وما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And indeed We brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, a guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a comprehensive and detailed source of guidance tailored for those who have faith. It suggests that the Qur'an is endowed with divine wisdom and serves as a means of enlightenment and compassion for believers. The phrase 'detailed with knowledge' highlights that this guidance is not arbitrary but rather based on divine understanding and wisdom that addresses the needs and conditions of humanity. Furthermore, it implies that belief is a prerequisite for fully benefiting from the Qur'an's teachings, indicating a reciprocal relationship between faith and the reception of divine guidance.
orig: ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم هدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Do they wait for anything but its interpretation? The day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, 'Indeed, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. So, is there any intercessors for us to intercede for us, or could we be returned to do otherwise than what we did?' They have certainly lost their souls, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable reality of the Day of Judgment, when the truth of all matters will be revealed. It illustrates the desperation of those who previously ignored or rejected divine guidance, realizing too late the consequences of their choices. Their plea for intercession signifies their recognition of the gravity of their actions; however, it also highlights their powerlessness in that situation. The phrase 'they have certainly lost their souls' conveys the profound loss associated with rejecting truth and responsibility. Ultimately, the verse serves as a warning against negligence in faith and actions, and it underscores the futility of attempts to repent when faced with the finality of divine justice.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا تأويله يوم يأتي تأويله يقول الذين نسوه من قبل قد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق فهل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا لنا أو نرد فنعمل غير الذي كنا نعمل قد خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and then established Himself on the Throne. He covers the night with the day, seeking it eagerly; and the sun, the moon, and the stars are all subjected to His command. Indeed, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique sovereignty and power of Allah as the creator and sustainer of the universe. The mention of creating the heavens and the earth in 'six days' reflects a divine plan and order in creation, highlighting the intentionality behind all existence. Establishing Himself on the Throne signifies His supreme authority over all creation, suggesting that He oversees and governs the universe with wisdom. The interplay of night and day illustrates the continuous cycle that Allah has ordained, demonstrating His control over time and the natural world. The subjugation of celestial bodies like the sun, moon, and stars reinforces His absolute command over the cosmos. Ultimately, this verse invites reflection on Allah's unparalleled power, the beauty of His creation, and the significance of His role as the Lord of all worlds, deserving of reverence and worship.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يغشي الليل النهار يطلبه حثيثا والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره ألا له الخلق والأمر تبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: Call upon your Lord with humility and in secret. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of approaching God with sincerity and humility, highlighting that true supplication should stem from a place of deep reverence and earnestness. The mention of 'in secret' suggests that one’s relationship with God is deeply personal; it is in the private moments of prayer and reflection where genuine faith flourishes. Furthermore, the verse cautions against transgression, indicating that those who exceed moral or ethical boundaries in their actions, particularly in prayer or supplication, are not favored by God. It serves as a reminder that sincerity and grace in worship are paramount, and that God desires His servants to seek Him humbly and respectfully.
orig: ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And do not cause corruption upon the earth after its reformation. And invoke Him in fear and aspiration. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the balance and harmony of the earth after it has been set right. Corruption implies actions that lead to injustice, destruction, or moral decay, which can undo the positive changes that have been made. It encourages believers to engage in prayer and supplication with a dual approach of hope for God's mercy and fear of His wrath, indicating the balance between hope and accountability in a believer's relationship with God. The assurance that God's mercy is close to those who do good emphasizes the importance of righteous actions and the hopeful nature of faith.
orig: ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها وادعوه خوفا وطمعا إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until, when they have carried a heavy cloud, We drive it to a dead land and We send down rain therein and bring forth thereby fruits from it. Thus will We bring out the dead; perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically illustrates the process of resurrection by comparing it to the cycle of nature. Just as rain revives the dead earth and brings forth life in the form of fruits, God's power will similarly bring the dead back to life. The mention of the winds serving as heralds of mercy indicates that divine mercy precedes the acts of creation and resurrection. It serves as a reminder that, just as one can see the visible signs of revival in nature, one should also reflect on the inevitable reality of resurrection and accountability in the hereafter.
orig: وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته حتى إذا أقلت سحابا ثقالا سقناه لبلد ميت فأنزلنا به الماء فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات كذلك نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And the good land - its vegetation emerges by permission of its Lord; and that which is bad - its vegetation emerges only sparsely. Thus do We diverse the signs for a people who give thanks.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrast between what is good and wholesome and what is harmful or of lesser value. The 'good land' symbolizes those who receive divine guidance and flourish in their faith and actions, producing abundant good in their lives. In contrast, the 'bad land' signifies a lack of guidance, resulting in sparse and unproductive outcomes. The mention of 'signs' emphasizes that these differences serve as reminders for people to appreciate and be grateful for the blessings they receive, encouraging a mindset of gratitude that leads to greater awareness and acknowledgment of God's gifts.
orig: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته بإذن ربه والذي خبث لا يخرج إلا نكدا كذلك نصرف الآيات لقوم يشكرون

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a Great Day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the central tenet of monotheism in Islam, emphasizing the importance of worshiping Allah alone. Noah's warning to his people demonstrates the urgency of recognizing the oneness of God and serves as a reminder that neglecting this fundamental belief can lead to dire consequences, particularly the fear of a significant punishment on the Day of Judgment. It illustrates the role of prophets as messengers who call their communities to righteousness and awareness of divine accountability.
orig: لقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: The elite of his people said, 'Indeed, we see you in obvious error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and condemnation faced by the prophet from the powerful and influential members of his community. Their assertion of 'obvious error' reflects a common reaction from those in positions of authority when confronted with a message that challenges their beliefs or status quo. It illustrates the theme of resistance to prophetic guidance, suggesting that truth often encounters hostility from those who are invested in maintaining their existing power and traditions. The term 'obvious error' indicates their refusal to engage with the message meaningfully, suggesting a shallow understanding of the truth while reinforcing the divide between the messenger and his people.
orig: قال الملأ من قومه إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين

translation: He said, "O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse underscores the idea of prophetic authority and the transmission of divine messages. The speaker asserts clarity in his mission and role as a messenger, distancing himself from any notions of delusion or misguidance. By addressing his people directly, he emphasizes his commitment to conveying the truth he has received from God. The phrase 'from the Lord of the worlds' highlights the universality and the high divine source of his message, reinforcing his legitimacy and the importance of the guidance he offers to his community.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي ضلالة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you; and I know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the messenger in conveying divine messages and offering guidance to the people. It reflects the responsibility of a prophet to not only deliver revelations but also to provide counsel to help others navigate life's challenges. Furthermore, it highlights the limitation of human knowledge compared to divine wisdom, suggesting that there are truths and insights that only Allah possesses. This calls on individuals to trust in the guidance provided by prophets, as they have been granted a deeper understanding of the realities that guide human existence.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنصح لكم وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Do you marvel that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, so that he may warn you and that you may fear (Allah) and perhaps receive mercy?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of divine guidance delivered through a human messenger. It challenges the listener's expectations about how revelation would occur, urging them to reflect on the nature of prophetic messages. The call to fear Allah and seek mercy highlights the relationship between awareness of divine warnings and the moral obligation to respond with reverence and humility. It implies that the arrival of such a reminder is a blessing and an opportunity for spiritual growth, prompting the community to consider their response to God's message.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم ولتتقوا ولعلكم ترحمون

translation: So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people blind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and the severe fate that befalls those who reject divine signs. The mention of saving Noah and his followers signifies the mercy and protection of God towards the believers, while the drowning of the disbelievers serves as a stark reminder of the inevitable justice that comes from denying the truth. It illustrates the theme of divine support for the faithful and the stark realities faced by those who turn away from guidance, characterized here as 'blind' to the truth.
orig: فكذبوه فأنجيناه والذين معه في الفلك وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوما عمين

translation: And to 'Aad (We sent) their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Hud as a messenger to his people, the 'Aad, urging them to abandon polytheism and worship the one true God, Allah. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism and fear of divine retribution for disobedience. The sentiment reflects a common theme in the Qur'an where prophets call their communities to recognize their Creator and eschew false idols, underlining the urgent need for moral rectitude and awareness of the consequences of one's actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: The leaders of his people who disbelieved said, 'Indeed, we see you in clear deviation, and we think you are among the liars.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the reaction of the disbelieving leaders towards a prophet or messenger, indicating their refusal to accept the truth he presents. They accuse him of foolishness and dishonesty, highlighting their arrogance and unwillingness to acknowledge the validity of his message. This demonstrates a common pattern in history where powerful figures dismiss the truth for the sake of maintaining their status and control, illustrating the clash between belief and disbelief and the challenges faced by those who seek to bring forth divine guidance.
orig: قال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه إنا لنراك في سفاهة وإنا لنظنك من الكاذبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, I am not a madman, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the struggle of a prophet who is faced with the rejection and mockery of his people. By asserting that he is not insane, the prophet emphasizes the seriousness of his message and challenges the misconceptions about him. His declaration as a messenger from the Lord of the worlds highlights his divine appointment and the gravity of the message he carries. This serves as a reminder of the importance of listening to divine guidance, even when it comes from unexpected sources, and underscores the themes of faith, resistance, and the responsibility of prophetic communication.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي سفاهة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a trustworthy advisor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of delivering divine messages with sincerity and integrity. The speaker, likely a prophet, indicates their role not just as a messenger, but as a genuine advisor who seeks the best for the people. It signifies a relationship built on trust and responsibility, highlighting that the guidance provided is for the welfare of the community, urging them to heed the revelations for their own benefit and salvation.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنا لكم ناصح أمين

translation: Do you marvel that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, to warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature. So remember the favors of Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of receiving divine guidance through a messenger who is relatable and shares the human experience. It speaks to the importance of recognizing the blessings and favors provided by Allah, suggesting that awareness of these gifts can lead to success both in this life and the hereafter. The reference to being successors after the people of Noah highlights a responsibility to act righteously and learn from past communities, reminding the believers of their origins and the continuous support from Allah in their creation and growth. Overall, it calls the community to gratitude and awareness to ensure they do not lose sight of their purpose and divine blessings.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح وزادكم في الخلق بسطة فاذكروا آلاء الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us that we should worship Allah alone and leave what our forefathers used to worship? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be among the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and resistance faced by prophets when calling to monotheism. The people question the abandonment of their ancestral beliefs for the sake of following a new message. It highlights a common human tendency to cling to tradition, even when it conflicts with the truth. Their challenge for proof implies a demand for signs or miracles to validate the prophet's claims, which underscores the tension between faith and rational skepticism in the face of new theological ideas.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لنعبد الله وحده ونذر ما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'Indeed, there has come to you from your Lord, defilement and anger. Are you disputing with me about names that you have named, you and your forefathers, for which Allah has not sent down any authority? So wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the futility of arguing over names or titles that individuals or their ancestors have created, which bear no divine backing or truth. It reflects a deeper concept of accountability to divine guidance rather than human constructs. The speaker conveys a sense of prophetic patience, indicating that the awaited consequence of such disputes, grounded in arrogance or ignorance, will ultimately reveal divine justice. It serves as a reminder that true authority and understanding come from God alone, and reliance on fabricated names which lack divine support leads to misguidance and sin.
orig: قال قد وقع عليكم من ربكم رجس وغضب أتجادلونني في أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما نزل الله بها من سلطان فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We cut off the root of those who denied Our signs and were not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the believers and disbelievers, emphasizing divine mercy and protection for those who follow the truth. It underscores the ultimate consequence of rejecting God's signs, which leads to their downfall. The phrase 'cut off the root' suggests a complete eradication of their influence, indicating that disbelief has dire repercussions not only for the individual but also for their community and legacy.
orig: فأنجيناه والذين معه برحمة منا وقطعنا دابر الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وما كانوا مؤمنين

translation: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah, sent to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the core message of monotheism, urging the people of Thamud to worship Allah alone and recognize His signs. The she-camel is presented as a divine miracle, a tangible proof of God's existence and power. The instructions given to them emphasize the importance of treating this sign with respect, warning of severe consequences should they harm it. This narrative illustrates the broader themes of the Qur'an, including divine guidance, the consequences of disbelief, and the importance of recognizing and adhering to God's signs in the world.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب أليم

translation: And remember when He made you successors after 'Aad and settled you in the earth, you make for yourselves palaces from its plains and you carve from the mountains houses. So remember the favors of Allah and do not commit abuse in the land, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and favors that Allah has granted to the people, highlighting their abilities to thrive, build, and settle in the land. It serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with such blessings, urging them to acknowledge and appreciate what they have received. The call to 'remember' is both a directive to reflect on past grace and a warning against abusing the resources and the environment, to avoid spreading corruption and causing harm. The mention of 'Aad, a people known for their might and subsequent downfall due to disobedience, serves as a cautionary tale about the consequences of misusing Allah's blessings.
orig: واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد عاد وبوأكم في الأرض تتخذون من سهولها قصورا وتنحتون الجبال بيوتا فاذكروا آلاء الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: The elite who were arrogant among his people said to those who were oppressed – to those who had believed from among them – 'Do you know that Salih is a messenger from his Lord?' They said, 'Indeed, we have believed in what he has been sent with.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dynamics between the powerful and the powerless in society, highlighting the skepticism of the elite towards the prophetic message brought by Salih. The arrogance of the elite is contrasted with the faith of the oppressed believers, showcasing the challenges faced by prophets and their followers. It emphasizes the theme of belief in divine messages despite societal pressures and the importance of acknowledging true guidance irrespective of one's social status.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم أتعلمون أن صالحا مرسل من ربه قالوا إنا بما أرسل به مؤمنون

translation: The arrogant said, 'Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have believed in.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection of faith by those who hold power and pride, emphasizing the conflict between belief and arrogance. It reflects the reality that those who see themselves as superior often dismiss the beliefs of the humble, demonstrating how pride can lead to disbelief. The arrogance represents a greater challenge to faith, showing that societal pressures can influence personal beliefs, leading to a collective denial of truth.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا بالذي آمنتم به كافرون

translation: But they hamstrung the she-camel and were insolent toward the command of their Lord, and said, "O Salih, bring us what you promised us, if you should be among the messengers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the defiance of the people towards Prophet Salih despite the clear signs and the divine warning he had presented to them. Their act of hamstringing the she-camel, a miracle assigned to them, signifies a severe rejection of the message and authority of God. The insolence showcased here reflects a deeper spiritual obstinacy; they demanded proof of his prophethood even after witnessing miraculous signs, showcasing their disbelief and arrogance. It embodies a theme of accountability and the tragic outcome that follows from ignoring divine guidance.
orig: فعقروا الناقة وعتوا عن أمر ربهم وقالوا يا صالح ائتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من المرسلين

translation: Then the quake seized them, and they became in their home lifeless bodies.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the suddenness and severity of divine punishment. The 'quake' symbolizes a powerful and overwhelming force that can bring about destruction and death, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. The mention of them being 'lifeless bodies' signifies the finality of their fate, emphasizing that there is no escape from the repercussions of their actions. It reflects the ultimate justice of God, showcasing His power over creation and the certainty of accountability in the hereafter.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not love the advisers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the frustration of a messenger who has fulfilled his duty to communicate the divine message and offer guidance, yet faced rejection and disdain from his people. It illustrates the common theme in the Qur'an where prophets encounter resistance and hostility despite their sincere efforts. The phrase "you do not love the advisers" emphasizes the human tendency to resist those who advocate for truth and moral rectitude, highlighting the societal challenges faced when confronting collective wrongdoing. It serves as a reminder for believers to appreciate and heed the guidance given by those who seek their welfare, instead of turning away in animosity.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

translation: And [mention] when Lot said to his people, "Do you commit such immorality as has not occurred before you by anyone among the worlds?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound moral and ethical decline exhibited by the people of Lot (Lut) as they indulged in acts considered abominable. Lot's rhetorical question underscores their deviation from social and divine norms, emphasizing that their immorality was unprecedented. It serves as a reminder of the importance of moral integrity and the consequences that befall societies that abandon it.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: This verse addresses the act of engaging in same-sex relations and highlights the unnaturalness of the behavior as it deviates from the prescribed order of creation, which promotes relationships between men and women. The term 'behaving ignorantly' suggests a lack of understanding and awareness regarding the natural laws established by God. It calls for self-reflection and consideration of actions in light of divine guidance, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the moral and ethical standards set forth by religion.
orig: إنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your town; indeed, they are a people who keep themselves pure."
interpretation: This verse reflects the reaction of a community against those who uphold virtue and righteousness. The exclamatory response of the people reveals their disdain for what they consider the moral superiority of the prophets or righteous individuals. Their desire to expel those who 'keep themselves pure' indicates a fear of being confronted with their own immorality and a retreat into a state of rejecting the truth. It illustrates a common response by societies that prefer to silence those who challenge their corrupt practices rather than engage with their message.
orig: وما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوهم من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; she was among those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy shown towards those who follow the guidance and the severe consequences for those who do not. It emphasizes the importance of individual choice and accountability, even within familial relationships. The mention of the wife, who chose to stay behind, serves as a reminder that one's associations do not guarantee safety or reward if they do not align with righteousness. Thus, it underscores the broader theme of the Qur'an regarding the fate of communities and the inevitable justice that follows divine judgment.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We sent down upon them a rain. So see how was the end of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of wrongdoing and the ultimate fate of those who oppose divine guidance. The mention of rain can symbolize both punishment and purification. The metaphor of rain falling upon the criminals reflects the divine retribution that overtakes those who persist in their transgressions. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing the signs and lessons from history, urging believers to reflect on the fate of past nations as a warning to guide their own conduct and decision-making.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And to Midian We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear proof from your Lord. So give full measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption. That is better for you if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and ethical conduct in economic activities. Shu'ayb, as a prophet, addresses his people, reminding them that their worship should be directed solely to Allah and that they must conduct their affairs with justice and honesty. The call to 'give full measure and weight' highlights the necessity of fairness in trade, while the warning against 'spreading corruption' underscores the moral responsibility individuals have to maintain societal harmony. The mention of receiving 'clear proof from your Lord' indicates that belief should be rooted in understanding and evidence. Overall, the verse encapsulates the synergy between faith and ethical behavior, stressing that adherence to these principles leads to prosperity and is a sign of true belief.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not sit on every road, threatening and turning away from the path of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you. And see what was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting the path of faith and righteousness against those who seek to disrupt it. It warns against obstructing believers and distorting the truth of God's message. The reference to their past as a small, vulnerable group reflects a reminder that with God's support, they grew in number and strength. It serves as a cautionary tale about the fate of those who corrupt God's message and lead others astray, which should inspire believers to remain steadfast and committed to the truth.
orig: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون وتصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن به وتبغونها عوجا واذكروا إذ كنتم قليلا فكثركم وانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And if a party of you believes in that which I have been sent with, and a party does not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and faith in the face of division among believers.
