The provision of good things highlights the generosity of God in meeting their needs. The verse reflects the concept of human superiority in terms of intellect, moral responsibility, and spiritual potential, calling upon mankind to recognize and fulfill their potential as stewards of the Earth.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: The Day We will call forth every people with their leader. Then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their record; and they will not be wronged a single date-fiber.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of accountability on the Day of Judgment, where each group of people will be summoned alongside their respective leaders or representatives. The leaders can be prophets, righteous individuals, or even the embodiment of their collective choices and actions. The phrase 'whoever is given his record in his right hand' signifies a favorable judgement, indicating success and righteousness. The promise that they 'will not be wronged a single date-fiber' underlines divine justice; it assures that every individual will receive fair treatment, where even the smallest deeds are accounted for, thereby highlighting the importance of every action in one’s life.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and even more astray in [his] way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who choose ignorance and turn away from the truth and guidance in this life will face greater consequences in the Hereafter. It reflects the spiritual blindness that comes from a refusal to see and accept divine guidance, suggesting that such individuals will not only be deprived of insight in the afterlife but will also find themselves lost and misled, highlighting the importance of awareness and acceptance of divine truth.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, they were about to mislead you from that which We have revealed to you, that you might invent about Us something else; and then they would have taken you as a friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense pressure and temptation faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from those who opposed him. They sought to divert him from the divine revelations, suggesting that he could fabricate a message of his own. The verse underscores the seriousness of such an attempt, as it could compromise the very nature of prophethood and divine communication. Furthermore, it illustrates the loyalty and bond they attempted to establish with him through manipulation, as though suggesting that by complying, he could gain favor or companionship with them. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges of remaining steadfast in truth while being surrounded by falsehood and the importance of adhering to divine guidance despite external pressures.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And if We had not made you stand firm, you would have almost inclined to them a little.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strength and support provided by God to His Messenger in the face of challenges and pressures. It highlights the danger of succumbing to temptation or being swayed by outside influences, even if it is just a little. The mention of God's assistance reflects the idea that, without divine guidance, individuals may falter and compromise their principles. This serves as a reminder of the importance of steadfastness and reliance on God to uphold one's faith and conviction in the face of adversity.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: Indeed, We would have made you taste double the (punishment) in life and double (again) after death; then you would not find for yourselves against Us any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of ingratitude and disbelief. It indicates that those who reject God's guidance and persist in wrongdoing may face an intensified form of punishment, both in their earthly existence and in the afterlife. The reference to 'double' signifies not just an increase in suffering, but a profound sense of despair and isolation from any support or guidance. It serves as a warning about the severity of divine justice, underscoring the importance of seeking repentance and guidance while there is still time.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, they were about to frighten you out of the land, but then they would not remain behind you except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attempts of adversaries to provoke or intimidate the Prophet Muhammad, seeking to expel him from his land. The emphasis on their temporary success illustrates the transitory nature of their power and the ultimate resilience of faith. It serves as a reminder that opposition may rise, but it will not endure in the face of divine support and guidance. The phrase 'except for a little while' suggests that their efforts are futile and will soon diminish, contrasting their fleeting influence with the enduring truth of the message being conveyed.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: This is the Sunnah (way) of those We sent before you among Our messengers, and you will not find Any alteration in Our Sunnah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unchanging nature of God's divine laws and decrees as established through His messengers throughout history. It reassures the believers that the principles and challenges faced by the prophets of the past are consistent and that God's guidance remains steadfast and reliable over time. The assurance that there will be no alteration in God’s Sunnah serves to strengthen the faith of the believers, reminding them that divine support and wisdom have always been available to those who strive in faith, and that they should have confidence in their path even amidst challenges.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night and the Quran at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Quran at dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayers throughout the day, specifically highlighting the times between the decline of the sun and nightfall. It underscores the spiritual significance of pre-dawn prayer and recitation of the Qur'an, indicating that this practice is attended by angels and holds a special status among the acts of worship. It serves as a reminder of the connection between prayer, the timing of the day, and the importance of engaging with the Qur'an as a source of guidance and light in the life of a believer.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And in the night, keep vigil with it as a supererogatory [prayer] for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of night prayers (Tahajjud) as a means of drawing closer to Allah and attaining spiritual elevation. The phrase 'a praiseworthy station' suggests a level of honor and recognition from Allah for those who sincerely engage in worship, especially during the quiet of the night when distractions are minimal. It inspires believers to dedicate themselves to extra acts of devotion, acknowledging that such efforts may lead to significant rewards and a status of commendation in the sight of God.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say, 'My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep yearning for guidance and support from Allah in both entering and exiting situations in life with integrity and truth. It emphasizes the importance of seeking a path that is honest and righteous, suggesting that the believer desires not only to act rightly but also to be aided in that process. The request for a 'supporting authority' indicates a recognition of one's own limitations and a call for divine assistance to succeed in righteous endeavors.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And say, "The truth has come, and falsehood has perished. Indeed, falsehood by its nature is bound to perish."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of truth prevailing over falsehood. It reflects a deep assurance that, regardless of how powerful or deceptive falsehood may appear, it ultimately lacks substance and is destined to disappear. The phrase 'the truth has come' signifies a revelation or realization that can dismantle the structures of falsehood, leading to the triumph of justice and reality. This serves as both a declaration and a form of encouragement for believers to remain steadfast in their pursuit of truth, reinforcing the idea that divine order prevails.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We send down from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual purpose of the Qur'an as a source of healing and mercy for those who believe, indicating that it provides spiritual nourishment and guidance. However, for those who reject or act unjustly, the Qur'an serves only to increase their loss, suggesting that their resistance to its message may lead to further moral and spiritual degradation. The contrast emphasizes the transformative power of faith and the negative consequences of injustice and disbelief.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency in human nature regarding gratitude and despair. When people receive blessings, they often become complacent and neglectful, distancing themselves from the source of those blessings, which is God's mercy. In contrast, when faced with adversity or hardship, they easily fall into despair, forgetting the mercy they previously enjoyed. This reflects the fickle nature of humanity and serves as a reminder of the need for consistent thankfulness and resilience in the face of challenges.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, 'Each works according to his own manner, but your Lord is Most Knowing of who is best guided in [his] way.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual paths and diverse actions based on personal inclinations and circumstances. It underscores that while people may pursue different routes in their lives, God possesses ultimate knowledge of their intentions, behaviors, and which of these paths leads to righteousness. The verse invites humility and understanding, acknowledging that ultimate guidance is in God's hands, and it serves as a reminder that the true measure of one's actions is known only to the Creator.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you about the Spirit. Say, 'The Spirit is from the command of my Lord. And you (mankind) have not been given of knowledge except a little.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mysterious nature of the soul or spirit, which is described as a command of Allah, indicating its profound significance and divine origin. Additionally, it emphasizes human limitations in understanding the complexities of existence, suggesting that while humans possess knowledge, it is only a fraction of what is out there, particularly regarding metaphysical matters. This serves as a reminder of humility in the pursuit of knowledge and recognition of divine wisdom.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We willed, We could take away what We have revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself any protector against Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of God over His revelations and messengers. It serves as a reminder that God's will prevails, and His guidance is a privilege that can be withdrawn. It highlights the dependence of His messengers on God's support, underlining that, without divine assistance, they would have no means of protection or advocacy. This encourages humility and reliance on God’s mercy, illustrating the severe consequences of turning away from divine instruction.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: Except for a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has been great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense mercy of Allah towards humanity, highlighting that it is through this mercy that individuals can find guidance and support. It suggests that despite human shortcomings and the challenges faced, the grace and favor of Allah are significant and play a crucial role in the lives of believers. The verse encourages reflection on the blessings that come from divine mercy, suggesting that one should remain grateful for the guidance and assistance provided by Allah's compassion.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: Say: If mankind and jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce its like, even if they were to assist one another.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inimitability of the Qur'an, asserting that no combination of human or jinn effort can replicate its literary, spiritual, and linguistic qualities. It emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, suggesting that its depth, wisdom, and guidance are beyond human capacity. The phrase 'even if they were to assist one another' underscores the futility of such attempts, implying that no amount of collaboration or collective strength among beings can equate to the divine eloquence and truth contained within the Qur'an.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: And We certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example; but the most of the people refused except for disbelief.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, indicating that it contains examples and teachings relevant to various aspects of human life and experience. Despite the clarity and abundance of guidance offered, the verse highlights that many people choose to reject this guidance in favor of disbelief. This reflects a broader theme in the Qur'an about the human tendency to resist truth and the consequences of such rejection.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they said, 'We will not believe in you until you make for us a spring gush forth from the earth.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the attitudes of disbelief and the demand for tangible signs before accepting the truth of a prophet's message. It highlights a common theme in the Quranic narrative where people ask for miraculous demonstrations to validate the claims of messengers. Their skepticism reflects a broader human tendency to require proof through sensory experiences rather than faith. The reference to a 'spring' signifies a desire for immediate gratification and the physical manifestation of divine power, contrasting with the deeper, spiritual faith that focuses on belief without needing constant validation through miraculous signs.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or do you have a garden of date palms and vines, with rivers flowing underneath it, and you can have it as you wish?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine blessings and the provision of paradise. It highlights the abundance and beauty of the gardens and fruits, symbolizing both material wealth and spiritual fulfillment. The rivers flowing underneath represent continuous sustenance and life's pleasures, implying that those who are grateful for their blessings and strive on the righteous path will ultimately enjoy eternal rewards in the hereafter.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or the heaven should fall down upon us in pieces as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us face to face.
interpretation: This verse reflects a sense of challenge and skepticism towards prophecies or claims made by the Prophet Muhammad. It reveals the attitude of disbelief among some people who demand overt signs or tangible proof of divine intervention or presence. The verse underscores the arrogance of those who reject faith, insisting on miraculous events instead of embracing the message of faith and submission. It highlights a crucial theme in the Qur'an: the contrast between belief based on faith and the human tendency to seek physical proof. The mention of the heavens falling signifies a desire for extraordinary signs to validate spiritual truths, pointing to the limitations of human understanding when confronted with the divine.
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend to heaven. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring us a book to read. Say, 'Exalted is my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and demands of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They challenge him to perform supernatural feats or provide tangible proof of his prophethood, such as descending with a book. The Prophet responds by affirming his humanity and his role as a messenger, emphasizing that he is not divine and that faith should come from understanding the message rather than seeking spectacle. This underscores the notion that belief should not be contingent on miraculous signs, but on the clear guidance of the revelation he brings.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human messenger?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief that some people exhibit when faced with divine guidance, particularly when it is delivered through a human being. It reflects a common human tendency to doubt the legitimacy of a messenger based solely on their human characteristics, rather than on the message itself. This skepticism can act as a barrier to faith, emphasizing that many reject truth not due to lack of evidence, but rather due to preconceived notions and biases regarding the origin of the message. It underscores the importance of recognizing the divine source of guidance, regardless of the human form it takes.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: Say, "If there were on the earth angels walking peacefully, We would have sent down to them from the heavens an angel as a messenger."
interpretation: This verse suggests that if the conditions were such that angels existed among humans in a state of peace and tranquility, God would have sent an angel as a messenger specifically for them. It emphasizes the message that divine communication is tailored to the nature of the recipients. The use of 'angels' here symbolizes purity and divine qualities; therefore, the verse indicates that the message of God is delivered through messengers suited to the circumstances and characteristics of the audience. It underscores the human condition and the necessity of prophetic guidance in a world inhabited by humans who are flawed and in need of divine instruction.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is Knowing and Seeing of His servants."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and witness of Allah in matters of truth and justice. It suggests that human disputes and disagreements are secondary to divine knowledge and oversight. Allah's awareness of His servants' actions reinforces the idea that He is fully informed about all matters, encouraging individuals to act with integrity. The phrase 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness' is a powerful reminder that, regardless of external validation or human testimonies, God's knowledge prevails and will ultimately be the judge of all deeds.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whomever Allah guides is truly guided, and whomever He leads astray, you will not find for them any allies besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, mute, and deaf. Their dwelling will be Hell; whenever it abates, We will increase for them the blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah in guiding and misguiding individuals. It highlights the futility of seeking support or allies apart from Allah, as ultimate guidance can only come from Him. The imagery of being gathered on the Day of Resurrection in a state of blindness, muteness, and deafness symbolizes the complete loss of awareness and understanding for those who turned away from divine guidance. Their plight is further emphasized by the description of Hell, indicating a relentless punishment that intensifies as their suffering persists, suggesting that their choices in life lead to dire consequences in the hereafter.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'When we have become decayed bones, will we then be raised up as a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief in divine signs and the skepticism towards resurrection after death. It illustrates a common argument made by those who reject the idea of life after death, questioning the possibility of resurrecting once they have decomposed. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God to bring creation into existence anew, regardless of the state of physical matter, and highlights the ultimate accountability that awaits those who deny truth.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them? And He has set for them an appointment, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse anything but disbelief.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah in creation, highlighting that just as He created the heavens and the earth, He can easily create human beings anew. The mention of a predetermined time (the 'appointment') implies accountability and the certainty of resurrection. The verse also critiques the stubbornness of those who, despite witnessing creation and the signs of Allah, choose to reject the truth and persist in disbelief. It suggests a warning about the consequences of such obstinacy and the importance of recognizing the signs of divine power.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, "If you possessed the treasures of my Lord's mercy, you would hold back for fear of spending. And man is ever miserly."
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of human beings and their reluctance to spend, particularly in doing good or assisting others. It suggests that if they had unlimited resources, they would still hesitate to share due to fear of running out, which reflects a deeper issue of greed and a lack of trust in God's provision. The verse serves as a reminder that true generosity comes from a place of faith and understanding of God's continuous bounty.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel when he came to them. And Pharaoh said, "I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the signs that were granted to Prophet Moses as proof of his prophethood and the divine authority backing him. The mention of 'nine clear signs' refers to the miracles that Moses performed to demonstrate God's power and to challenge Pharaoh's tyranny. The response from Pharaoh, who dismisses Moses by accusing him of being 'affected by magic,' reflects the repeated human tendency to reject divine truth in favor of disbelief. It also portrays the opposition Moses faced in his mission, illustrating the themes of faith versus disbelief and the divine support provided to those who stand for justice.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: He said, 'I certainly know that none has sent down these (signs) except the Lord of the heavens and the earth. I believe you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, where Moses asserts the divine origin of the signs he presents. It emphasizes the belief in the superiority of God's power over earthly authority and the eventual downfall of those who oppose divine guidance. The phrase 'I believe you, O Pharaoh, are doomed' serves as a condemnation of Pharaoh's arrogance and rejection of the truth, indicating that those who do not heed the signs from God are destined for failure and destruction.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: So he intended to provoke them from the land, and We drowned him and all with him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and oppression. The person's intention to provoke and harm others reflects a deep-seated tyranny. The drowning signifies divine retribution for his actions and serves as a reminder of the ultimate power of God over those who misuse their authority. This moment underscores the principle that those who oppress others may find themselves facing severe consequences, illustrating the justice of God in protecting the oppressed.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth as a mixed multitude.'
interpretation: This verse conveys a profound message about the journey and destiny of the Children of Israel. It emphasizes their temporary dwelling in the land, indicating a divine plan that extends beyond their immediate reality. The phrase 'when the promise of the Hereafter comes' points to a future fulfillment of God's promises, suggesting a resurrection or gathering of the faithful. The term 'mixed multitude' signifies unity among believers, transcending individual distinctions and implying that divine justice and mercy will prevail in the end. Overall, it encourages patience and faith in God's ultimate plan for humanity.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And We have certainly sent it down with the truth and in truth; and We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bearer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that it is revealed with truth and for a true purpose. The repetition of 'truth' highlights the importance of authenticity in divine messages. Furthermore, it delineates the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger who brings good news to the faithful while simultaneously warning those who may stray from the path of righteousness. This dual role of bringing hope and caution serves to guide humanity towards a balanced understanding of their faith, responsibilities, and the consequences of their actions.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an distinct, so that you may recite it to the people at intervals, and We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the careful and deliberate manner in which the Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad. The phrase 'distinct' indicates that the Qur'an is clearly articulated and organized, facilitating understanding and reflection. The instruction to recite it 'on the people at intervals' points to the importance of gradual learning and comprehension, rather than overwhelming the listeners. The term 'progressively' signifies that the revelation was tailored to fit the needs and circumstances of the early Muslim community, promoting a thoughtful approach to the divine message.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say: 'Believe in it or do not believe.' Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recognition of truth among those who possess knowledge. It suggests that true understanding leads to humility and submission, symbolized by prostration. It highlights the transformative power of knowledge—while some may reject the divine message, those who truly comprehend it are moved to reverence and worship. This serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge and being open to divine guidance.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, 'Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of realization and acknowledgment of God's greatness and the fulfillment of His promises. It emphasizes the trust and faith of the believers in God's words. The exclamation 'Exalted is our Lord' signifies a deep reverence and the acknowledgment of His omnipotence. It indicates a strong link between faith and the certainty of ultimate divine justice, highlighting that God's promises are never in vain and serve as a reassurance for the believers amidst challenges.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound emotional impact of divine revelation or understanding upon individuals. The act of falling upon their faces signifies deep humility and submission to God, showing that true recognition of divine majesty induces a state of vulnerability. The increase in humility reflects that such moments of clarity lead to an even greater acknowledgement of one's own limitations and the greatness of God. It emphasizes the idea that spiritual insights can evoke powerful emotional responses that lead believers closer to their Creator.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names." And do not raise your voice in your prayer or convey it with a voice low, but seek between that an avenue.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of God's names, highlighting that regardless of which name is invoked, they all encompass the divine attributes of God. It suggests that prayers should be made sincerely but without ostentation—maintaining a balance in the manner of invocation, avoiding extremes of loudness or quietness. The teaching here serves to guide believers towards a humble and respectful approach in their relationship with God, encouraging them to find moderation in their worship.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son and has no partner in sovereignty. And has no protector from humiliation. And exalt Him with [great] exaltation.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, highlighting that He is not in need of any offspring or partners, which counters polytheistic beliefs. It underscores His supreme authority and independence, reminding believers to hold Him in the highest regard and to express their devotion through praise. The mention of 'humiliation' suggests that Allah's strength and honor are unmatched, affirming His position as the ultimate protector and source of dignity.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and reliability of the Qur'an as a divine text. It highlights that Allah, in His wisdom and authority, has revealed a scripture that is free from any contradictions or errors. The phrase 'عبده' (His Servant) signifies the honor bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad, illustrating his role as the messenger of divine guidance. The absence of 'عوجا' (deviance) affirms the idea that the Qur'an is a clear and straight path for humankind, guiding them toward righteousness and away from confusion or misguidance. This verse establishes a foundation of faith in the Qur'an's authenticity and its role as a moral and spiritual guide.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: A Messenger, to warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of the Messenger, serving both as a warning against divine punishment for those who disbelieve or engage in wrongdoings, and as a source of glad tidings for the believers who strive to perform good deeds. It highlights Allah's mercy and justice; while He warns of consequences for those who stray from righteousness, He also reassures the faithful with the promise of a rewarding outcome for their virtuous actions. This instills hope and encourages moral conduct among the believers.
orig: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا

translation: They will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This phrase indicates the eternal and unchanging nature of the state that awaits those who have earned it, often referring to the rewards of Paradise for the righteous. It emphasizes the permanence and joy of this existence, contrasting it with the transient nature of worldly life. The use of 'forever' suggests not only a lack of end but also a profound security and contentment that comes from being in the presence of divine mercy.
orig: ماكثين فيه أبدا

translation: And warn those who say, 'God has taken a son.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the grave misbelief of attributing offspring to God, emphasizing the uniqueness and oneness of God. It reflects the core Islamic tenet that God is beyond human characteristics and does not engage in familial relationships as humans do. The verse calls for accountability and serves as a reminder of the seriousness of such declarations that undermine the oneness of God, which is a central pillar of faith in Islam.
orig: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor do their forefathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who speak about matters they do not understand, emphasizing the gravity of their words. It highlights the idea that falsehoods can be perpetuated through generations, resulting in a significant weight of deception in their speech. The verse serves as a warning against pride in one's opinions without a solid foundation of knowledge, underscoring the importance of truth and awareness in communication.
orig: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم إن يقولون إلا كذبا

translation: So perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their following, if they do not believe in this message.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional burden that can accompany the prophetic mission, particularly the sorrow a messenger may feel for those who reject the truth. It emphasizes the intensity of a prophet's concern for the spiritual well-being of their community, illustrating that despite the clarity of the message, some may remain obstinate. The term 'kill yourself with grief' underscores the limit of responsibility one has over others' choices, suggesting that while the prophet is deeply invested in guiding others, ultimately, each individual holds the accountability for their own faith or disbelief.
orig: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا

translation: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly possessions and beauty, indicating that they serve as a means to test humanity. The adornments of the earth are not for mere appreciation but are a divine test to discern who will engage in the best of actions. It emphasizes the importance of intent and righteousness in one's deeds, suggesting that true value lies not in material wealth or aesthetics, but in the quality and morality of our actions.
orig: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

translation: And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren land.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eventual fate of the earth, emphasizing the transient nature of the world and its possessions. It serves as a reminder of the impermanence of worldly affairs, indicating that all that exists will ultimately face destruction and transformation. The term 'barren land' suggests a state devoid of life, highlighting the futility of material pursuits in the face of the ultimate reality of divine will, judgment, and the hereafter. It instills a sense of humility and encourages individuals to focus on what is eternal rather than what is temporary.
orig: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا

translation: Or did you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder?
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary nature of the story of the companions of the cave, illustrating that it is a significant event demonstrating God's miraculous power. It invites reflection on the belief in God's signs and encourages the listener to acknowledge that there are many wonders in creation which serve as reminders of God's ability to transcend the ordinary. It suggests that some may underestimate the importance of such events, yet they are profound examples of divine intervention and the reality of the unseen.
orig: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

translation: When the youths sought refuge in the cave, they said, 'Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us in our affair right guidance.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincere supplication of the youths who sought refuge from oppression and idolatry. It illustrates their recognition of God's mercy and guidance as essential for overcoming their dire situation. Their request for divine help reflects a deep understanding that human efforts alone are insufficient; thus, they seek divine intervention to attain righteousness and wisdom in navigating their challenges. This emphasizes the importance of turning to God in times of need and illustrates a model for believers on how to seek assistance through faith and prayer.
orig: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا

translation: So We cast a cover over their ears within the Cave for a number of years.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the miraculous nature of the sleep of the companions of the Cave, emphasizing God's protection over them during their prolonged slumber. It symbolizes a period of withdrawal from the world, allowing them to escape the oppressive environment of their time. The phrase 'cast a cover over their ears' suggests a divine intervention that sheltered them not only physically but also spiritually, preserving their faith amidst adversity. The years mentioned indicate the passage of time, which highlights both the significance of their trial and the power of God to control time and provide safety to His believers.
orig: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

translation: Then We raised them up so We could make evident which of the two factions was more precise in calculating the time they had remained.
interpretation: This verse indicates a divine test to reveal which group had a more accurate understanding of the duration of their stay, symbolizing the importance of knowledge and awareness of time in the context of belief and actions. It emphasizes the idea that the awareness of one's circumstances and the ability to reflect on them is crucial for accountability and understanding one's place in the divine plan.
orig: ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

translation: We relate to you their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of faith and divine guidance. The 'youths' symbolize those who stand firm in their belief despite challenges. Their faith in God leads to increased wisdom and guidance, implying that true belief attracts divine favor and enlightenment. The mention of 'We relate their story in truth' emphasizes the significance of conveying authentic narratives to reinforce moral and spiritual lessons.
orig: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى

translation: And We tied [with courage] upon their hearts when they stood up and said, 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never invoke besides Him any deity. We would have certainly spoken then an excessive transgression.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of steadfastness and faith in moments of trial and adversity. It illustrates how divine support can empower believers to stand firm in their beliefs, even when faced with overwhelming opposition. The declaration of faith emphasizes the exclusivity of God as the only deity worthy of worship, rejecting any claims to polytheism. This serves as a reminder of the importance of unity in belief and the inherent strength found in a collective, unwavering commitment to the truth.
orig: وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

translation: These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring a clear authority against them? And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity of associating partners with Allah and the lack of proof for such beliefs. It emphasizes that those who claim other deities have a responsibility to provide valid justification for their beliefs, underscoring the injustice of fabricating lies about God. It serves as a call for accountability in matters of faith and a reminder that true justice aligns with the understanding of monotheism.
orig: هؤلاء قومنا اتخذوا من دونه آلهة لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان بين فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

translation: And when you have separated yourselves from them and from that which they worship other than Allah, then retreat to the cave; your Lord will extend for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of separating oneself from falsehood and idolatry to seek refuge in the sincere worship of Allah. It emphasizes the idea that by distancing oneself from those who worship other than Allah, believers can find solace and guidance through divine mercy. The mention of retreating to the cave symbolizes a safe haven where one can reflect, connect with their faith, and find strength against adversity. It reassures believers that Allah will provide them with assistance and ease their difficulties when they sincerely turn to Him.
orig: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

translation: And you will see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, it passes away from them to the left, while they are in a gap therein. That is of the signs of Allah. Whomever Allah guides is the rightly guided, and whomever He leaves astray - for him you will not find a protector.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine protection and the miraculous nature of the People of the Cave, emphasizing that their state and surroundings are manifestations of Allah's signs. The specific description of the sun's trajectory around the cave symbolizes the wisdom and control of Allah over creation. It suggests that those who are guided by Allah are under His mercy and protection, while those who stray are left without guidance, underscoring the importance of divine guidance in one's life. The juxtaposition of the natural phenomena with the fate of the individuals highlights the theme of faith, guidance, and the signs of divine presence in the world.
orig: وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال وهم في فجوة منه ذلك من آيات الله من يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

translation: And you would think them awake while they were asleep, and We turned them to the right and to the left, and their dog stretching its forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned back from them in flight and been filled with terror.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary state of the sleepers mentioned, who appear to be awake yet are in deep sleep. It emphasizes the miraculous nature of their situation, where divine intervention has kept them safe and undisturbed for an extended period. The mention of the dog adds to the scene of protection and loyalty. The overwhelming fear experienced by an observer illustrates the power of the unseen phenomena surrounding these individuals, evoking both awe and a sense of the unknown. This serves as a reminder of the mysteries of creation and the omnipotence of God, reinforcing the theme of trust in His plans and the reality of life beyond mere appearances.
orig: وتحسبهم أيقاظا وهم رقود ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا ولملئت منهم رعبا

translation: And thus We raised them up, that they might question one another. A speaker among them said, 'How long have you remained (here)?' They said, 'We have remained a day or part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look at what sustenance is purest and bring you provision from it, and let him be cautious and let no one know about you.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a theme of resurrection and inquiry about time and existence. The act of raising them up serves as a reminder of divine power and knowledge. Their discussion highlights humanity's innate curiosity about the passage of time and their experiences. The instruction to send one of them to the city for pure sustenance signifies the importance of seeking what is good and beneficial in life. Additionally, it underscores the need for caution and discretion when faced with societal change or potential risks, suggesting that faith and prudence are essential when navigating life’s challenges.
orig: وكذلك بعثناهم ليتساءلوا بينهم قال قائل منهم كم لبثتم قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم قالوا ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه إلى المدينة فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما فليأتكم برزق منه وليتلطف ولا يشعرن بكم أحدا

translation: Indeed, if they prevail against you, they would stone you or force you back into their religion. And you will never succeed if that happens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the harshness and hostility faced by those who uphold their faith in the face of opposition. It underscores the potential consequences of losing one's beliefs under pressure from external forces and serves as a warning to remain steadfast in the pursuit of truth and righteousness. The mention of stoning and coercion highlights the extreme measures that might be employed against believers, while the assertion that they will 'never succeed' implies that true success lies not in conforming to oppression but in maintaining faith despite challenges.
orig: إنهم إن يظهروا عليكم يرجموكم أو يعيدوكم في ملتهم ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا

translation: And thus We made their case known, so that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it. When they disputed among themselves concerning their affair, they said, 'Construct a building over them. Their Lord knows best about them.' Those who prevailed over their affair said, 'We will surely take [for ourselves] a masjid (place of worship) over them.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a significant moment of revelation emphasizing the truth of divine promises, particularly regarding the Day of Judgment. It reflects on the consequences of faith and the enduring nature of God's will. The dialogue among the individuals highlights human tendencies to dispute and the subsequent decisions made in acknowledgment of a higher truth. The suggestion to build a mosque signifies a desire for remembrance and connection to the divine, illustrating how such encounters with faith can lead to communal expressions of worship and recognition of divine omniscience.
orig: وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم ليعلموا أن وعد الله حق وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها إذ يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم فقالوا ابنوا عليهم بنيانا ربهم أعلم بهم قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا

translation: They will say, 'Three, and their dog is the fourth of them.' And they will say, 'Five, and their dog is the sixth of them,' guessing at the unseen. And they will say, 'Seven, and their dog is the eighth of them.' Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except for a few.' So do not debate about them except for an outward appearance, and do not inquire about them among them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the uncertainty and speculation of people regarding certain truths, emphasizing that only God truly knows the particulars of every matter. It warns against excessive debate and speculation, indicating that knowledge of certain realities is limited to divine wisdom. It suggests that human understanding may be flawed and encourages believers to focus on what is clear and evident, rather than engaging in frivolous arguments based on conjecture.
orig: سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا

translation: And do not say of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and recognizing the limitations of human planning. It serves as a reminder that no one can guarantee what will happen in the future, as it is ultimately in the hands of God. Instead of claiming certainty about future actions, individuals should acknowledge that unforeseen circumstances may arise, and they should express their intentions with a sense of humility, invoking God's will. This verse encourages Muslims to rely on God's knowledge and plan rather than their own understanding of the future.
orig: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا

translation: Unless Allah wills. And mention your Lord when you forget, and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this in guidance."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two key aspects in the journey of faith and guidance. First, it highlights the importance of divine will, suggesting that all outcomes are contingent upon Allah's decree. Second, it encourages the believer to remain connected to their Creator, especially in moments of forgetfulness or doubt. By mentioning Allah in times of forgetfulness, one acknowledges reliance on divine guidance, and the supplication reflects a hopeful seeking of further clarity and righteousness in one's actions. It speaks to the continuous quest for deeper understanding and the importance of seeking Allah's guidance actively.
orig: إلا أن يشاء الله واذكر ربك إذا نسيت وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and increased by nine.
interpretation: This verse describes the remarkable duration of the sleep of the People of the Cave, signifying not just the passage of time but also the miraculous preservation of their faith. It emphasizes the idea that time has no hold over those who are divinely favored. The mention of 'three hundred years' and 'nine more' can also signify a completion of a significant era, as well as the notion that divine will transcends human understanding of time. This serves as a reminder of the infinite power of God and the transient nature of earthly life.
orig: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا

translation: Say, 'Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How clear of sight and hearing is He! They have not besides Him any protector, and He does not share in His command anyone.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and authority of Allah over all matters, including the unseen aspects of existence. It highlights that only Allah has knowledge of the time the individuals in question spent in a state of uncertainty, reinforcing His unique position as the ultimate knower of all things. The mention of His sight and hearing underscores His ability to comprehend every detail of creation without limitation. Additionally, the verse asserts that no one else has the power to influence His decrees, signifying His absolute sovereignty and the futility of seeking external intercessors in His affairs. This serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of relying solely on Allah for guidance and support.
orig: قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا له غيب السماوات والأرض أبصر به وأسمع ما لهم من دونه من ولي ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changer of His words, and you will not find any refuge besides Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of adhering to divine revelation and the immutability of God's words. It serves as a reminder that no one can alter the truth of God's message, which remains constant and unchanging. Moreover, it highlights the futility of seeking refuge or solace outside of God's guidance, as ultimate security and direction can only be found in the divine. This underlines the need for believers to guard and disseminate the teachings of the Qur'an as the ultimate source of wisdom and understanding in their lives.
orig: واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك لا مبدل لكلماته ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: And keep yourself patient by being with those who invoke their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever in transgression.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of companionship and the influence of one’s environment on their spiritual journey. It advises believers to remain in the company of those who are devoted to God and sincerely seek His pleasure, signifying that spiritual aspiration should take precedence over worldly attractions. The mention of not letting one’s vision stray towards worldly beauty highlights the transient nature of material gains compared to the eternal rewards of piety. Additionally, it warns against associating with those who neglect the remembrance of God, as they may lead one astray with their desires and frivolous pursuits, illustrating the critical choice between nurturing one's faith or succumbing to fleeting worldly temptations.
orig: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا

translation: And say, 'The truth is from your Lord.' So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will encompass them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, that will scald their faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will in matters of faith. Each individual is given the choice to accept or deny the truth revealed by God. The warning against disbelief is starkly illustrated with vivid imagery of the punishment awaiting the unjust. The description of the fire and the molten metal-like water serves as a powerful reminder of the consequences of one's choices in life. Here, the verse not only addresses the reality of divine judgment but also invites reflection on the gravity of one's decisions regarding belief and morality.
orig: وقل الحق من ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will not waste the reward of one who does well in deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and encouragement for believers. It reassures those who possess faith and engage in good actions that their efforts will not be overlooked or rendered futile. It underscores the importance of combining belief with righteous deeds, highlighting that true faith necessitates action. The promise of reward serves as motivation for individuals to maintain their commitment to doing good, fostering a sense of hope and accountability.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا

translation: They are the ones who will have Gardens of Eternity beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and thick silk, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward and good is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rewards awaiting the righteous in Paradise. The imagery employed symbolizes luxury, beauty, and comfort, reflecting the ultimate bliss and contentment in the afterlife. The mention of gardens and flowing rivers suggests abundance and tranquility, while the adornments of gold and sumptuous clothing highlight the honor afforded to the believers. The phrase 'reclining on adorned couches' signifies a state of ease and delight, portraying a heavenly experience far removed from worldly struggles. Overall, the verse encapsulates the idea that faithfulness and righteousness in this life lead to unparalleled rewards in the hereafter.
orig: أولئك لهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتهم الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ويلبسون ثيابا خضرا من سندس وإستبرق متكئين فيها على الأرائك نعم الثواب وحسنت مرتفقا

translation: And set forth for them a parable of two men. We made for one of them two gardens of vines and We surrounded them with date palms and placed crops in between them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrast between two individuals, emphasizing the richness and blessings bestowed upon one while hinting at the futility or lack of such blessings in the other. The gardens symbolize abundance and prosperity, representing Allah's provision and mercy. It encourages reflection on the rewards of gratitude and the responsibilities that accompany such gifts, urging the believers to appreciate and wisely utilize the blessings they receive in their lives.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا

translation: Both gardens produced their fruit and did not fall short thereof in anything, and We caused a river to gush forth therein.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the bountiful provision of God and reflects on the abundant blessings that are granted to those who are righteous and grateful. The 'two gardens' symbolize a state of spiritual and material prosperity, where nothing is lacking from one's sustenance as long as one remains within the boundaries of faith and gratitude. The mention of the river signifies both physical nourishment and the flow of divine mercy, indicating that such prosperity is sustained by a continuous source of grace from God.
orig: كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها ولم تظلم منه شيئا وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا

translation: And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, 'I am more than you in wealth and stronger in manpower.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of a wealthy individual who boasts about his possessions and influence. The emphasis on material wealth and strength reflects a common human tendency to measure success through external means. This serves as a reminder of the transitory nature of worldly possessions and the importance of humility and gratitude. The dialogue encapsulates a sense of competition and rivalry, which can divert one from recognizing the greater, enduring values in life.
orig: وكان له ثمر فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا

translation: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, 'I do not think that this will ever perish.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and self-delusion of a man who, despite facing the blessings of his garden, fails to recognize the transient nature of worldly possessions. His belief that his wealth and status are eternal reflects a lack of humility and an omission of faith in God's decrees. It serves as a reminder of the impermanence of material success and the moral consequences of complacency, encouraging individuals to be mindful of their own limitations and the ever-changing nature of life.
orig: ودخل جنته وهو ظالم لنفسه قال ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا

translation: And I do not think that the Hour will arise; and even if I were returned to my Lord, I would surely find better than this as a return.
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep-seated disbelief in the Day of Judgment and a sense of self-sufficiency. The speaker expresses skepticism about the afterlife, indicating a reliance on worldly possessions and status rather than on spiritual values. The claim of finding something better in the hereafter reveals a lack of understanding of divine wisdom and the value of faith. It serves as a cautionary reminder of the arrogance and denial that can lead individuals to dismiss accountability in the eyes of God.
orig: وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا

translation: His companion said to him while conversing: 'Do you disbelieve in the One who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you into a man?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the incredulity of rejecting the Creator, who is responsible for the intricate process of human creation. It highlights the various stages of human development, from the most basic element (dust) to a more complex form (sperm-drop) and ultimately to a fully formed human being. The dialogue serves to challenge disbelief by reminding individuals of the divine origin and development of life, thus illustrating the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the Creator's power and wisdom in the creation of humanity.
orig: قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

translation: But He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the absolute oneness of God. It reflects a deep personal relationship with Allah, where the speaker acknowledges Him as their only Lord, thereby rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. It highlights the fundamental Islamic principle of tawhid, the belief in the indivisible oneness of God, which is central to the faith and serves as a guiding principle for a believer's actions and worship.
orig: لكنا هو الله ربي ولا أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And if you had entered your garden and said, 'What Allah has willed; there is no power except in Allah.' If you see me less than you in wealth and children.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing God's will and power when experiencing personal success or prosperity. The mention of humility in the face of one's blessings serves as a reminder not to boast or envy. The believer is encouraged to attribute all goodness to Allah and to remain mindful of the transient nature of worldly possessions. Additionally, it underscores that wealth and offspring should not be a basis for arrogance, and that true strength comes from reliance on Allah.
orig: ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا

translation: So perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden and will send upon it a calamity from the sky, so that it becomes a slippery sand.
interpretation: This verse reflects the theme of divine power and the transient nature of material wealth and success. Here, the speaker expresses a hope that God may bless him with something far better than what he sees as the fleeting riches of another. It emphasizes the concept that human achievements can be easily undone by divine will, as seen in the mention of a calamity that could befall the garden, turning it into mere sand. This serves as a reminder that reliance solely on worldly possessions is misguided, and that true sustenance and success come from God alone.
orig: فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا

translation: Or its water will become sunken, then you will never be able to seek it.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically reflects on the fragility of life and resources. It underscores the reality that blessings, like water, can be abundant but may also become scarce or completely inaccessible. The imagery of water becoming sunken serves as a warning that neglect or mismanagement can lead to loss. It prompts individuals to appreciate and safeguard their resources, highlighting the importance of responsibility and foresight in ensuring sustainability in life and faith.
orig: أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا

translation: And his fruits were surrounded, and he began to turn his hands in dismay over what he had spent on it while it was in ruins upon its trellises. And he said, 'Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of realization and regret faced by an individual who, despite his material success and lavish investments, finds himself in a state of despair when those investments fail. The imagery of him turning his hands signifies a sense of helplessness and loss, emphasizing that material wealth is transient and can be taken away. The regret expressed in wishing he had not associated partners with God underscores the importance of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry. It reflects a broader existential lesson about the futility of worldly ties when compared to spiritual fidelity and the ultimate accountability one has before God.
orig: وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And he had no group to support him besides Allah, nor was he victorious.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the notion of divine support and the ultimate reliance on God. It emphasizes that in moments of trial or adversity, human alliances or groups may be ineffective if they are not backed by divine will. The lack of support mentioned indicates a state of isolation in the face of challenges, highlighting the futility of seeking help solely from other human beings without faith in God. Ultimately, true victory and support come solely from Allah, reminding believers of the importance of turning toward their Creator in times of need.
orig: ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان منتصرا

translation: Indeed, the sovereignty belongs to Allah. The truth is, He is the best reward and the best outcome.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exclusive sovereignty of Allah over all matters, emphasizing that ultimate authority and power rest with Him. The phrase 'the best reward and the best outcome' suggests that true success and fulfillment come from aligning oneself with divine will and that earthly rewards pale in comparison to what Allah offers. It serves as a reminder to seek Allah's pleasure above all else, as His rewards are everlasting and far superior to any worldly gains.
orig: هنالك الولاية لله الحق هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا

translation: And present to them the example of the worldly life, like water We have sent down from the sky, which has mingled with the vegetation of the earth, and then it becomes dry fragments scattered by the winds. And Allah is competent over all things.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transient nature of worldly life compared to the eternal reality of the hereafter. The imagery of water, which gives life to plants, highlights how life can flourish but is ultimately fleeting. Just as vegetation can quickly dry up and be scattered by the wind, so too can worldly possessions and status vanish. This serves as a reminder for believers to not become overly attached to the temporary pleasures of this world, as they will inevitably fade away, while God's power and authority remain constant.
orig: واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا

translation: Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for [one's] hope.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly possessions and relationships, emphasizing that while wealth and children are valuable and can enhance our lives, they are ultimately temporary. In contrast, the 'enduring good deeds' refer to righteous actions that have a lasting impact and can lead to divine reward. The verse encourages believers to prioritize actions that yield long-term benefits in the sight of God, as they provide true hope and sustenance in the afterlife, rather than being solely focused on the ephemeral pleasures of this world.
orig: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا

translation: And the day We will move the mountains and you will see the earth appearing and We will gather them and not leave behind any one of them.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, a significant event in Islamic eschatology, where all creation will be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds. The imagery of moving mountains and the earth being exposed signifies the dramatic transformation of the natural order, emphasizing the majesty and power of Allah during that moment. The phrase 'not leave behind any one of them' underscores the concept of divine justice, indicating that everyone will be gathered for judgment without exception, highlighting the thoroughness of Allah's knowledge and the gravity of the accountability that awaits.
orig: ويوم نسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows. 'Indeed, you have come to Us just as We created you the first time; but you claimed that We would never make for you an appointment.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the concept of accountability before God on the Day of Judgment, where all individuals will stand in rows, facing their Creator. It emphasizes the continuity of creation, indicating that humans will return to their original state before their Lord. The mention of their previous claims highlights humanity's skepticism regarding divine promises, particularly concerning resurrection and judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of facing divine justice and encourages believers to reflect on their actions and the reality of the afterlife.
orig: وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا

translation: And the record [of deeds] will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of that which is [written] therein. And they will say, 'Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or large except that it has enumerated it?' And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and thoroughness of divine judgment. The 'book' symbolizes the record of every individual's actions, reflecting how nothing escapes God's awareness. It portrays a scene of terror for wrongdoers as they confront the weight of their deeds, realizing that their actions, whether minor or significant, have been meticulously documented. This highlights the justice of God, who does not wrong anyone, ensuring that everyone is held accountable for their choices and actions. The verse serves as a reminder of moral responsibility and the consequences of one's behavior in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا مال هذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis; he was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between angels and Iblis, showing that while the angels obeyed God's command to prostrate to Adam, Iblis, out of pride and rebellion, refused to submit. This act of defiance represents a fundamental choice between obedience to God's will and the egocentric desire for superiority. The verse warns the believers about the consequences of befriending those who oppose God, indicating that Iblis and his progeny are natural adversaries to humanity. It advises against siding with these enemies, as it would lead to spiritual ruin, particularly for those who are unjust and oppressive.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا

translation: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves; and I would not take those who mislead as supporters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that human beings have no knowledge of the creation process of the universe or even of their own existence. It serves as a reminder of the limitations of human understanding and the futility of relying on misguided beliefs or those who lead others astray. The statement implies that divine authority and knowledge are far superior to human limitations, suggesting that misguided figures cannot be true supporters in the quest for understanding and truth.
orig: ما أشهدتهم خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا

translation: And the Day He will say, 'Call upon My partners whom you claimed.' And they will not respond to them, and We will make evident for them the punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of false associations and the consequences of disbelief. On the Day of Judgment, those who attributed partners to Allah will be called to account, and their partners will be unable to assist them. This serves as a reminder of the reality of divine authority and the ultimate inability of anyone other than Allah to provide help or salvation. The mention of punishment emphasizes the seriousness of rejecting the oneness of Allah and the misguided paths chosen by individuals in their worldly lives.
orig: ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا

translation: And the criminals saw the Fire and deemed that they were to fall into it, and they found no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of realization for the wrongdoers when they face the consequences of their actions. The imagery of the Fire symbolizes punishment and despair, highlighting the inevitability of divine justice. The criminals' belief that they are destined to fall into the Fire reflects their guilt and the weight of their sins. The phrase 'and they found no escape from it' signifies the hopelessness of their situation, emphasizing that their past choices have led them to a point of no return, making them aware of the gravity of their misdeeds and the certainty of their fate.
orig: ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفا

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every [kind of] example. But man has ever been, most of anything, a disputant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of the teachings and examples presented in the Qur'an, indicating that it caters to various aspects of human experience and thought. Despite this diversity, it points out a fundamental characteristic of humanity—our tendency to engage in disputes and arguments. This could reflect a deeper commentary on human behavior, suggesting that instead of seeking understanding or unity through the wisdom offered in the Qur'an, many choose to argue and debate. It is a call to reflect on the wisdom contained within the Qur'an and to approach its message with an open heart rather than a contentious spirit.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا

translation: And what has prevented the people from believing when guidance has come to them and seeking forgiveness from their Lord, except that there has come to them the way of the ancients or that the punishment has come to them face-to-face?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the reasons that hinder people from accepting faith and repenting to God even when they are presented with clear guidance. It suggests that individuals may be waiting for a significant event or trial similar to those faced by previous nations, or they may be afraid of facing immediate divine punishment. This highlights human tendencies towards doubt and procrastination in faith, often tied to a desire for validation through tangible experiences or historical occurrences.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ويستغفروا ربهم إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا

translation: And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to avert [people] from the way of Allah. And they take My verses and that of which they are warned in ridicule.
