It also serves as a reminder that illusions created by those who practice magic or deceit hold no real substance and that ultimately, such practices will lead to failure in the face of truth and divine authority.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: Then the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a powerful moment of recognition and submission to the truth, as the magicians, who had initially been in opposition to Moses, acknowledge the supremacy of his God over their former practices. The act of prostration signifies not just belief but a transformative surrender, showcasing how the truth can lead even the most unlikely individuals to faith. Their declaration highlights the advancement of divine recognition, emphasizing that true worship stems from understanding and acknowledging God's might, as seen in the contrast between the magicians' previous allegiance to sorcery and their newfound faith in the God of Moses and Aaron.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: He said, "Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet from opposite sides and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more enduring."
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation and fear of the Pharaoh in response to the challenge posed by Moses and the belief of the people in the message of monotheism. It showcases the lengths to which tyranny can go to suppress the truth, showing how those in power often resort to intimidation and violence to maintain control. The mention of severe punishments serves as a grim reminder of the consequences faced by those who choose to follow the path of righteousness against oppressive authority. It illustrates the broader theme of the struggle between truth and falsehood, as well as the ultimate sovereignty of divine justice over worldly power.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, 'We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and over Him who created us. So decree whatever you will. Your decree is only in this worldly life.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the defiance of those who deny the truth despite having clear signs and revelations. Their insistence on not prioritizing the divine message demonstrates a profound ignorance of the reality of existence and the Creator. The statement 'Your decree is only in this worldly life' signifies their focus on temporal power and influence, neglecting the ultimate reality of the hereafter. It reveals the arrogance of those who believe they can judge and decide matters of faith based solely on worldly perceptions, failing to recognize the limitations of their own understanding and the consequences of their denial.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins and what we were compelled to do from sorcery. And Allah is the best and everlasting.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound acknowledgment of the sovereignty of God and the believers' recognition of their own shortcomings. It highlights the importance of faith as a means to seek forgiveness for past wrongdoings, particularly those actions that were forced upon them, such as engaging in sorcery, which is often seen as a serious sin. The phrase 'Allah is the best and everlasting' serves as a reminder of God's eternal nature and ultimate supremacy over all things, indicating that reliance on Him is the path to mercy and redemption.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dire consequences of wrongdoing and negligence towards divine guidance. It emphasizes the concept of accountability in the afterlife, illustrating that those who transgress and act unjustly will face eternal punishment. The phrase 'neither die nor live' suggests a state of suffering that is both unbearable and unending, indicating the futility of seeking relief in that condition. It serves as a warning to reflect on one's actions and the importance of striving for righteousness.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds – for those are the highest degrees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of faith coupled with righteous actions. It suggests that individuals who approach Allah in a state of belief and have engaged in good deeds will attain high ranks or status in the Hereafter. The 'highest degrees' indicate a reward that is not only a reflection of their faith but also of their commitment to doing good in their lives. This highlights the concept that true belief in God manifests through actions and that both components are essential for spiritual elevation.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: Gardens of Eternity, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever; and this is the reward of one who purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards awaiting those who strive for spiritual purification and righteousness. The imagery of eternal gardens and flowing rivers signifies ultimate peace, abundance, and a harmonious existence in the afterlife. It highlights the concept that true success and salvation are achieved through personal effort in attaining purity of heart and actions, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of accountability for one's deeds.
orig: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء من تزكى

translation: And We inspired Moses, 'Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued.' Strike for them a dry path through the sea. Do not fear being overtaken, and do not fear.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance provided to Moses during a critical moment of deliverance for the Israelites. The command to travel by night indicates the urgency and need for stealth in order to escape from the pursuing Pharaoh and his army. The instruction to strike a dry path in the sea symbolizes miraculous support from God, emphasizing His power to create a way out of seemingly impossible situations. The reassurance to not fear being overtaken reinforces the theme of trust in divine protection and providence, reminding believers that faith can lead to salvation against overwhelming odds.
orig: ولقد أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي فاضرب لهم طريقا في البحر يبسا لا تخاف دركا ولا تخشى

translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his armies, and the sea covered them as it covered.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine retribution faced by Pharaoh and his armies for their arrogance and oppression of the Israelites. It signifies the power of God in protecting His chosen people and punishing those who defy Him. The mention of the sea serves as a metaphor for absolute defeat and the ultimate triumph of faith over tyranny. It underscores the theme of liberation from oppression, reinforcing the message that those who place their trust in God will ultimately prevail, while tyrants will face dire consequences for their actions.
orig: فأتبعهم فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the detrimental leadership of Pharaoh, who, instead of guiding his people towards righteousness and truth, misled them into ignorance and oppression. It serves as a warning against tyrannical rulers whose influence can corrupt moral and spiritual values in society. The lack of guidance from such a leader emphasizes the responsibility of leaders to be just and to seek the welfare of their people, in contrast to Pharaoh's example of self-interest and tyranny.
orig: وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى

translation: O Children of Israel, We have saved you from your enemy and promised you the side of the right mount, and We sent down to you the manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and guidance towards the Children of Israel by reminding them of their liberation from oppression. It emphasizes the fulfillment of God's promises, as He not only saves them but also provides for their needs through divine sustenance in the form of manna and quails. This serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and faithfulness to God's commands after receiving His blessings.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى

translation: Eat of the good things We have provided for you, and do not transgress therein, lest My anger descend upon you. And whosoever incurs My anger has certainly fallen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming what is pure and good, as bestowed by God, while also warning against excessiveness or transgression in enjoying these provisions. The admonition suggests that failure to adhere to this guidance could lead to divine displeasure and consequences. It highlights the balance between enjoying God's bounty and maintaining obedience to His commandments, signifying that one's actions in response to God's gifts directly impact their standing with Him.
orig: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى

translation: And indeed, I am the Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who genuinely repent and turn back to Him. It highlights the conditions for this forgiveness: true faith, righteous deeds, and maintaining a path of guidance. It reminds believers that no matter the gravity of their past sins, Allah's doors of forgiveness remain open for those who sincerely seek to reform themselves and adhere to a life of righteousness.
orig: وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى

translation: And what has hastened you from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of questioning and accountability. It signifies a divine inquiry regarding Moses' actions and priorities. The question implies that there is a significant expectation for Moses to lead and guide his people, and his absence raises concerns. It also underscores the importance of community and leadership, suggesting that one's responsibilities to their people should not be taken lightly. This moment serves to remind us that even leaders are held accountable for their decisions and the welfare of those they lead.
orig: وما أعجلك عن قومك يا موسى

translation: They are right behind me, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You may be pleased.
interpretation: This verse reflects a sense of urgency and dedication in seeking the approval of God. The speaker expresses a strong commitment to fulfill their responsibilities, indicating they are aware of those who follow them and are eager to reach God's presence. The act of hastening towards God signifies an active pursuit of His favor, showcasing a deep desire for divine acceptance and satisfaction. It illustrates the relationship between a believer and their Creator, emphasizing the importance of intention and the urgency to meet spiritual obligations.
orig: قال هم أولاء على أثري وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

translation: He said, 'Indeed, We have led your people astray after you, and the Samaritan has misled them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of leadership and the responsibility that comes with guiding a community. It reflects how the absence of a strong, righteous leader can lead to chaos and misguidance, as exemplified by the role of the Samaritan who misled the people. The mention of temptation and testing serves to remind believers of the need for vigilance and faithfulness in the face of challenges, and that misguided influences can arise from within the community. It also underscores the importance of accountability for one's actions in relation to others, especially in matters of faith and guidance.
orig: قال فإنا قد فتنا قومك من بعدك وأضلهم السامري

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Did the time period seem too long for you, or did you wish for the anger of your Lord to descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?"
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' deep disappointment and frustration with his people for breaking a covenant with God. It reflects their impatience and lack of faith during his absence, showcasing the challenges of leadership and the consequences of straying from divine guidance. Moses' emotive response illustrates the seriousness of their actions and serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding commitments made to God.
orig: فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال يا قوم ألم يعدكم ربكم وعدا حسنا أفطال عليكم العهد أم أردتم أن يحل عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي

translation: They said, "We did not fail to meet you, but we were burdened with the ornaments of the people, and we threw them in. Thus did the Samaritan cast."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the excuses made by the people of Moses for their actions in his absence. They claim that they were overwhelmed by the distractions and pressures from surrounding influences, represented by the ornaments of the people. The reference to the Samaritan shows the ease with which some individuals can sway the collective group away from guidance, emphasizing the importance of personal responsibility and the potential consequences of yielding to temptation.
orig: قالوا ما أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها فكذلك ألقى السامري

translation: Then he brought out to them a calf, having a body and a mooing sound. They said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses,' but he had forgotten.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the folly of idolatry and the human tendency to turn to false gods in times of uncertainty or weakness. The people, having witnessed the miracles of Moses, still chose to worship an idol, showing how easily one's faith can be swayed. The calf symbolizes the material and sensual desires that can lead one away from the true and unseen God. The phrase 'but he had forgotten' implies a moment of spiritual lapse and lack of awareness, emphasizing the need for constant mindfulness and remembrance of the divine truth.
orig: فأخرج لهم عجلا جسدا له خوار فقالوا هذا إلهكم وإله موسى فنسي

translation: Do they not see that it cannot return to them a word nor possess for them harm or benefit?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of relying on false deities or idols that cannot communicate or provide any real benefit or harm. It invites reflection on the nature of true power and the importance of placing trust in the One who is truly in control of all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of created beings compared to the sovereignty of God, urging individuals to recognize and reject the illusions of power associated with anything besides Him.
orig: أفلا يرون ألا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

translation: And indeed, Aaron had said to them before, 'O my people, you have certainly been wronged by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.'
interpretation: In this verse, the moment captures a pivotal call from Aaron to his people to abandon their misguided worship of the golden calf. His statement reflects the deep concern and responsibility of a leader who wishes to guide his community back to the true worship of God. The mention of God's mercy highlights the hope for redemption and forgiveness, emphasizing that turning back is not just an obligation but a path towards divine mercy. Aaron's plea for obedience underscores the importance of following divinely ordained guidance as a means to escape the consequences of their actions and restore their spiritual integrity.
orig: ولقد قال لهم هارون من قبل يا قوم إنما فتنتم به وإن ربكم الرحمن فاتبعوني وأطيعوا أمري

translation: They said, 'We will not cease being devoted to it until Moses returns to us.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the unwavering commitment of the people to a certain idol or belief, illustrating their misguided loyalty and dependence on a physical representation rather than the true monotheism that Moses preached. It signifies the challenges faced by prophetic figures in guiding their communities away from idolatry and the human tendency to cling to familiar objects or practices in the absence of spiritual leadership. This moment emphasizes the importance of patience and faith during times of uncertainty, as well as the need for guidance and enlightenment from a dedicated messenger of God.
orig: قالوا لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى

translation: He said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray?'
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment of questioning and accountability. It signifies a relationship between leadership and responsibility, where the speaker, likely Moses, confronts Aaron about his failure to intervene when the people deviated from the right path. It emphasizes the importance of guiding others and reflects on the consequences of inaction in the face of wrongdoing. The inquiry serves as a reminder of the moral obligation to stand against misguidance and protect the community from straying.
orig: قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا

translation: Did you not follow me? Did you disobey my command?
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of accountability and confrontation, emphasizing the importance of obedience and adherence to guidance. It highlights the consequences of turning away from instruction, suggesting a deeper exploration of the relationship between authority and responsibility. The questioning tone indicates disappointment and a call for self-reflection regarding the decisions made in the face of leadership or divine command.
orig: ألا تتبعن أفعصيت أمري

translation: He said, 'O my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of vulnerability and accountability. Moses, when confronted about his actions, expresses his deep concern for the perception of his leadership among his people and the consequences of miscommunication. His plea not to seize him symbolizes a desire for understanding rather than judgment. It highlights the weight of leadership and the anxiety that comes with the responsibility of guiding a community, stressing the importance of maintaining unity and conveying truth in the face of challenges.
orig: قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

translation: He said, 'So what is the matter with you, O Samiri?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of confrontation and inquiry, highlighting the interaction between Moses and Samiri. It signifies a critical point where accountability is at stake, as Moses seeks to understand the motives behind Samiri's actions. The question suggests an invitation to reflection on one's choices and the consequences of straying from a righteous path, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and truthfulness in faith.
orig: قال فما خطبك يا سامري

translation: He said, 'I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger and I threw it away, and thus my soul made fair-seeming to me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of weakness and misguidance, where the speaker justifies his actions by claiming a vision of something unseen to others, suggesting a false sense of superiority or knowledge. The act of taking a handful from the trace of the Messenger symbolizes a desire for something sacred or significant, yet throwing it away reveals a choice to abandon true guidance for self-deception. This highlights the conflict between divine guidance and personal inclination, illustrating how one's desires can lead to misjudgment and the rejection of profound truths.
orig: قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي

translation: He said, "Go! For you have in life that you will say, 'No touching!' and indeed, you have an appointment which you will not fail to meet. And look at your god to which you remain devoted; we will surely burn it and then we will surely scatter it in the sea, scattering."
interpretation: This verse reflects the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, emphasizing the futility of idolatry. The command to go implies a directive for Moses to continue his mission against Pharaoh's tyranny. The phrase 'No touching!' can symbolize a separation from the unworthy or impure, indicating a repudiation of false worship. The mention of 'your god' highlights the falsehood of Pharaoh's idol worship, and the intent to burn and scatter it signifies the inevitable downfall of false gods in the face of true divine authority. Ultimately, this verse underscores the theme of the triumph of monotheism over polytheism and the destructiveness of idolatry.
orig: قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا

translation: Your God is but one God. There is no deity except Him. He has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of monotheism, asserting the uniqueness and oneness of God. It highlights that there is no other deity worthy of worship except Him. The mention of God's omniscience ('He has encompassed all things in knowledge') serves to remind believers of God's complete understanding and control over all aspects of creation, which reinforces His supreme authority and the importance of turning to Him in faith and reliance.
orig: إنما إلهكم الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وسع كل شيء علما

translation: Thus We recount to you some of the news of what has happened before, and We have certainly given you from Us a Reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of historical narratives, showcasing that learning from past events is essential for guidance in the present. The mention of 'Reminder' signifies that these stories serve a purpose beyond mere storytelling; they are lessons intended to reinforce faith and inspire moral reflection. It highlights the continuity of divine communication throughout history, indicating that the wisdom and messages conveyed are not new but rather part of a consistent, ongoing revelation meant to assist humanity in understanding their path and responsibilities.
orig: كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا

translation: Whoever turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of neglecting the message of the Qur'an. It serves as a warning that turning away from divine guidance leads to spiritual burdens and responsibilities that one must carry in the Hereafter. The term 'burden' signifies not only the weight of one's actions but also the regret and accountability one faces for abandoning the truth. This reflects the importance of engaging with divine teachings and the moral imperative to understand and follow them to avoid grave consequences on the Day of Judgment.
orig: من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا

translation: They will abide therein, and wretched is the load for them on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence of the consequences faced by those who have turned away from righteousness. It illustrates the burden they will carry, not just in the afterlife but as a reflection of their choices and actions in this world. The mention of a 'wretched load' suggests the immense regret and suffering they will experience on the Day of Judgment, underlining the serious consequences of one's decisions and the importance of leading a life aligned with moral and spiritual values.
orig: خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا

translation: The Day the Horn is blown, and We will gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse vividly depicts the day of resurrection when the Horn is blown, marking the end of the world and the beginning of accountability. The gathering of criminals described as having 'blue eyes' symbolizes a state of despondency and fear, highlighting their culpability and the consequences of their actions in the worldly life. It serves as a reminder of the reality of divine justice and the inevitable result of one's deeds, emphasizing the stark transformation from life to the afterlife.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

translation: They whisper to one another, "You have remained but ten (days)."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of quiet communication among the people who are likely concerned or anxious about the situation they find themselves in. It suggests a sense of disbelief or intrigue about the time spent, emphasizing how fleeting worldly time can appear under certain circumstances. This interaction illustrates human tendencies to seek reassurance and clarity, even in disorientation, highlighting the importance of time perception in shaping one's experience and reality.
orig: يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

translation: We know very well what they say when their best among them says, "You have only remained for a day."
interpretation: This verse highlights the knowledge and awareness of Allah regarding the conversations and thoughts of people, particularly during moments of doubt or denial about the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that even in their skepticism, the truth about the duration of life after death and the reality of resurrection is apparent. It suggests a theme of accountability and the brevity of worldly existence compared to the eternal truth of the hereafter.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما

translation: And they ask you about the mountains. Say, 'My Lord will blow them away with a blast.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly things, including mountains, which are often seen as unchanging and permanent. It underscores the power of God to transform and obliterate even the most steadfast elements of creation. The mention of God’s ability to ‘blow them away’ serves as a reminder of His ultimate authority and control over the universe, encouraging believers to reflect on the temporary nature of earthly life and the permanence of the hereafter.
orig: ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا

translation: So it will be left a level, smooth plain.
interpretation: This verse suggests imagery of destruction or transformation, where once there may have been life, activity, or structures, it is now reduced to a barren, flat landscape. It can symbolize the consequences of moral decay, divine punishment, or the impermanence of worldly affairs, highlighting that ultimately, all things of this world will face demise and what remains is a stark reminder of accountability and the fleeting nature of human existence.
orig: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا

translation: You will see no crookedness in it nor any expanse.
interpretation: This verse suggests the perfection and straightness of the design created by God in paradise. It indicates that there will be no flaws, deviations, or imperfections in the beauty and layout of paradise, contrasting it with worldly experiences where one might encounter flaws or irregularities. The focus is on the idea of ultimate harmony and balance in the afterlife, where everything is in its rightful place and completely fulfilling God's promise of a perfect abode for the righteous.
orig: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا

translation: On that Day, they will follow the caller with no deviation, and the voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment when people will be fully attentive to the call of truth, following it without deviation or distraction. The imagery of humbled voices signifies the profound awe and submission before Allah, the Most Merciful, illustrating the overwhelming presence of His majesty. The mention of only hearing whispers emphasizes the gravity of the moment, where every individual is focused, reflecting on their actions and standing before their Creator, stripped of pretense and superficial noise.
orig: يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا

translation: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except for one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose word He accepts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of God on the Day of Judgment and the specific conditions under which intercession can take place. It highlights that only those who have been granted permission by God and whose intercession aligns with His will are allowed to intercede on behalf of others. This underscores the idea that ultimate authority and judgment belong to God alone, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking His pleasure and aligning one's words and actions with His will.
orig: يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge of Allah, highlighting that His understanding encompasses all that exists, both in the past and the future. It reflects the idea that human knowledge is limited and inadequate in comparison to the divine wisdom of Allah, underscoring the importance of humility in the face of His omniscience.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما

translation: And the faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence; and whoever carries injustice will certainly be disappointed.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate humbling of humanity before Allah, the Ever-Living and Sustainer. It implies a moment of reckoning where one's true condition is revealed, emphasizing that all power and existence depend on Allah alone. The latter part serves as a warning that those who act unjustly or oppress others will face dire consequences and disappointment. It reinforces the principle of accountability for one's actions, highlighting the significance of justice and righteousness in life.
orig: وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: This verse reinforces the idea that true belief in God manifests itself through righteous actions. It assures believers that their good deeds, coupled with faith, will protect them from the injustices and inequities of the world. It highlights a fundamental principle in Islam: that faith and good actions are intrinsically linked and provide a sense of security and hope in the face of life's trials.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have detailed therein from warning that perhaps they will fear or it will cause them a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the intentionality behind the revelation of the Qur'an as an Arabic text, catering to the linguistic and cultural context of its audience. The 'warning' mentioned indicates that the Qur'an serves as a means to instill consciousness of one's actions and their consequences. It suggests that the purpose of this divine communication is to invoke a sense of fear that leads to piety and reverence, and to prompt reflection on one's behavior and the reminders inherent in the teachings of the Qur'an. The dual approach of warning and remembrance highlights the balance in the Qur'anic message, aimed at guiding humanity towards righteousness.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا

translation: So exalted is Allah, the True King. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you. And say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the greatness and supremacy of Allah as the ultimate sovereign. It reminds believers to be patient and not rush the process of revelation, suggesting that understanding and guidance come at their own pace through divine will. Additionally, it encourages a spirit of seeking knowledge, highlighting that true wisdom and insight stem from continuous learning and a humble request for Allah's guidance.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما

translation: And We had certainly taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.
interpretation: This verse reflects the nature of human forgetfulness and the inherent frailty of human resolve. It highlights that even a foundational figure like Adam, who was entrusted with a covenant, fell short due to forgetfulness. This can be seen as a reminder of the limitations of human strength and willpower, and it underscores the importance of persistence and mindfulness in upholding one's commitments and responsibilities. It suggests that forgetfulness is part of the human condition, and that one must strive to remember and act with determination in the face of challenges.
orig: ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except for Iblis; he refused.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of humility and obedience to divine command. The angels' willingness to prostrate to Adam symbolizes their recognition of God's creation and authority. In contrast, Iblis's refusal reflects pride and disobedience, highlighting the moral struggle of free will in choosing to follow God's directives. This event sets the stage for understanding the nature of sin and the consequences of rebellion against God’s will.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى

translation: So We said, 'O Adam, indeed this [devil] is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not remove you from Paradise, so you would suffer.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the direct warning given to Adam about the enmity of the devil and the consequences of yielding to temptation. It signifies the dangers of succumbing to external influences that can lead one astray, emphasizing the importance of vigilance in protecting one's spiritual state. Additionally, it illustrates the interconnectedness between Adam and his wife, portraying their unity in the face of adversity. The mention of suffering implies that disobedience leads to hardship, thereby urging adherence to divine guidance.
orig: فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى

translation: Indeed, you will not hunger therein, nor will you be naked.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the state of abundance and comfort in Paradise. It reflects God's promise of eternal satisfaction and security for the believers. The mention of not experiencing hunger or nakedness symbolizes the removal of physical and emotional suffering, illustrating the complete fulfillment and grace that awaits the faithful in the afterlife.
orig: إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى

translation: And you will not suffer from thirst there, nor from heat.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea of comfort and abundance in the afterlife, specifically in Paradise. The mention of not experiencing thirst or heat symbolizes the absence of hardship, struggle, and suffering that one might face in the earthly life. It is a reassurance to the faithful that their sacrifices and patience will be rewarded with a state of existence free from physical discomfort, reflecting God's mercy and care for those who strive in His path.
orig: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى

translation: Then Satan whispered to him, saying, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and to a kingdom that will not deteriorate?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive nature of Satan as he preys on Adam’s curiosity and desire for permanence. The phrase 'tree of eternity' symbolizes an alluring temptation that promises immortality and unending power, which contrasts with the transient nature of human existence. It highlights the idea that temptations often come disguised as beneficial or attractive offers, enticing individuals to abandon divine commandments. The verse serves as a reminder of the struggle between following divine guidance and succumbing to misleading whispers that seek to lead one away from righteousness.
orig: فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى

translation: So they ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. Thus did Adam disobey his Lord, and he erred.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of human vulnerability and the consequences of disobedience. Adam and Eve's act of eating from the forbidden tree led to their realization of their nakedness, symbolizing awareness and loss of innocence. Their attempt to cover themselves with leaves represents the instinctual response to shame and guilt that arises from moral failing. This act of disobedience not only signifies a turning point in their existence but also highlights the human condition of erring and the inherent struggles with temptation and moral judgment. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of choices and the journey toward seeking forgiveness and understanding one's own nature.
orig: فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وعصى آدم ربه فغوى

translation: Then his Lord chose him and turned towards him and guided him.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine process of guidance and repentance. It emphasizes that ultimately, it is Allah who chooses individuals for His mercy and guidance. The phrase 'turned towards him' indicates a personal relationship where Allah accepts repentance, suggesting that regardless of past transgressions, sincere repentance is always welcomed. Furthermore, the act of being guided reflects Allah's support in leading individuals towards righteousness after they have sought His forgiveness. This reinforces the concept of hope and redemption in Islam, showing that one can always return to a path of faith.
orig: ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى

translation: He said, "Descend from it, all of you. Some of you are the enemies of others. But if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be miserable."
interpretation: This verse addresses the human condition after the initial transgression. The directive to 'descend' signifies the beginning of human life on Earth, where enmity between individuals is acknowledged as a consequence of the fall. The verse highlights the importance of divine guidance as a path to avoid going astray and experiencing misery. It emphasizes that adhering to God's guidance leads to fulfillment and protection from despair, suggesting that the key to overcoming the struggles of existence lies in a conscious and active relationship with divine instruction.
orig: قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of neglecting the remembrance of God. It indicates that turning away from divine guidance leads to a life characterized by hardship and spiritual deprivation. The imagery of being 'gathered blind' on the Day of Resurrection highlights the idea of spiritual blindness resulting from a lack of faith and awareness of God's presence in one's life. It suggests that this negligence not only affects one's current life but also has repercussions in the hereafter, where one is deprived of the ability to see the truth and guidance that was accessible during their earthly existence.
orig: ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى

translation: He said, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the anguish and confusion of an individual who, after being resurrected, is confronted with a state of blindness despite having had the capability of sight in their previous life. It raises profound questions about divine justice, the nature of human existence, and the implications of one's actions in life. The individual is grappling with the consequences of their choices, suggesting a deeper reflection on one’s responsibilities and the realization that one's life choices can lead to eternal implications. It serves as a reminder of accountability in the Hereafter and the transformative nature of the life of this world compared to the afterlife.
orig: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

translation: Thus Our verses came to you, but you forgot them; and likewise, today you will be forgotten.
interpretation: This verse reflects the consequences of neglecting the signs and messages from God. It emphasizes the state of being forgetful, both in the earthly life and in the hereafter. Those who disregard divine guidance during their lives will find themselves forgotten and abandoned by God on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a warning about the importance of being mindful of God's revelations and the accountability that comes with ignoring them.
orig: قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

translation: And thus do We reward whoever transgresses and does not believe in the verses of his Lord; and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and everlasting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences faced by those who exceed the limits set by God and fail to acknowledge His signs. It reminds believers that transgression is not taken lightly and that the consequences in the afterlife are not only more intense but also eternal. This serves as a warning to instill consciousness about one's actions and beliefs, urging individuals to reflect on their accountability in the sight of God.
orig: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى

translation: Did they not see how many nations We destroyed before them, walking in their dwellings? Indeed, in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder for individuals to reflect on the fate of past communities that were destroyed due to their transgressions. It emphasizes the importance of learning from history and recognizing the consequences of actions. The mention of 'those of understanding' highlights that true comprehension comes from reflecting on divine signs and the lessons embedded in the past. It calls for contemplation, urging believers to take heed of the outcomes faced by previous generations, thereby encouraging a lifestyle aligned with divine guidance to avoid similar fates.
orig: أفلم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: And if it had not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord, [punishment] would have been obligatory and a specified time set.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and wisdom of Allah in delaying punishment for disbelievers and wrongdoers. It suggests that Allah has predetermined a time and context for every event, showing that His decisions are guided by knowledge and justice. The mention of a 'word' from Allah indicates that divine decrees exist, preempting immediate recompense, thus highlighting the balance between divine justice and mercy in the unfolding of events in the world.
orig: ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى

translation: So be patient over what they say and glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and in the hours of the night, and at the ends of the day, perhaps you will be pleased.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of criticism or negativity from others, encouraging believers to maintain a strong connection with their faith through the worship of God. The specific timing of glorifying God reflects a structured approach to devotion and remembrance, inviting individuals to find peace and contentment in their spiritual practice. The notion of pleasing God indicates that spiritual fulfillment and personal satisfaction can be cultivated through consistent acts of worship and resilience against adversity.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. And the provision of your Lord is better and everlasting.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to not covet the temporary pleasures and material wealth that others possess, as these are merely tests designed to distract us from our true purpose. The 'splendor of the worldly life' is transient and can lead one astray if they become too attached to it. In contrast, what God provides is described as 'better and everlasting,' indicating that spiritual fulfillment, righteous actions, and the rewards of the Hereafter are far superior to any ephemeral enjoyment in this life. The verse encourages believers to focus on their relationship with God and the everlasting rewards that come with it, rather than being lured by the superficial attractions of this world.
orig: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى

translation: And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast therein. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good end is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prayer, not just as a personal duty but as a family obligation. It highlights the need for patience in maintaining this practice, indicating that such perseverance in worship will yield spiritual rewards. Furthermore, it reassures believers that Allah is the provider of sustenance, freeing them from the anxiety about worldly provisions. Instead, they are encouraged to focus on their responsibilities towards worship and righteousness, with the ultimate outcome favoring those who are conscious of Allah.
orig: وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى

translation: And they said, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' Had there not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures?
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and demand for miraculous signs from the messengers of Allah. It emphasizes the notion that those who reject divine messages often seek tangible proof while overlooking the established truths revealed in previous scriptures. The rhetorical question serves to remind them that prior revelations already contain clear guidance, suggesting that faith should be built on understanding and accepting the messages already given rather than incessantly seeking new signs. It reflects a deeper theme of faith versus disbelief, underscoring the responsibility of individuals to reflect upon and recognize the evidence of truth that surrounds them.
orig: وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to blame divine justice when faced with calamity. It reflects the idea that when people are confronted with their own accountability, they may regret not having received guidance, underscoring the importance of messengers as a means of divine communication. It illustrates the necessity of spiritual awareness and the responsibilities of individuals to heed the teachings sent to them, as well as the consequences of ignoring such guidance. The verse serves as a reminder that guidance is provided as a mercy, and recognizing it is crucial to avoiding disgrace in the hereafter.
orig: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى

translation: Say, "All [those who] await [our outcome], so await. Indeed, you will know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of patience and waiting for the truth to manifest. It encourages individuals to observe and reflect on the results of their choices and actions over time. The promise of knowing who truly follows the righteous path and who is rightly guided serves as a reminder that guidance is ultimately revealed through one's perseverance and the outcomes that follow. It suggests a contrast between those who wait and the eventual realization of their respective standings in relation to divine guidance.
orig: قل كل متربص فتربصوا فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى

translation: The time of reckoning has drawn near for mankind, while they are in heedlessness, turning away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the imminent arrival of the Day of Judgment, which serves as a reminder for people to be aware and conscious of their actions. The contrast between the closeness of this significant event and the state of heedlessness in which many find themselves highlights human tendencies to ignore spiritual responsibilities and warnings. It calls for reflection on one's life choices and encourages a sense of urgency in seeking righteousness before it is too late.
orig: اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون

translation: No reminder comes to them from their Lord that is newly revealed except that they listen to it while they are playing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the indifference and distraction of certain individuals towards the divine messages being conveyed to them. Despite the profound significance of the reminders from God, they are preoccupied with trivial pursuits, represented here as 'playing.' This signifies a lack of seriousness or consideration for spiritual matters, emphasizing the tendency of some people to disregard important truths in favor of fleeting pleasures and distractions. The mention of 'newly revealed' also suggests that divine guidance is continuous and evolving, yet still ignored by those who choose not to engage with it meaningfully.
orig: ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

translation: Their hearts are distracted, and they secretly converse. Those who have wronged say, 'Is this anything but a human being like yourselves? Will you approach magic while you are witnesses?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and denial faced by the Prophet Muhammad and the revelations he brought. It highlights the hearts of the disbelievers being preoccupied with distractions, which leads them to dismiss the divine message as mere magic or deception. The verse emphasizes their refusal to recognize the truth of the message because of their bias and misunderstanding, portraying a broader human tendency to resist new ideas that challenge established beliefs.
orig: لاهية قلوبهم وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم أفتأتون السحر وأنتم تبصرون

translation: My Lord knows the saying in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting that He is fully aware of all spoken words and thoughts, whether they are uttered openly or kept secret. The inclusion of both 'the heavens and the earth' indicates that His knowledge encompasses all of creation. The terms 'All-Hearing' and 'All-Knowing' reinforce His attributes of never overlooking anything, suggesting that every speech and thought is acknowledged and understood by Him. This serves as a reminder of divine accountability, underscoring the importance of sincerity in one's words and actions.
orig: قال ربي يعلم القول في السماء والأرض وهو السميع العليم

translation: But they said, 'These are but mixed dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign, as the former messengers were sent with signs.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of those who rejected the message of the Prophet. They dismiss the revelations as mere confusion or fabrications, rather than recognizing their truth and divine origin. Their demand for a sign reflects a common challenge posed to prophets, showcasing a lack of faith and understanding. It illustrates the human tendency to question divine messages and the delays in acknowledging prophetic authority, while also underscoring the importance of faith beyond mere signs or miracles.
orig: بل قالوا أضغاث أحلام بل افتراه بل هو شاعر فليأتنا بآية كما أرسل الأولون

translation: No community believed before them that we destroyed; so will they believe?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine punishment for disbelief and serves as a reminder that past civilizations faced destruction for rejecting the messages of their prophets. It raises a rhetorical question about the likelihood of contemporary communities embracing faith in light of historical evidence of consequences faced by those who refused to believe. The verse suggests a continuity in human behavior, indicating that the signs and warnings have often gone unheeded, and begs the current audience to reflect on their own faith in the face of such precedents.
orig: ما آمنت قبلهم من قرية أهلكناها أفهم يؤمنون

translation: And We did not send before you any except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle that God has always sent human messengers to guide humanity, emphasizing that they are relatable and can convey divine messages authentically. It encourages seeking knowledge from those who possess it ('the people of remembrance'), suggesting the importance of consultation and learning from others, especially when one lacks understanding. This also underscores the value of scholarship and religious authority in interpreting the scriptures and living a life aligned with divine guidance.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, nor were they eternal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity and mortality of certain beings, highlighting that they are not beyond the natural human condition of needing sustenance and are subject to death. It serves to remind the reader that, unlike divine entities, all beings, including prophets and other revered figures, are created with physical needs and limitations. This underscores the fundamental aspect of human existence, which is tied to reliance on nourishment and the inherent temporary nature of life.
orig: وما جعلناهم جسدا لا يأكلون الطعام وما كانوا خالدين

translation: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, so We saved them and those whom We willed, and We destroyed the evildoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine justice and mercy. It emphasizes that God's promises are fulfilled, particularly in delivering those who are faithful and righteous, while also indicating that those who transgress and cause corruption will face consequences. The distinction between those who are saved and those who are punished suggests a moral order in the world where faithfulness leads to salvation and wrongdoing results in destruction. The phrase 'and those whom We willed' signifies God's sovereign choice in determining who receives mercy, reinforcing the belief in His ultimate authority and wisdom.
orig: ثم صدقناهم الوعد فأنجيناهم ومن نشاء وأهلكنا المسرفين

translation: We have sent down to you a Book in which is your mention. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a divine revelation that contains guidance and remembrance for humanity. It calls upon individuals to reflect on its teachings and meaning, urging them to engage with the text intellectually and spiritually. The phrase 'in which is your mention' suggests that the Qur'an addresses fundamental aspects of human existence, moral guidance, and the purpose of life, prompting believers to consider their relationship with God and their responsibilities towards each other in society.
orig: لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون

translation: And how many a city that was unjust have We destroyed, and We raised up after it another people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of justice and accountability. It reflects the recurring theme in the Qur'an of the rise and fall of communities based on their moral choices. Cities or societies that engage in oppression and wrongdoing ultimately face destruction, while new communities arise that may learn from the past. This serves as a warning and a reminder for people to remain righteous and just in their dealings, as the consequences of injustice are severe, not only for individuals but for entire societies.
orig: وكم قصمنا من قرية كانت ظالمة وأنشأنا بعدها قوما آخرين

translation: But when they felt Our torment, here they ran from it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of panic and fear when people confront the consequences of their actions. It signifies a natural human response to danger, emphasizing the futility of escaping divine retribution. The act of running symbolizes a denial or avoidance of accountability, highlighting the theme that one cannot flee from the consequences of their deeds. Ultimately, it serves as a reminder of the seriousness of heeding warnings and the urgency of repentance before it is too late.
orig: فلما أحسوا بأسنا إذا هم منها يركضون

translation: Do not rush; return to what you have been given to enjoy and your dwellings, perhaps you will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transience of worldly pleasures and comforts. It suggests that in moments of crisis or urgency, one should not hastily abandon the foundational aspects of life that they have enjoyed. The call to return implies a reflection on one's previous state of being and a contemplation of the blessings they previously took for granted. The mention of being questioned serves as a warning of accountability, encouraging individuals to consider their actions and the consequences they may face, urging them to seek understanding and mindfulness regarding their choices and their relationship with God's blessings.
orig: لا تركضوا وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه ومساكنكم لعلكم تسألون

translation: They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of recognition and regret among individuals who have realized the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'woe to us' signifies deep despair and remorse, acknowledging the wrongs they have committed. This moment serves as a profound reminder of the importance of justice and morality, as well as the inevitable accountability that follows one's actions. It emphasizes the theme of personal responsibility and the awakening of consciousness to one's misdeeds, which often leads to a quest for forgiveness and redemption.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: So their claim continued until We made them like a harvest, extinguished.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate consequence of persistent disbelief and denial of the truth. The term 'حصيدا' (harvest) suggests that they were reduced to something lifeless, emphasizing that their actions led to their own destruction. The imagery of being 'extinguished' reinforces the idea of punishment and the finality of their fate, serving as a warning to those who persist in falsehood and neglect the divine guidance.
orig: فما زالت تلك دعواهم حتى جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and whatever is between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness and purposefulness of creation. It conveys that the universe is not merely a place for trivial pursuits or idle play, but is part of a divine plan with profound significance. It invites reflection on the existence and the responsibilities of human beings within this vast creation, hinting at the idea that life should be lived with intention and awareness of a greater purpose beyond mere amusement.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: If We had intended to take a pastime, We could have taken it from what is with Us, if We were to do so.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the majesty and sovereignty of God, illustrating that if He desired to engage in amusement or entertainment, He could easily fabricate it from His infinite power. The statement also highlights the seriousness of God's intention in creation and His purposeful nature, as He does not indulge in trivial pursuits. It serves to remind believers of the divine seriousness behind God's actions and to understand that His will and purpose are beyond mere amusement.
orig: لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا لاتخذناه من لدنا إن كنا فاعلين

translation: But We hurl the truth at falsehood, and it crushes it; and thereupon it departs. And woe to you for what you describe.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It emphasizes that no matter how entrenched or powerful falsehood may seem, when confronted by the absolute and divine truth, it will be invalidated and destroyed. The imagery of hurling truth implies an active and forceful engagement against falsehood, suggesting that truth does not passively exist but rather asserts itself against misconceptions. The warning of 'woe' serves as a caution for those who distort or misrepresent reality, highlighting the serious consequences of such actions.
orig: بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق ولكم الويل مما تصفون

translation: And to Him belongs whosoever is in the heavens and the earth, and those who are near Him do not disdain His worship nor do they tire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal nature of God's sovereignty over all beings in the heavens and the earth. It conveys that all creatures, whether near to God in proximity or in allegiance, approach Him without arrogance and do not grow weary in worship. This serves to emphasize the unwavering devotion of the angels and other celestial beings, who are always engaged in the worship of God. It encourages believers to emulate this dedication and humility in their own worship and to recognize the importance of submitting to the will of God, as even the most exalted beings do so without reluctance.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون

translation: They glorify Him night and day, they do not slacking.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuous and unwavering devotion of certain beings—often understood to refer to angels or celestial beings—who are engaged in the act of glorifying Allah at all times, without fatigue or interruption. It highlights the concept of perpetual worship and servitude, suggesting that true devotion does not tire or sleep. This can serve as a reminder for believers of the importance of steadfastness in their own acts of worship, encouraging them to strive for consistency and sincerity in their relationship with Allah.
orig: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth, who can raise [the dead]?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of polytheism by questioning the ability of earthly entities to possess divine attributes such as power over life and death. It emphasizes the futility of relying on created beings as gods, highlighting that true divinity lies solely with Allah, who alone has the power to create and resurrect. It serves as a reminder of the limitations of creation compared to the majesty and authority of the Creator.
orig: أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون

translation: If there had been in them any gods except Allah, they would have certainly been in a state of ruin. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah and the impossibility of the existence of multiple deities. If there were other gods alongside Allah, the harmony of the universe would be disrupted due to conflicting wills and powers. The verse calls for recognizing the greatness and uniqueness of Allah, who is above any flawed descriptions attributed to Him by those who misinterpret divine nature.
orig: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: He will not be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of God over all creation. It suggests that God's actions are beyond any form of accountability or inquiry from humans, who often question divine decrees or the nature of life. In contrast, humans are accountable for their actions and will be questioned about their deeds on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder of the limitations of human understanding and the importance of faith and submission to God's will.
orig: لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, "Bring your proof. This is the mention of those with me and the mention of those before me. But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away."
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of taking other deities apart from Allah and challenges those who do so to provide their evidence. It highlights the importance of knowledge and truth, indicating that many individuals are oblivious to the reality of monotheism and the oneness of God. The response implies a need for introspection and acceptance of divine guidance, emphasizing that ignorance of the truth leads to spiritual denial.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة قل هاتوا برهانكم هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون

translation: And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistent message of monotheism across all prophets sent by God. It highlights the fundamental principle of Islam: the oneness of God (Tawhid) and the call to worship Him alone. The repetition of this core message through various prophets signifies its importance and the unchanging nature of divine guidance. It also serves as a reminder that despite the varying contexts and cultures, the essence of the message remains the same, urging humanity to turn towards God in worship and obedience.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

translation: And they said, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are but honored servants.
interpretation: This verse addresses the erroneous belief held by some that Allah, the Most Merciful, has a son. The strong negation 'Exalted is He!' emphasizes the transcendence of Allah above human concepts of parentage and lineage. Instead, it reaffirms that the beings referred to are not divine but rather honored servants of Allah, highlighting the distinction between the Creator and His creation. This serves to underline the importance of monotheism and the honor of being a servant to the divine rather than elevating beings to a status of divinity.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون

translation: They do not speak before Him, and they act by His command.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah over His creation. It emphasizes that the angels, who are tasked with carrying out His commands, do not act independently or precede Him in speech. Their actions are fully aligned with His will, reflecting a perfect obedience and subservience. This serves as a reminder to humans of the need for humility and submission to divine guidance, as well as the importance of recognizing the power and knowledge of Allah, who knows all that is in the hearts of His creation.
orig: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one with whom He is pleased, and they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute knowledge and sovereignty of God, emphasizing that He is aware of all that humanity has done and will do. The mention of intercession indicates that such an act is reserved for those whom God chooses, reflecting His mercy and authority. Additionally, the fear expressed by those who act as intercessors underscores their reverence for God's power, showing that even they are not exempt from accountability and remain humble before Him.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون

translation: And whoever of them says, 'Indeed, I am a deity besides Him' - for that one We will confer Hellfire. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of associating partners with Allah, highlighting that such a belief and declaration is met with dire consequences in the afterlife. It underscores the idea that wrongdoing, especially in the context of divinity and worship, has a specific and severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning against the arrogance and injustice of declaring oneself as a deity or counterpart to Allah, reminding believers of the importance of sincere monotheism and the repercussions of misguiding beliefs.
orig: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a closed-up mass, then We opened them out? And We made every living thing from water. Will they not then believe?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the creation of the universe, highlighting the initial state of the heavens and the earth as a unified mass before God separated them. It underscores the miraculous nature of creation and the role of water as the source of life, suggesting that the complexity and interdependence of nature should lead one to recognize the signs of God. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the expectation that such profound revelations should compel disbelief to give way to belief.
orig: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون

translation: And We have set on the earth mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We have made therein broad highways, that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's provisions for humanity, showcasing His mercy and wisdom. The reference to mountains signifies stability and prevents the shaking of the earth, symbolizing the foundational support that sustains human life. The mention of pathways indicates guidance and direction, as these routes facilitate travel and exploration, allowing people to seek knowledge and connect with one another. Overall, the verse reflects the harmony of creation, illustrating how the natural world is structured to support and guide human existence towards a purposeful life.
orig: وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بهم وجعلنا فيها فجاجا سبلا لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We made the heaven a protected canopy, and they, from its signs, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the greatness of God's creation, specifically referring to the sky as a 'protected canopy' that serves both physical and metaphysical purposes. The 'protection' can be understood as the sky safeguarding the earth from various cosmic threats, while metaphorically, it alludes to the divine signs and manifestations of God's power that are often overlooked by people. The phrase 'they are turning away' signifies a willful neglect or rejection of these signs and truths, reflecting human tendency to ignore what is evident due to distractions or disbelief. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being aware of and reflective upon the natural world and its connection to faith.
orig: وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون

translation: And He it is who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; all (the celestial bodies) are swimming along in their orbit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authority and creativity of God in establishing the cycles of time and the celestial bodies. The phrase 'each in an orbit' suggests not only their physical movement but also a sense of order and purpose in the universe, indicative of God's wisdom. It serves to remind believers of the intricate design of creation, urging them to reflect on the greatness of God and the signs surrounding them which point to His existence and sovereignty over all that exists.
orig: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر كل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And We did not grant immortality to any human before you. So if you die, will they be eternal?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death for all beings, including the Prophet Muhammad. It serves as a reminder that mortality is a fundamental aspect of human existence and that no one has been granted eternal life. This calls believers to reflect on their own lives and the temporary nature of worldly existence, highlighting the importance of preparing for the hereafter rather than being attached to this fleeting life.
orig: وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد أفإن مت فهم الخالدون

translation: Every soul will taste death, and We test you with evil and good as a trial; and to Us, you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death for every individual, underscoring the transient nature of worldly existence. The mention of being tested with both good and evil highlights that life is a series of trials meant to assess one's character and faith. Ultimately, it reminds believers that all will return to God, suggesting accountability and the importance of how one lives their life amidst these tests.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة وإلينا ترجعون

translation: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], 'Is this the one who mentions your gods, and in their mention is the Most Merciful?' And they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mockery and disdain that disbelievers express towards the message of Islam and its messenger. It illustrates how they trivialize the Prophet Muhammad by questioning his legitimacy and the seriousness of his teachings. Their scorn stems from their disbelief in the concept of the One God, particularly the nature of Allah as 'the Most Merciful.' The verse emphasizes the conflict between faith and disbelief, showcasing the arrogance of those who reject divine guidance.
orig: وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون

translation: Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not hasten.
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate tendency of human beings to seek immediate answers and results, indicating a natural impatience in our nature. It serves as a reminder from God to trust in His timing and to be patient as we await His signs and manifestations in our lives. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to understand that divine wisdom may not always align with human urgency.
orig: خلق الإنسان من عجل سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be among the truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of those who doubt the prophecies or promises made by the believers about the Day of Judgment or other divine occurrences. It emphasizes the challenge posed by the disbelievers, who demand tangible evidence for what they perceive as future events. The verse serves to highlight the contrast between faith and skepticism, urging believers to maintain their conviction in the truth of God's promises despite the doubts expressed by others.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not be able to avert the Fire from their faces or their backs, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound consequences of disbelief, emphasizing a looming reality where those who reject faith will find themselves helpless in the face of divine retribution. It underscores the certainty of punishment and the futility of trying to escape it. The imagery of not being able to protect oneself from the Fire illustrates the intensity of the suffering and the lack of support or aid at that moment, serving as a warning for reflection and a call to faith before it's too late.
orig: لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم ولا هم ينصرون

translation: But it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, so they will not be able to repel it nor will they be given any respite.
interpretation: This verse highlights the suddenness and inevitability of divine retribution. It signifies that when the moment of accountability arrives, those who were heedless will be caught off guard and unable to respond. The state of bewilderment indicates a lack of preparedness for the consequences of their actions, emphasizing the urgency of being aware and vigilant in one's conduct. It serves as a reminder that awareness of accountability should influence behavior, as the end can arrive unexpectedly.
orig: بل تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم فلا يستطيعون ردها ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but there came upon those who mocked them that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences faced by those who mock or belittle the messengers of God. It highlights a historical pattern where the messengers faced ridicule from their communities, but ultimately, those who scoffed experienced a turnaround in fate, facing the reality of their denials and mockeries. The verse stresses the seriousness of disbelief and warns against the arrogance of those who refuse to accept divine truth, reinforcing the notion that such mockery leads to dire repercussions.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, 'Who can protect you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?' But they are not in any mention of their Lord, turning away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine protection and care, highlighting the omnipresence of Allah as the Most Merciful. It underscores the futility of relying on other forces for protection in contrast to the assurance of Allah's guardianship.
