The latter part of the verse points out the neglect of individuals regarding the remembrance of their Lord, suggesting that those who turn away from spiritual remembrance not only miss out on divine protection but also fall into a state of heedlessness. It serves as a reminder for believers to recognize and acknowledge Allah's mercy and to remain aware of their relationship with Him.
orig: قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون

translation: Or do they have gods that can protect them from Us? They cannot even help themselves, nor can they be supported by Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of relying on false deities for protection and support. It highlights the utter helplessness of those who place their faith in anything other than God, illustrating that these entities cannot provide assistance in times of need. The verse serves as a reminder of God's ultimate power and sovereignty, affirming that no one can intercede for those who are against His will, as they cannot even defend themselves.
orig: أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون

translation: But We have enjoyed these [disbelievers] and their forefathers until a long life has passed over them. Do they not see that We come to the earth and reduce it from its outlying borders? Is it they who will overcome?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the transient nature of worldly pleasures and the false sense of security that individuals and their forebearers might feel. It points to the divine power in controlling destiny, reminding that despite enjoying prolonged lives and material wealth, the ultimate reality is that God's decrees prevail. The reduction of the earth's borders symbolizes the gradual decline of their influence and power, suggesting that ultimately, it is God's will that prevails, not the false pride of those who oppose Him.
orig: بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها أفهم الغالبون

translation: Say: I only warn you by revelation, and the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitations of communication and understanding among people who are not receptive to the message being conveyed. It suggests that those who are spiritually or morally 'deaf'—unaware or indifferent to divine warnings—will not respond to the truth when it is presented to them. The focus on revelation denotes the importance and authority of divine guidance, while the metaphor of deafness highlights the challenges faced by the prophet or messenger in reaching those who refuse to listen or heed the warnings. Ultimately, it serves as a reminder that divine communication requires openness and readiness to learn.
orig: قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون

translation: And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the human tendency to recognize their wrongdoing only when faced with the consequences of their actions. It highlights a moment of clarity in which individuals acknowledge their injustices and shortcomings in the case of divine retribution. This serves as a reminder of the importance of self-reflection and accountability, encouraging believers to seek forgiveness and strive for righteousness before facing inevitable judgment.
orig: ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be wronged in the least; and if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accounting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment. It conveys the idea that every action, no matter how insignificant it may seem, will be precisely accounted for. The imagery of a mustard seed, one of the smallest seeds, represents that even the minutest deeds will not go unnoticed. This serves to remind believers of the importance of their actions and the thoroughness of divine judgment, assuring that no one will suffer injustice, thus encouraging a life of righteousness and accountability.
orig: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين

translation: And We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance provided to Moses and Aaron, emphasizing the importance of the 'criterion' (which is often understood as discernment between right and wrong) and the light (representing enlightenment and clarity) that they brought to their people. The reference to a 'reminder for the righteous' signifies that their message serves as a continual prompt for those who are conscious of their moral and spiritual duties. It reinforces the concept that true guidance is not only about delivering a message but also about being a beacon of light and wisdom for others, particularly for those who seek to live virtuously.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين

translation: Those who fear their Lord in secret, and they are apprehensive of the Hour.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of true believers who possess a deep, inward fear of God that transcends external appearances. Their reverence for Allah is sincere and not just a display, as they feel His presence even when alone. Furthermore, their concern about the coming Day of Judgment ('the Hour') emphasizes their awareness of accountability and the transient nature of worldly life. This awareness shapes their actions and decisions, motivating them to live righteously and seek forgiveness, showcasing their humility and submission to God's will.
orig: الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وهم من الساعة مشفقون

translation: And this is a blessed mention that We have sent down. So will you deny it?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and divine source of the Qur'an, referring to it as a 'blessed mention.' The rhetorical question at the end challenges the listeners or readers about their disbelief or rejection of the message. It invites reflection on the nature of the revelation, asserting its importance and urging individuals to acknowledge the truth of the Scriptures rather than dismissing it.
orig: وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه أفأنتم له منكرون

translation: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before, and We were of him knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Abraham was bestowed with wisdom and guidance by Allah even before he was sent as a prophet. It emphasizes that God has knowledge of His servants and their potential. The use of the phrase 'sound judgement' signifies the clarity and truthfulness in Abraham's understanding of monotheism and righteousness, suggesting that God equips His chosen individuals with the ability to discern truth from falsehood, often in their formative years. Furthermore, it indicates an ongoing divine relationship and acknowledgment of Abraham's faithfulness and capacity to lead others toward the path of truth.
orig: ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a critical moment of questioning and confrontation about the practice of idolatry. The speaker challenges his father and community regarding their unwavering devotion to idols, highlighting a theme of seeking truth and understanding rather than blindly following traditions. It underscores the importance of rational thought and the pursuit of monotheism, illustrating the struggle between faith in one God and the pervasive influence of societal customs. This moment serves as an invitation to reconsider false beliefs and encourages an examination of deeper spiritual truths.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a religion.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the common human tendency to adhere to the beliefs and practices passed down from previous generations without questioning their validity. It reflects a cultural and familial loyalty to tradition, potentially serving as an excuse to reject new ideas or revelations. In a broader sense, it underscores the need for individuals to critically examine their beliefs rather than blindly following the paths of their ancestors.
orig: قالوا وجدنا آباءنا لها عابدين

translation: He said, "Indeed, you and your forefathers were in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse highlights a pivotal moment of realization and accountability. The speaker addresses a group who have followed false beliefs or misguided practices, implying that their ignorance has persisted through generations. It underscores the importance of seeking truth and acknowledging one’s own misconceptions, while stressing that continued adherence to falsehood, especially passed down from ancestors, leads to severe consequences. The term 'manifest error' suggests that the misleading nature of their beliefs was clear and evident, yet they chose to remain in that state, emphasizing the need for enlightenment and the pursuit of genuine understanding.
orig: قال لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the playmakers?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of confrontation where individuals question the sincerity and authenticity of the messenger. It highlights the tension between truth and deception, illustrating how people may respond to a genuine message with skepticism, often resorting to dismissive reactions. The term 'playmakers' suggests a perception that the messenger might be engaging in trivial or misleading behavior, emphasizing the struggle between recognizing divine truth and succumbing to doubts or cynicism.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا بالحق أم أنت من اللاعبين

translation: He said, 'But your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them; and I am, upon that, of those who witness.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights the importance of acknowledging God's role in creation and existence. The speaker asserts certainty and witness to this truth, indicating a deep conviction and a call to recognize the majesty of God as the source of all that exists. It serves as a reminder of the divine authority over the universe and addresses those who may doubt or overlook the supremacy of Allah.
orig: قال بل ربكم رب السماوات والأرض الذي فطرهن وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين

translation: And by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and fled.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a strong resolve and determination to confront and dismantle false beliefs and idols that people worship in disregard of the divine truth. It signifies a moment of defiance against idolatry, highlighting the importance of faithfulness to the one true God. The speaker, likely a prophet, is declaring an intention to reveal the futility of these idols, especially in the context of those who abandon their misguided faith. It emphasizes the contrast between the permanence of divine truth and the temporary nature of human-made idols, representing a broader theme of rejecting polytheism and embracing monotheism.
orig: وتالله لأكيدن أصنامكم بعد أن تولوا مدبرين

translation: So he made them into pieces, except for a [large] statue of theirs that they might return to it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the confrontation between Prophet Abraham and the idol worshippers of his time. By destroying the idols but leaving one intact, Abraham aimed to provoke thought among the idolaters, inviting them to reflect on the futility of worshiping inanimate objects that cannot defend themselves. This act serves as a powerful metaphor for calling people to rationalize their beliefs and reconsider their practices, highlighting the need to turn towards the one true God instead of false deities.
orig: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

translation: They said, 'Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the outrage of a community whose idols have been disrespected or destroyed. It reveals the intense feelings of loyalty and attachment people have towards their deities. It highlights the human tendency to perceive any challenge or destruction of one’s belief systems or icons as an injustice and wrongdoing. This situation can also serve as a point of reflection on the nature of belief and the defense of faith, where individuals may react strongly when their beliefs are challenged. Additionally, it sets the stage for a deeper discussion about the implications of idolatry and the true nature of divinity.
orig: قالوا من فعل هذا بآلهتنا إنه لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, "We heard a young man mentioning them, who is called Abraham."
interpretation: This verse reveals the societal dynamics and the role of young individuals in challenging established beliefs. The mention of Abraham indicates the recognition of a strong voice opposing idolatry. It highlights the importance of dialogue and questioning established norms, suggesting that even youth can have a significant impact on communal beliefs and practices.
orig: قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم

translation: They said, "Bring him before the eyes of the people so perhaps they will witness."
interpretation: This verse likely reflects a moment of public spectacle or demonstration, indicating a desire for validation and acknowledgment from the community. It suggests the importance of visibility and recognition in asserting the truth or significance of an event. The phrase implies that the act of presenting someone or something to a collective audience holds the potential for them to bear witness to an important truth, thus elevating the event's legitimacy and the role of communal observation in establishing reality.
orig: قالوا فأتوا به على أعين الناس لعلهم يشهدون

translation: They said, 'Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment of confrontation and accusation against Prophet Abraham. It signifies the challenge of monotheism against polytheism. The phrase illustrates the disbelief of the people regarding Abraham's rejection of their idols and underscores a pivotal point in his prophetic mission. Abraham's action of destroying the idols was a bold statement against the false gods worshipped by his community, and this moment reflects the tension between truth and falsehood. It emphasizes the struggle that prophets face in conveying and standing firm in their belief against the prevailing practices of their time.
orig: قالوا أأنت فعلت هذا بآلهتنا يا إبراهيم

translation: He said: "Rather, it was this, their chief, that did it. So ask them if they should be able to speak!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between the Prophet Abraham and the idol-worshippers. When challenged about the destruction of their idols, Abraham points to the largest idol, suggesting that if the idols were indeed powerful, they should be capable of defending themselves or explaining their own existence. This reflects a deeper critique of idolatry, indicating that reliance on created things instead of the Creator is ultimately futile. The verse invites reflection on the nature of belief, the limitations of blind faith, and the importance of questioning the validity of one's convictions.
orig: قال بل فعله كبيرهم هذا فاسألوهم إن كانوا ينطقون

translation: Then they returned to themselves and said, 'Indeed, you are the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of self-awareness and acknowledgment of wrongdoing among a group of individuals. It signifies a turning point where they confront their actions and recognize their faults. This recognition suggests the importance of self-reflection and accountability in human behavior, indicating that realizing one's mistakes is a crucial step towards seeking forgiveness and rectifying one's path. It serves as a reminder that in times of conflict or injustice, one should introspect rather than blame others, fostering a culture of responsibility and ethical conduct.
orig: فرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فقالوا إنكم أنتم الظالمون

translation: Then they turned their heads away, for you know what these speak.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of realization and acknowledgment, where the speaker emphasizes the futility of the words and actions of a certain group. The turning away signifies a rejection of the truth, highlighting a disconnect between their understanding and reality. It also suggests that ignorance or dismissal of divine signs leads to a state of disbelief or lack of insight, where individuals choose to ignore what is evident and clear.
orig: ثم نكسوا على رءوسهم لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون

translation: He said, 'Do you worship besides Allah what holds for you no benefit or harm?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshipping entities that lack the power to provide benefit or avert harm. It emphasizes the concept of monotheism by questioning the rationale behind idolatry or reliance on false deities that are unable to assist their worshippers. The rhetorical nature of the question serves to challenge believers to reflect on the significance of placing their trust and devotion solely in Allah, the only One who possesses true power over benefits and harms in life.
orig: قال أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم

translation: Woe to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not understand?
interpretation: This verse serves as a call to reflection and reason. It highlights the futility of worshipping deities other than Allah, emphasizing the importance of understanding the nature of true divinity. The phrase 'do you not understand?' challenges those who commit idolatry or follow false beliefs to use their intellect and reconsider their actions. It stresses the disconnection between mere rituals of worship and the need for genuine comprehension of the Creator.
orig: أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون

translation: They said, 'Burn him and support your gods if you are to act.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extreme measures taken by the people against those who challenge their beliefs. It reflects the intensity of their devotion to their idols, demonstrating their willingness to resort to violence instead of engaging in rational debate. This situation serves as a broader metaphor for how people often react defensively when their deeply held convictions are questioned. It highlights the conflict between monotheism and polytheism, and the lengths to which those clinging to false beliefs may go to protect them.
orig: قالوا حرقوه وانصروا آلهتكم إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: We said, 'O Fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine intervention and protection granted to Prophet Abraham when he was thrown into the fire by his enemies. The command for the fire to become cool and safe illustrates Allah's power over nature and serves as a profound reminder of His ability to protect His chosen ones from harm. It symbolizes a miraculous event where what should normally cause destruction becomes a means of tranquility and safety, reinforcing the importance of faith and trust in God's mercy and protection during trials.
orig: قلنا يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم

translation: And they intended to harm him, but We made them the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate failure of those who plot against the faithful or intend harm. It highlights that, despite their schemes and plans, divine justice prevails, and those who wish ill to others will face consequences. The phrase 'the greatest losers' signifies not just a material loss but a profound spiritual failure, suggesting that their actions not only result in the loss of their intended target but also lead to their own ruin and misguidance. This serves as a reminder of the futility of opposing God's will and the necessity of faith and sincerity in one's intentions.
orig: وأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأخسرين

translation: And We saved him (Ibrahim) and Lut to the land which We had blessed for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and the salvation of the prophets Ibrahim and Lut, highlighting the significance of the land they were brought to—a place blessed by God. It reflects the theme of divine favor for the righteous and warns against the consequences faced by those who reject God's message, serving as a reminder of hope and divine support for believers amidst adversity.
orig: ونجيناه ولوطا إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها للعالمين

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob as a gift, and all of them We made righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grace and blessings of God upon the Prophet Abraham, as He bestowed upon him not only Isaac but also Jacob, illustrating the continuation of prophethood and righteousness through his lineage. It underscores the theme of divine favor, emphasizing that both Isaac and Jacob were endowed with righteousness, signifying their moral integrity and steadfastness in faith. This also reflects God’s plan in establishing a noble lineage, which contributes to the history of prophetic messages in Islam.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب نافلة وكلا جعلنا صالحين

translation: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired them to do good deeds, to establish prayer, and to give zakah; and they were worshippers of Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of appointed leaders who are guided by divine instruction. It indicates that true leadership in a spiritual sense is rooted in fulfilling the commands of God, engaging in righteous actions, and performing acts of worship such as prayer and charity. The reference to 'inspiring' implies that these leaders are not only given authority but also the necessary guidance to fulfill their responsibilities. Their devotion is highlighted, demonstrating that genuine leadership is intertwined with deep faith and submission to God's will.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا وأوحينا إليهم فعل الخيرات وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وكانوا لنا عابدين

translation: And We gave Lut judgment and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that was committing vile deeds. Indeed, they were a people of wickedness and disobedience.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the righteous and the corrupt, illustrating the divine assistance granted to Prophet Lut in the face of moral decay. It emphasizes the importance of judgment and knowledge for those who strive to uphold righteousness. The 'vile deeds' signify the moral corruption of Lut's people, serving as a reminder of the consequences of persistent disobedience to divine commands. Ultimately, it reflects the theme of protection for the faithful amidst the transgressions of society.
orig: ولوطا آتيناه حكما وعلما ونجيناه من القرية التي كانت تعمل الخبائث إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فاسقين

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine mercy and the criteria for receiving it. The specific mention of 'righteousness' indicates that a life lived in accordance with moral and ethical principles earns one a place in God's mercy. It emphasizes that God's mercy is accessible to those who strive to be good and follow the ethical path. This serves as an encouragement to believers to embody righteous behavior, as mercy from God is a reward for those who are steadfast in their faith and virtuous in their actions.
orig: وأدخلناه في رحمتنا إنه من الصالحين

translation: And (remember) Nuh (Noah) when he called (to Us) before; so We answered him and saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine response to sincere supplication and the mercy of God in delivering the faithful from severe trials. Nuh's invocation signifies a deep reliance on God in times of suffering, and the subsequent salvation emphasizes God's promise to support those who call upon Him with faith. It also reflects the notion that trials may serve a purpose, leading individuals toward a more profound relationship with the Divine and ultimately to a state of relief and protection.
orig: ونوحا إذ نادى من قبل فاستجبنا له فنجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We saved him from the people who denied Our signs; indeed, they were a wicked people, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support provided to the prophets and the consequences faced by those who reject the signs of God. The mention of drowning signifies complete destruction as a result of the people's disbelief and immorality. It serves as a reminder of accountability in the face of divine justice, illustrating the idea that persistence in wrongdoing ultimately leads to ruin. This can also be interpreted as a reassurance to the faithful that God protects them from harm while punishing the oppressors.
orig: ونصرناه من القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And [mention] when David and Solomon judged concerning the field when the sheep of the people had strayed therein. And We were witness to their judgment.
interpretation: This verse highlights a story involving two prophets, David and Solomon, who were known for their wisdom and fairness in judgment. The scenario presented revolves around a dispute regarding a field that was damaged by the sheep of a neighboring party. This situation illustrates the importance of justice and the role of divine oversight in such matters. It emphasizes that righteous leadership is characterized by the ability to resolve conflicts with fairness and equity, and the example of David and Solomon serves as a model for believers in their own interactions and judgments.
orig: وداوود وسليمان إذ يحكمان في الحرث إذ نفشت فيه غنم القوم وكنا لحكمهم شاهدين

translation: So We gave understanding to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge, and We subjected the mountains to praise with him, and the birds, and We were doing this.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine gifts of wisdom and knowledge bestowed upon the prophets, particularly Solomon and David. It emphasizes the concept of divine support in their missions, showcasing how nature itself was made to respond to their worship and authority. The mention of mountains and birds signifies the harmony in creation that responds to the commands of the righteous. This serves as a reminder of the profound relationship between the divine and the natural world, illustrating that true wisdom leads to a greater understanding of one's role within it and the importance of obedience to God's will.
orig: ففهمناها سليمان وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما وسخرنا مع داوود الجبال يسبحن والطير وكنا فاعلين

translation: And We taught him the making of coats of armor to protect you from each other’s violence. Are you then grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance given to humanity in the form of skills and knowledge, specifically the crafting of armor for protection in conflict. It points to the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings and tools provided by God to safeguard ourselves. The rhetorical question at the end serves as a reminder of our duty to acknowledge these gifts and be grateful, emphasizing that our advancements and means of protection are not merely the result of human effort but also a product of divine instruction. It calls for reflection on how we use the knowledge bestowed upon us and reminds us of the need for gratitude in our lives.
orig: وعلمناه صنعة لبوس لكم لتحصنكم من بأسكم فهل أنتم شاكرون

translation: And for Solomon, the wind [was made] a strong gale, blowing by his command to the land which We had blessed. And We were knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and power granted to Prophet Solomon (Sulaiman), emphasizing his ability to control the wind as a force of nature. The mention of the land that is blessed indicates a reference to the holy land or regions of significance, suggesting that Solomon's reign was not only marked by authority but also by a special connection to God. The phrase 'We were knowing of all things' emphasizes God's omniscience, implying that everything occurs within His knowledge, encouraging reflection on God's wisdom in the grand scheme of creation and governance.
orig: ولسليمان الريح عاصفة تجري بأمره إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها وكنا بكل شيء عالمين

translation: And among the devils are those who dive for him and do work other than that. And We were protecting them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of supernatural beings, specifically devils, who serve various roles, including performing tasks for humans, such as diving for pearls or treasures. The mention of Allah's protection implies that despite these actions, there is an overarching divine guardianship that prevents harm or mischief from reaching the believers. It also suggests the existence of both good and bad influences in the world and emphasizes the importance of divine oversight in human affairs.
orig: ومن الشياطين من يغوصون له ويعملون عملا دون ذلك وكنا لهم حافظين

translation: And (mention) Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and you are the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound connection between Job and his Lord during times of suffering. Job's calling out to God reflects his deep faith and trust in divine mercy despite his afflictions. It emphasizes the importance of turning to God in times of hardship and acknowledges that even in our greatest trials, God's mercy is ever-present. The verse serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the comfort that believers can find in invoking God's compassion and help.
orig: وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: So We responded to him, and We removed what was causing him harm, and We gave him his family and the same number with them as a mercy from Us and a lesson for those who worship.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine mercy and responsiveness of God to the prayers of those in distress. It emphasizes that God not only alleviates the suffering of the afflicted but also rewards them abundantly. The restoration of family signifies the importance of relationships and community support in healing processes. Additionally, it serves as a reminder and a lesson to worshippers of the power of faith and the importance of turning to God in times of hardship, highlighting that reliance on the Divine can lead to both physical and spiritual relief.
orig: فاستجبنا له فكشفنا ما به من ضر وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة من عندنا وذكرى للعابدين

translation: And Isma'il (Ishmael) and Idris (Enoch) and Dhul-Kifl (Ezekiel); all were of the patient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience as a significant quality of certain prophets. It implies that enduring trials and maintaining faith in the face of adversity are essential traits that these figures exemplified. The mention of Isma'il, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl serves to illustrate that patience is not only a personal quality but also an integral part of the prophetic mission and legacy, encouraging believers to emulate these steadfast individuals in their own struggles.
orig: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed, they were among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward of those who live righteously and obey God's commands. It signifies that those who make sincere efforts towards goodness and righteousness will be granted God's mercy and compassion. The use of 'Our mercy' indicates a personal and intimate relationship between God and the righteous, highlighting that their virtuous actions lead to divine acceptance and everlasting peace in the hereafter.
orig: وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا إنهم من الصالحين

translation: And [mention] the man of the fish, when he went away in anger and thought that We would not constrain him. And he cried out within the belly of the fish, 'There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of vulnerability and realization of wrongdoing by Prophet Jonah (Yunus) when he found himself in the belly of the fish. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing one’s faults and turning to God in sincere repentance. The phrase 'There is no deity except You' reflects the core tenet of monotheism and the acknowledgment of God's supremacy. The use of 'exalted are You' indicates the speaker's deep respect and reverence for God’s perfection, contrasting his own failure and human frailty. This story also serves as a reminder that no matter how dire the circumstances, turning to God with sincerity can bring solace and redemption.
orig: وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر عليه فنادى في الظلمات أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

translation: So We responded to him and saved him from distress. And thus do We save the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and support for His faithful servants during times of trouble. It highlights the importance of prayer and turning to God in distress, showcasing that God not only hears but also responds to the supplications of His believers. The phrase 'thus do We save the believers' suggests a pattern of divine assistance that is consistent for those who have faith, implying a deep connection between belief and salvation.
orig: فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين

translation: And (mention) Zechariah when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone while You are the best of inheritors."
interpretation: This verse reflects Zechariah's plea to God for companionship and support, highlighting his deep longing for a successor to carry on his legacy. It emphasizes the human experience of vulnerability and the need for divine assistance. The phrase 'You are the best of inheritors' signifies trust in God's eternal nature and the assurance that true sustenance and legacy come from Him. It indicates that while worldly connections may fade, God's grace and providence are everlasting.
orig: وزكريا إذ نادى ربه رب لا تذرني فردا وأنت خير الوارثين

translation: So We responded to him and granted him John, and We cured his wife for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were submissive to Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine response to the prayers of those who are devoted and strive for righteousness. The mention of granting John (Yahya) and curing his wife signifies that God rewards sincere supplication with blessings, emphasizing the importance of faith and perseverance in pursuing good deeds. The attributes of 'hope' and 'fear' illustrate a balanced approach to worship, where a believer loves and relies on God's mercy while also recognizing His majesty and power. The term 'submissive' further underscores a state of humility and devotion, reflecting a deep relationship between the believers and their Lord.
orig: فاستجبنا له ووهبنا له يحيى وأصلحنا له زوجه إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا وكانوا لنا خاشعين

translation: And she who guarded her chastity, We breathed into her of Our Spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the virgin birth of Mary and the significance of both her and Jesus as signs for all of humanity. It underscores the sanctity of purity and the divine intervention in bringing forth miraculous events. By stating that Mary 'guarded her chastity,' it emphasizes the importance of virtue, while the phrase 'We breathed into her of Our Spirit' illustrates the direct involvement of God in miraculous occurrences. The implication is that Jesus and Mary serve as exemplary figures, representing faith, purity, and a profound connection to the divine, meant to inspire wonder and reverence among believers and those who reflect on their lives.
orig: والتي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

translation: Indeed, this is your nation, one nation, and I am your Lord; so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the Muslim ummah (community) as one cohesive entity under the sovereignty of Allah. It calls for collective worship and devotion to God, highlighting the importance of maintaining strong spiritual and communal bonds among believers. The declaration of oneness also serves as a reminder of shared purpose and identity, encouraging followers to support one another in faith and practice.
orig: إن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاعبدون

translation: And their matter has been cut off among them; to Us they will all be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that ultimately, all matters and disputes among people will come to an end. It serves as a reminder that the true resolution and judgment lie with Allah, as everyone will ultimately return to Him for accountability. It indicates a sense of divine sovereignty and the temporary nature of worldly disagreements, reinforcing the importance of seeking truth and justice in this life while being aware of the eventual return to the Creator.
orig: وتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم كل إلينا راجعون

translation: So whoever does righteous deeds while believing, there will be no denial of his effort, and indeed, We will record it for him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of combining faith with righteous actions. It assures the believer that their good deeds will not go unacknowledged or wasted; rather, they will be meticulously recorded. This serves as a reassurance that God is aware of every effort made in the spirit of faith, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in their good works, knowing that such efforts contribute to their eternal reward.
orig: فمن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا كفران لسعيه وإنا له كاتبون

translation: And it is forbidden for a people that We have destroyed that they should ever return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the finality of divine judgment and the inescapable consequences of a community's persistent wrongdoing. Once a nation has faced destruction due to its transgressions, it is irrevocable, serving as a warning to others. The verse illustrates the importance of heeding moral and spiritual guidance to avoid similar fates, reinforcing the notion of accountability in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون

translation: Until the Gog and Magog are opened, and they are from every hill they slide down.
interpretation: This verse signifies the release of Gog and Magog, two tribes often associated with chaos and destruction. Their emergence symbolizes a time of great turmoil and test for humanity. The imagery of them descending from every hill suggests that their influence and corruption will spread widely and uncontrollably. This event is a precursor to significant trials in the world, representing both a literal and metaphorical upheaval where moral and ethical chaos prevails, prompting believers to remain steadfast in their faith amidst adversity.
orig: حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

translation: And the true promise has drawn near; then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring in horror. They will say, "Woe to us! We were indeed in a state of heedlessness regarding this, and indeed, we were transgressors."
interpretation: This verse captures the moment of realization for those who have disbelieved when the truth becomes evident, and they can no longer deny their past negligence and wrongdoing. It reflects a profound sense of regret and despair as they confront the consequences of their actions. The term 'heedlessness' indicates their prior indifference to the signs of truth that were presented to them, emphasizing the importance of awareness and recognition of one's moral and spiritual responsibilities. This verse serves as a warning and an admonition to remain vigilant and conscious of the teachings of faith, highlight the gravity of disbelief, and the inevitable accountability that follows.
orig: واقترب الوعد الحق فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا بل كنا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will surely enter it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of idolatry and the consequences of turning away from the worship of Allah. It highlights that those who place their faith and devotion in anything or anyone other than Allah will find themselves facing severe consequences in the hereafter. The imagery of being fuel for Hell serves as a strong warning about the gravity of associating partners with Allah and can be seen as a call to reflect on one's beliefs and to turn back to the worship of the One true God.
orig: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون

translation: If there were gods other than Allah, they would not have entered it (the Hellfire); and all would have been therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of polytheism and asserts the absolute oneness of Allah. It suggests that if there were multiple deities, they would have the power to prevent their followers from entering Hell. The inevitability of all entering Hell reinforces the idea that there is no divine competition; it emphasizes Allah's singular authority and the futility of worshiping other gods, showcasing the unique and unparalleled nature of His sovereignty.
orig: لو كان هؤلاء آلهة ما وردوها وكل فيها خالدون

translation: For them therein is exhalation, and they therein will not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of punishment that awaits those who have rejected faith and done wrong in their lives. The term 'زفير' (exhalation) suggests a deep, mournful cry, indicative of the despair and anguish they experience in the afterlife. The phrase 'لا يسمعون' (will not hear) signifies that they will be deprived of any comforting or uplifting sounds; they are cut off from hope, mercy, and the ability to receive any positive reinforcement. This creates a stark contrast between the bliss of the righteous and the torment of the sinful, underlining the gravity of their choices in life.
orig: لهم فيها زفير وهم فيها لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, those for whom goodness has previously been decreed from Us - they are removed far from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine predestination and the special status of those who have been granted God's favor. It suggests that certain individuals, due to their prior merits or divine decree, are safeguarded from the trials and tribulations that others may face, particularly in the context of the afterlife. The 'goodness' referred to can be interpreted as a promise of reward, peace, and protection from punishment, indicating that God's mercy and wisdom prevails in determining one's fate.
orig: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون

translation: They will not hear its sound while they abide in that which their souls desire.
interpretation: This verse reflects the state of the believers in Paradise, highlighting their experience of bliss and contentment. The sound mentioned represents the chaos and torment of Hell, which they are completely shielded from. Their eternal dwelling in Paradise is filled with fulfillment of their desires, emphasizing the peace and joy they encounter. It illustrates a stark contrast to the fate of those who reject faith, and serves as a reminder of the eternal rewards awaiting the righteous.
orig: لا يسمعون حسيسها وهم في ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون

translation: Let not the greatest terror grieve them, and the angels will meet them. This is your Day which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse conveys a profound sense of reassurance to the believers, indicating that on the Day of Judgment, they will be comforted by angels, alleviating the fear and anxiety associated with the impending events. The phrase 'the greatest terror' refers to the overwhelming challenges that will unfold on that day, yet for the believers, it is mitigated by divine support and the fulfillment of God's promises. This highlights the theme of hope and salvation for the faithful, suggesting that their endurance and devotion will culminate in a rewarding and joyful reunion with the divine.
orig: لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر وتتلقاهم الملائكة هذا يومكم الذي كنتم توعدون

translation: On the Day We will fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll for writings; as We began the first creation, We will repeat it. It is a promise We have undertaken. Indeed, We will do it.
interpretation: This verse conveys the certainty of resurrection and the transformation of creation. It uses the metaphor of folding the heavens like a scroll to illustrate the power of Allah to recreate and revert the universe to its initial state. Just as He initiated creation from nothing, He will also bring it back in a new form. The repetition of creation signifies Allah's control and determination, emphasizing that His promise is fulfilled without fail. This serves as a reminder of the transient nature of the worldly life and the significance of the hereafter.
orig: يوم نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وعدا علينا إنا كنا فاعلين

translation: And We have written in the Psalms, after the mention, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of divine justice and the ultimate victory of the righteous. It signifies that despite the trials and tribulations faced by the believers, those who are pious and remain steadfast in their faith will eventually inherit the earth. This idea of inheritance reflects a significant spiritual and material legacy, where the righteous are rewarded for their faithfulness, suggesting a conclusion to the struggles that they endure in this life. It also reinforces the theme of continuity of divine message across scriptures, aligning the Psalms with the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون

translation: Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the message being conveyed, highlighting that it is intended for those who are dedicated in their worship of Allah. It suggests that for true worshippers, the teachings and signs provided within the context of the verse serve as a profound reminder or guidance, reinforcing the need for spiritual awareness and dedication to the divine.
orig: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a universal figure whose mission transcends cultural, national, and temporal boundaries. It positions him as a source of compassion and kindness, highlighting that the essence of his message is rooted in mercy. The term 'worlds' indicates the broad scope of his impact, suggesting that his teachings are relevant not just to a specific community or era but to all of humanity. This reinforces the idea that the message of Islam is meant to uplift and guide people towards justice, love, and understanding, reflecting a holistic approach to human welfare.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين

translation: Say, "It has been revealed to me that your God is but one God. So will you not submit [to Him]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of monotheism, declaring the oneness of God and urging people to submit to His will. It highlights the core message of Islam, which is to recognize and worship only one God. The call to submission reflects the fundamental principle of surrendering oneself to the divine authority, inviting individuals to reflect on their beliefs and encouraging them to embrace faith in a singular, all-powerful deity.
orig: قل إنما يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: So if they turn away, say, 'I have warned you of a suffocating punishment. But I do not know if what you are promised is near or far.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of delivering a warning to those who choose to turn away from guidance. It emphasizes the responsibility of the messenger to convey the message without possessing knowledge of when or how the consequences will unfold. The phrase indicates a lack of ultimate knowledge about divine decrees, underscoring human limitations and the significance of faith and patience in facing the unknown. It calls on individuals to reflect on their choices and the possible repercussions, reminding them that the truth cannot be ignored without consequence.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل آذنتكم على سواء وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون

translation: Indeed, He knows the open speech and He knows what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omniscience, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge, whether it is spoken openly or hidden in the heart. It serves as a reminder to individuals that their thoughts and intentions are fully known to God, which can have a profound impact on moral consciousness and ethical behavior. The verse encourages sincerity and honesty in both actions and words, urging believers to align their inner thoughts with their external expressions, as all will be judged by God.
orig: إنه يعلم الجهر من القول ويعلم ما تكتمون

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and a temporary enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse suggests the uncertainty regarding the true nature of worldly trials and pleasures. It conveys that what may seem like a blessing or advantage can also serve as a test of faith and character. The phrase 'temporary enjoyment' reflects the transient nature of worldly affairs, urging believers to remain vigilant and discerning about their spiritual priorities. The verse prompts individuals to reflect on whether their experiences and possessions are genuinely beneficial or merely distractions that could lead them away from their ultimate purpose.
orig: وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين

translation: My Lord, judge between us in truth, and our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe.
interpretation: This verse is a plea for divine justice, emphasizing the importance of truth and fairness in judgment. It reflects the believer's reliance on God's mercy and support in facing the challenges posed by false accusations or injustices. The mention of 'the Most Merciful' highlights the nature of God as compassionate and supportive, reinforcing the idea that believers should trust in divine guidance and assistance when confronting adversities or opposition.
orig: قال رب احكم بالحق وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the quake of the Hour is a tremendous thing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the urgency to be conscious of one's actions and the reality of accountability before Allah. The earth's shake, as referenced, symbolizes the immense upheaval and the profound changes that will occur at the end of time. The call to 'fear your Lord' urges individuals to cultivate piety and prepare spiritually for the inevitable reality of this event, highlighting the importance of living a life aligned with divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم

translation: On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and you will see the people appearing intoxicated while they are not intoxicated, but the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the overwhelming nature of the Day of Judgment. It conveys that on this day, the intensity of events will cause profound distraction and concern, even for those who are typically preoccupied with caring for others, like nursing mothers and pregnant women. The imagery of people appearing intoxicated illustrates the state of confusion and fear they will experience, despite not being under the influence of wine or any substance. The phrase 'the punishment of Allah is severe' serves as a stark reminder of the reality of divine justice and the consequences of human actions, compelling a sense of urgency to be mindful and prepare for that day.
orig: يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد

translation: And among the people are those who argue about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of individuals who engage in debates about the existence and attributes of God without possessing the requisite understanding or knowledge. It points to the futility of such arguments and underscores the danger of following misleading influences, symbolized by 'rebellious devils.' The passage warns that without true understanding, individuals may be led astray, emphasizing the importance of genuine knowledge and discernment in matters of faith.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ويتبع كل شيطان مريد

translation: It is decreed upon him that whoever takes him as a guardian, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse underscores the seriousness of taking false guardians or allies, warning that such choices can lead to spiritual and moral downfall. It reflects the belief that straying from righteous guidance can result in dire consequences, emphasizing the importance of choosing one's companions and leaders wisely, as they can influence one's path towards either salvation or punishment.
orig: كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير

translation: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop of sperm, then from a clump of flesh, fully formed and partially formed, so that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for an appointed term; then We bring you out as infants; then you attain your maturity. And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows nothing after having known. And you see the earth barren; but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and brings forth every lovely kind (of growth).
interpretation: This verse addresses the fundamental belief in resurrection and the stages of human development as a means to strengthen faith. It reminds humanity of their humble beginnings from dust and the intricate stages of creation, underscoring that life is a divine process governed by God's will. The analogy of the earth coming to life with rain symbolizes resurrection and renewal, portraying the cycles of life and death as God's signs. This serves to encourage reflection on the power and capability of God in creation and resurrection, emphasizing that even after decay, life can flourish anew.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا خلقناكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا وترى الأرض هامدة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and He gives life to the dead, and He is competent over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Allah as the ultimate reality and truth ('al-Haqq'). It affirms His power over life and death, indicating that He is not only the creator but also the sustainer of existence. The reference to giving life to the dead can be interpreted both literally, in terms of resurrection after death, and metaphorically, in terms of spiritual revival and guidance. The assertion of His authority over all things serves to remind believers of His omnipotence and sovereignty in every aspect of life, encouraging trust in His plan and actions.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأنه يحيي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it; and Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, highlighting that the arrival of this day is inevitable and beyond doubt. It serves as a reminder for believers about the reality of resurrection and accountability in the hereafter. The mention of Allah resurrecting those in the graves underscores the power of God over life and death, affirming the belief that all individuals will be brought forth to face judgment regardless of their status or condition in this world.
orig: وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور

translation: And among the people are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the phenomenon of individuals who engage in arguments about God despite lacking proper knowledge or understanding. It emphasizes the need for sound evidence and guidance when discussing spiritual matters. The mention of 'without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening book' suggests that true understanding of divine matters requires grounding in clear, divinely inspired knowledge rather than mere speculative debate. This serves as a warning against those who seek to challenge beliefs and truths without a firm foundation, leading to misguidance and confusion.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And whoever takes a second as a protector besides Allah, will find in this world disgrace and We will make him taste the punishment of the blazing fire on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of monotheism and the dangers of polytheism or relying on others besides Allah for guidance and support. It emphasizes that turning away from the path of Allah leads to humiliation and disgrace in this life, while in the Hereafter, such individuals will face severe consequences, symbolized by the 'punishment of the blazing fire.' This serves as a warning to maintain sincere devotion to God and not to be entrapped by false deities or worldly attachments that deviate one from the true path.
orig: ثاني عطفه ليضل عن سبيل الله له في الدنيا خزي ونذيقه يوم القيامة عذاب الحريق

translation: That is for what your own hands have sent before [to the Judgment], and indeed, Allah is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual accountability and the concept of divine justice. It highlights that every person is responsible for their actions, and the consequences they face are a direct result of what they have done in their lifetime. It reassures believers that God's governance is fair and just; He does not wrong anyone, and each person's situation arises from their own choices and deeds. It serves as a reminder to act righteously, as one's actions will ultimately determine their fate.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت يداك وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: And among the people are those who worship Allah on an edge. If good befalls him, he is reassured by it; but if a trial befalls him, he turns on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that some individuals approach faith in a superficial manner, characterized by a conditional belief that fluctuates with their circumstances. Their true devotion is tested when faced with challenges; a lack of genuine faith is revealed when these trials lead them to abandon their beliefs. This illustrates a deeper truth about reliance and sincerity in worship. True faith is not contingent upon material gains or losses, but rather is steadfast regardless of external circumstances. The ultimate consequence of such wavering faith is a loss not just in worldly terms but detrimental impacts on their spiritual integrity and afterlife.
orig: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: He calls upon besides Allah that which harms him not and benefits him not. That is the extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of invoking entities other than Allah for help or guidance. It emphasizes the misguided nature of seeking support from those who cannot provide any real benefit or protection, illustrating the profound error in placing trust and faith in the powerless. Ultimately, it underscores the importance of pure monotheism and reliance solely on Allah, as anything else leads to significant misguidance.
orig: يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: He calls upon one whose harm is closer than his benefit; what a miserable protector and what a miserable companion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and danger of relying on those who do not bring true benefit and whose negative influence outweighs any potential good they may provide. It serves as a warning against choosing allies or seeking assistance from those who can lead one astray or cause more harm than good. The characterization of such a person as a 'miserable protector' and 'miserable companion' further emphasizes the gravity of selecting companions wisely, as the wrong choice can lead to dire consequences in one's life.
orig: يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who have believed and done righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of eternal reward for those who possess faith and engage in good deeds. It signifies the mercy and justice of Allah, illustrating that entrance into paradise is not arbitrary but is contingent upon one's belief and actions. The imagery of gardens with flowing rivers denotes immense beauty and serenity, representing ultimate bliss for the believers. Furthermore, the affirmation that 'Allah does what He wills' reminds us of His sovereignty and control over all matters, reinforcing the importance of trusting in His divine plan while striving to live a righteous life.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار إن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help him in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch a rope to the sky, then let him cut it off; then let him see if his plot will remove that which enrages him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of disbelief in Allah's assistance and power. It emphasizes that those who doubt God’s help are encouraged to take extreme actions, like attempting to reach the heavens, to illustrate their desperation. The act of cutting the rope symbolizes the limits of human effort against divine will. Ultimately, it conveys that no matter how much one plots or schemes against the truth, it cannot alter God's plan or lessen the consequences destined for them.
orig: من كان يظن أن لن ينصره الله في الدنيا والآخرة فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ثم ليقطع فلينظر هل يذهبن كيده ما يغيظ

translation: And thus We have sent down clear verses, and indeed, Allah guides whom He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and purposefulness of the revelations brought by Allah. The phrase 'clear verses' indicates that the messages in the Qur'an are not obscure but rather evident for those seeking guidance. The latter part underscores the divine will in guidance—while the verses are available, it is ultimately up to Allah to guide those whom He chooses, reflecting the belief in divine sovereignty and the importance of intent in seeking truth.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه آيات بينات وأن الله يهدي من يريد

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated others with Allah, indeed, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse expresses the concept of divine justice and inclusivity in the assessment of faith and actions. It acknowledges a variety of religious groups, indicating that belief in God or allegiance to various faith traditions is recognized in the eyes of Allah. The ultimate judgment will be carried out by God on the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the idea that every individual's faith and actions, regardless of their religious affiliation, will be evaluated. The mention of 'Allah being Witness' underscores the omnipresence and omniscience of God, reinforcing that nothing escapes His knowledge and judgment.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة إن الله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of the people? And upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse reflects the omnipotence of Allah and the universal submission of all creation to Him. It emphasizes that every entity, whether celestial or terrestrial, is in a state of worship and prostration to Allah, which shows the greatness of His authority. Moreover, it highlights the distinction between those who humbly submit to Him and those who face His wrath due to their rejection of faith. The mention of 'many' being subject to punishment signifies the consequences of disbelief and the ultimate sovereignty of Allah in executing His will over humanity and all living beings.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب وكثير من الناس وكثير حق عليه العذاب ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم إن الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed concerning their Lord. As for those who disbelieved, garments of fire will be cut out for them, and boiling water will be poured over their heads.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers in the context of their ultimate fate. The 'two adversaries' symbolize the opposing sides in the battle of faith, where believers stand firm in their conviction while disbelievers reject their Lord. The imagery of 'garments of fire' signifies the severe punishment awaiting the disbelievers, reflecting the consequences of their choices. The pouring of boiling water over their heads serves as a metaphor for the unbearable suffering that stems from their ingratitude and rejection of divine guidance. Overall, this verse emphasizes the seriousness of accountability in the afterlife and warns against the consequences of disbelief.
orig: هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم فالذين كفروا قطعت لهم ثياب من نار يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم

translation: It melts what is within their bellies and their skins.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically conveys the severe consequences of wrongdoing and the punishment that awaits those who are unjust. The imagery of melting indicates a profound transformation or destruction, highlighting how the internal sins and wickedness will manifest in external suffering. It serves as a powerful reminder of accountability and the inevitable repercussions of one's actions in the afterlife.
orig: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود

translation: And they will have iron rods.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that the disbelievers will face in the afterlife. The mention of 'iron rods' symbolizes the severity and strength of the punishment. It illustrates the harshness of the consequences for those who reject faith and commit wrongdoing, indicating that divine retribution is not only just but also formidable. This serves as a warning and encourages accountability for one's actions.
orig: ولهم مقامع من حديد

translation: Whenever they desire to get out of it from anguish, they will be driven back into it, and taste the punishment of the burning fire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the relentless nature of punishment in the hereafter for those who denounce faith and righteousness. The repeated cycling back into suffering signifies an inescapable fate for the disbelievers, emphasizing the severity of their consequences and the absolute justice of divine retribution. The metaphor of fire serves not only as a representation of physical torment but also as a symbol of spiritual anguish, where the opportunity for salvation is perpetually denied once their fate is sealed.
orig: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم أعيدوا فيها وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who have believed and done righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their attire therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rewards that await the believers in the hereafter, emphasizing the bliss and luxury of paradise. The mention of gardens with flowing rivers symbolizes eternal peace and abundance. The adornment of bracelets made of gold and pearls signifies honor and elevated status, while the mention of silk attire represents purity, comfort, and high standing in the spiritual realm. Collectively, this verse underscores the significance of faith and righteous actions, reinforcing the idea that the ultimate reward for those who believe and perform good deeds is a life of unimaginable beauty and comfort in paradise.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And were guided to the good word and were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of receiving guidance towards noble speech and virtuous actions. The 'good word' reflects the essence of the truth and righteous discourse that uplifts the human spirit and fosters positive relationships. Furthermore, being guided to 'the path of the Praiseworthy' suggests a moral and ethical journey towards the ultimate truth and goodness, which leads to both spiritual fulfillment and societal harmony. It highlights the importance of divine guidance in navigating life's challenges and making choices that align with virtue.
orig: وهدوا إلى الطيب من القول وهدوا إلى صراط الحميد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder [others] from the path of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque, which We have made for people - equal is the resident therein and the visitor. And whoever intends therein [to commit] deviation by wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences for those who oppose faith and actively prevent others from following the path of Allah, particularly in relation to the Sacred Mosque, a symbol of spiritual unity and worship. It emphasizes the divine justice that awaits those who not only reject belief but also perpetuate harm and oppression against the sanctity of spaces dedicated to worship. The distinction made between residents and visitors illustrates inclusivity in faith, yet warns that those who distort that sacredness will face dire repercussions. This serves as a reminder of the importance of reverence and integrity in matters of faith and communal worship.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن سبيل الله والمسجد الحرام الذي جعلناه للناس سواء العاكف فيه والباد ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم

translation: And [mention] when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], 'Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stand and bow and prostrate.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism, highlighting the command to Abraham to maintain the purity of the sacred House, which represents the worship of Allah without associating partners with Him. It calls for the purification of the place of worship for those engaged in acts of devotion, such as pilgrimage and prayer. The emphasis on 'purifying' the House suggests both a physical and spiritual cleanliness, as it is a key condition for sincere worship. This call to purity relates to the broader Islamic principle of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and the necessary conditions for an accepted worship.
orig: وإذ بوأنا لإبراهيم مكان البيت أن لا تشرك بي شيئا وطهر بيتي للطائفين والقائمين والركع السجود

translation: And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage: They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universality and significance of the pilgrimage (Hajj) in Islam. It illustrates the call to worship and the human desire to seek spiritual fulfillment. People are encouraged to undertake the journey, regardless of their means of travel or physical condition, highlighting the inclusivity of the Hajj. It also signifies the importance of community and gathering, as pilgrims from diverse backgrounds come together, thus reinforcing the unity of believers in their devotion to Allah.
orig: وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق

translation: Let them witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on appointed days over what He has provided them of the beast of grazing animals. So eat from them and feed the needy poor.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings provided by Allah, particularly during specific days designated for worship and sacrifice. It encourages believers to engage in communal festivities that revolve around gratitude and sharing. The call to 'eat from them and feed the needy poor' emphasizes compassion and the obligation to support the less fortunate, reinforcing the concept of social responsibility and charity in Islam. Overall, the verse underlines the spiritual and social dimensions of gratitude and generosity.
orig: ليشهدوا منافع لهم ويذكروا اسم الله في أيام معلومات على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فكلوا منها وأطعموا البائس الفقير

translation: Then let them complete their rites and fulfill their vows and let them perform the tawaf around the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of completing the rituals associated with Hajj, the pilgrimage to the Kaaba in Mecca. The 'rites' referred to include the various acts of devotion and worship that are performed during Hajj, such as the standing at Arafat, stoning the devil, and the sacrificial offerings. Fulfilling vows indicates a commitment to God, reflecting an individual's promises or obligations made during the pilgrimage. Performing tawaf around the Kaaba symbolizes the unity of believers in the worship of the One God, as they circle around the sacred site, demonstrating humility and devotion.
orig: ثم ليقضوا تفثهم وليوفوا نذورهم وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق

translation: And that; and whoever honors the sacred rights of Allah - for him is good in the sight of his Lord. And He has made sacred for you the animals except what is specified to you, so avoid the uncleanliness of idols and avoid false statement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of revering the sacred laws and rights established by Allah. It suggests that honoring these divine ordinances yields spiritual benefits and a favorable standing with God. The mention of specific dietary laws underlines the importance of following divine guidance in everyday life. Furthermore, the commands to avoid idolatry and falsehood highlight the fundamental principles of monotheism and truthfulness in Islam, indicating that spiritual purity involves both the rejection of physical impurities and the moral integrity in one's speech.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور

translation: Inclining [in faith] to Allah, not associating anything with Him. And he who associates with Allah - it is as though he had fallen from the sky and was seized by the birds, or the wind carried him to a far place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism in the practice of faith, emphasizing that true submission to Allah involves complete devotion without any form of association (shirk). The metaphor of falling from the sky and being snatched away represents the precarious state of those who commit shirk, illustrating the severe spiritual and existential consequences of straying from the path of pure faith. Such individuals are depicted as vulnerable and lost, subject to the whims of chaos, which signifies how damaging it is to deviate from the oneness of God.
orig: حنفاء لله غير مشركين به ومن يشرك بالله فكأنما خر من السماء فتخطفه الطير أو تهوي به الريح في مكان سحيق

translation: That, and whoever honors the rites of Allah - indeed, it is from piety of the hearts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of honoring and respecting the rituals and signs of Allah as a manifestation of true faith. It suggests that such reverence comes from a deep-rooted piety that originates in the heart, highlighting that genuine devotion and the act of honoring these rituals lead to spiritual elevation and a strengthened connection with the divine.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم شعائر الله فإنها من تقوى القلوب

translation: There are benefits for you in them for a specified term, then their place is to the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary and beneficial nature of certain worldly gains. It reminds the believer that while there may be advantages in life, they are ultimately transient and intended for a limited time. The mention of the 'Ancient House' (Kaaba) signifies the ultimate return to a sacred and divine purpose, implying that material gains should not distract one from spiritual truths and the destination of one’s life, which is the worship of Allah and the acknowledgment of His grandeur.
orig: لكم فيها منافع إلى أجل مسمى ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق

translation: And for every nation We have appointed rites that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided them of the sacrificial animals. So your God is One God; so to Him submit, and give good tidings to the humble.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of worship and the fundamental oneness of God across different communities. It highlights that every community has its own rites and methods of worship which are designed to help them remember and glorify God, especially in the act of sacrificing animals, which is a significant ritual in many cultures. The call to submit to God reflects the importance of humility and sincerity in faith, suggesting that true submission is recognized and rewarded by God. The phrase 'give good tidings to the humble' indicates that those who approach God with humility and an open heart are favored and will receive His mercy and guidance.
